title: Discovery of a likely supermassive neutron star in a remarkably wide binary
abstract: Supermassive neutron stars ( M ≳ 2 M ⊙ ) provide stringent constraints on the equation of state of dense matter. We report the discovery of a wide binary system composed of a red giant star and an invisible companion with an orbital period P ≈ 1218 ± 3 days and a comparatively low eccentricity e ≈ 0.09 ± 0.01 (with 1σ uncertainty). By combining radial velocity measurements from the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope and the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE) with astrometric data from Gaia DR2 and DR3 catalogs, we derive a Keplerian orbit with an inclination angle i ≈ 73 ∘ ± 11 ∘ . The unseen companion has a mass in the range of 1.8 to 2.8 M ⊙ (spanning the full spread of all estimates), with a best-fit value of 2.20 − 0.13 + 0.14 M ⊙ . This potentially places the unseen companion within the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes. Spectral disentangling using high-resolution near-infrared APOGEE spectra shows no absorption features from an additional component, suggesting the presence of a compact object: either a supermassive neutron star or a low-mass black hole. The wide, low-eccentricity orbit is difficult to explain through standard binary evolution channels, pointing to the need for improved theoretical models to account for such systems.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: Incomplete synaptic vesicle priming functionally disconnects CA1 pyramidal cells
abstract: The hippocampal CA1 area is perceived as a nonrecurrent neuronal network, i.e., CA1 pyramidal cells (CA1PCs) within the CA1 area innervate mainly γ-aminobutyric acid–releasing interneurons but not each other. Here, we performed an unbiased examination of the functional properties of local CA1PC output synapses using in vitro two-photon glutamate imaging. Fluorescent transients measured with iGluSnFR3 in individual boutons displayed extraordinary heterogeneity in their amplitudes and short-term plasticity patterns upon a complex train of presynaptic action potential firing. Post hoc electron microscopy of the imaged boutons demonstrated that distinct postsynaptic structure-innervating boutons display different functional properties. Approximately 25% of the boutons innervate CA1PC spines, which either release glutamate with very low release probability or completely fail to release. Phorbol 12,13-dibutyrate and elevated calcium (2+) concentration, manipulations that enhance synaptic vesicle priming and fusion, convert these silent into properly functioning synapses. Our results provide evidence that CA1PCs are interconnected with structurally and molecularly intact glutamatergic synapses, but incomplete synaptic vesicle (SV) priming precludes SV release.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: Bent-tailed radio galaxies as tracers of the intrafilament medium
abstract: Bent-tailed radio galaxies have traditionally been associated with, and used as tracers of, the dense intracluster medium. In recent years, however, such sources have also been identified outside of clusters, with only a few discovered in low-density environments of cosmic filaments. Their occurrence in low-density environments remains rare and is still poorly understood. We announce the discovery of bent-tailed radio galaxies in galaxy cluster filaments. We have identified two bent-tailed radio galaxies, J0020-25 and J0019-26, within a filament at the redshift of z ∼ 0.1273, and another bent-tailed radio galaxy, J0019-25, in a separate filament at z ∼ 0.1126. We used MeerKAT observations of these bent-tailed radio galaxies to place constraints on their intrafilament medium (IFM). The effects of the filaments could be seen in the radio morphologies of these galaxies. Using faint regions in each galaxy, we estimate the intrafilament pressure, density, magnetic field strength, and total energy density. We found an IFM density of ̊ho_ ≈ 3.8 g cm IFM 10^ -29 -3 $ for the surrounding medium of J0020-25 and J0019-26, and ̊ho_ ≈ (0.2 - 1.1) g cm^-3 around J0019-25. We found that our estimates for the intrafilament environment around J0020-25 and J0019-26 lie within the $̊ho_ literature estimates, while the density estimate found using J0019-25 is higher than the literature density estimates for the IFM and in agreement with the density of group environments. J0019-25 likely resides in a galaxy group embedded within a filament. These discoveries show the capabilities of using bent-tailed radio galaxies as probes to locate the otherwise invisible large-scale filaments. IFM 10^ -26 IFM

title: Analysis of quasielastic scattering and one-neutron transfer channel in the N 14 + Yb 176 reaction
abstract: The strong interplay between the nuclear structure and reaction dynamics near the Coulomb barrier makes the reaction observables a powerful tool for probing the structural properties. To disentangle the roles of nuclear deformation and positive $Q$-value neutron transfer channels, the angular distributions for quasielastic scattering and neutron transfer have been measured for $^{14}\mathrm{N}+^{176}\mathrm{Yb}$ system and analyzed in the context of the midshell heavy nuclei $A=176$, where inelastic and transfer couplings compete each other. The measured angular distributions for quasielastic and one-neutron transfer have been interpreted in light of coupled reaction calculations using the $\mathrm{FRESCO}$ code. Analysis of the quasielastic angular distribution indicated a strong influence of inelastic excitations arising from the large nuclear deformation of $^{176}\mathrm{Yb}$ nucleus. The influence of $2n$-pickup channel was calculated in the single-step and sequential modes. The analysis suggests that the $2n$-pickup channel have a feeble impact on the angular distribution and the transfer of $2n$ in step mode more adequately explains the experimental data. Furthermore, the analysis of the angular distribution for one neutron pickup channel suggested a significant contribution from higher energy states compared to lower energy states, which might be due to the large deformation of $^{176}\mathrm{Yb}$ nucleus. The present study validates the reported values of deformation parameters and spectroscopic factors, respectively, for the $^{176}\mathrm{Yb}$ nucleus. The results show a significant impact of the collective nature on the spectroscopic behavior of the reaction partners $^{14}\mathrm{N} + ^{176}\mathrm{Yb}$, which is reflected in the experimental observables. These measurements provide important input for separating the contributions of positive $Q$-value transfer channels and nuclear deformation in governing the fusion dynamics.

title: Updating GEANIE Pu 239 prompt γ -ray experimental data using a modern Hauser-Feshbach fission fragment decay model
abstract: We calculate fission $\ensuremath{\gamma}$ rays for neutron-induced reactions on $^{239}\mathrm{Pu}$ with the Hauser-Feshbach fission fragment decay model. By applying the calculated fission $\ensuremath{\gamma}$ rays as a background contribution, the historical $^{239}\mathrm{Pu}(n\text{,}xn\ensuremath{\gamma})$ reaction cross section data measured by the GEANIE (GErmanium Array for Neutron Induced Excitations) spectrometer are corrected. The correction also includes other $(n\text{,}xn)$ reactions that have very similar energies to the $\ensuremath{\gamma}$ lines reported by GEANIE. In many cases, the original GEANIE data are strongly reduced and they become much closer to the statistical Hauser-Feshbach model predictions. The total inelastic scattering, $(n\text{,}2n)$, and $(n\text{,}3n)$ cross sections are inferred based on the corrected GEANIE data, and compared with available experimental data as well as the statistical model calculations. Expected $\ensuremath{\gamma}$-ray energy spectra for neutron-induced measurements on $^{239}\mathrm{Pu}$ are also discussed.

title: Production of the 4 ΛHe hypernucleus in Au+Au collisions at √s NN = 3 GeV with STAR
abstract: Abstract The STAR experiment reports the first measurement of the ⁴ΛHe hypernuclei yield as a function of rapidity and transverse momentum in 0–50% central Au+Au collisions at √s NN = 3 GeV. The ⁴ΛHe is reconstructed through its three-body decay channel, ⁴ΛHe → ³He + p + π⁻, with a statistical significance of about 9.5 standard deviations. We find that the yield of ⁴ΛHe as a function of rapidity is consistent with that of ⁴ΛH, and the rapidity-dependent yield ratio of ⁴ΛHe/⁴ΛH is consistent with that of ³He/t. All the measurements, as well as the transverse-momentum spectra, can be reasonably described by the JAM with a coalescence afterburner, suggesting a coalescence-based formation scenario for hyper-nuclei at this energy. The canonical thermal model reproduces the observed yield ratios but overpredicts the absolute hypernuclei yields.

title: First observation and interpretation of ion cyclotron emission from energetic ions accelerated by lower hybrid waves in a tokamak plasma
abstract: Abstract We report the first observation of ion cyclotron emission (ICE) from a tokamak plasma during lower hybrid wave (LHW) injection and electron cyclotron resonance heating. Using a novel approach derived from linear kinetic theory, we infer key parameter values for the LHW-accelerated fast-ion distribution which drives the observed ICE spectra, and for the bulk plasma. These ICE spectra from deuterium plasmas in the EAST tokamak exhibit peaks at successive deuterium cyclotron harmonics, consistent with the collective relaxation of energetic deuterons through the magnetosonic cyclotron instability (MCI). By carrying out a multi-dimensional parameter scan of MCI growth rates in high-resolution two-dimensional ( k ∥ , k _ b o t ) wavenumber space, we obtain best-fit values for: the magnetic field; plasma density; background electron and ion temperature; and the concentration of fast deuterons, together with their energy, pitch ( u ∥ / | u | ) and thermal spread. We find that the observed ICE spectrum is likely driven by 770 keV deuterons, plausibly accelerated through LHW–ion interactions, which then undergo the MCI. The assumptions of the linear analytically based model include an infinite homogeneous plasma, and a ring-beam distribution of fast deuterons. Our results demonstrate a new scenario in which ICE serves as a passive diagnostic of energetic ion populations, and invite further investigation of the ICE–LHW connection.

title: Equation of State for Warm Neutron Star Outer Crusts
abstract: Abstract We describe the equation of state (EoS) of a warm ion plasma as obtained by performing microscopic many-body simulations using molecular dynamics computational techniques. Using the cold one-component plasma (OCP) composition in the neutron star (NS) outer crust assumed in U. Murarka et al. with a representative heavy nucleus for each density, we refine previous calculations. We include electron screening and modeling of ions as finite-size Gaussian distributions in the interaction potential, together with an efficient Ewald energy summation procedure. From this, the EoS relation P ( n B , T ) is obtained as a function of baryonic number density n B ∈ [7.48 × 10 −10 , 2.09 × 10 −4 ] fm −3 and temperature k B T ∈ [1, 5] MeV in the NS outer crust conditions. In order to improve the usability of our results, we provide tabulated data values along with a neural network parameterization available in the Zenodo repository; see DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.15348712 . We find that even at moderate temperatures thermal effects of ions are key in the higher-density region closer to the inner crust, when described using a thermal effective parameterization based on the thermal adiabatic index Γ th . We compare our results with other EoSs in the literature and provide a critical discussion.

title: Erratum: New high-spin level scheme of neutron-rich Rh 112 [Phys. Rev. C 87, 057302 (2013)]
Long-Range and Short-Range Longitudinal Flow Decorrelations in the Quark-Gluon Plasma
abstract: The longitudinal structure of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) remains poorly constrained. Using a transport-model calculation of two-particle elliptic-flow correlations ${V}_{2\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}}(\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta})$ in relative pseudorapidity $\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta}$, we find two distinct initial-state components of flow decorrelation: a long-range component driven by the global geometry of participating nucleons and a short-range component reflecting local energy-deposition fluctuations. This short-range component extends to $|\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta}|\ensuremath{\sim}4$ and can be misidentified as final-state nonflow. For isobarlike nuclei with different shapes, the calculation predicts an experimentally testable fingerprint of this component: it dilutes the deformation contribution at small $|\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta}|$, so that the ${V}_{2\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}}(\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta})$ ratio between deformed and near-spherical systems, such as $\mathrm{U}+\mathrm{U}$-to-$\mathrm{Au}+\mathrm{Au}$, rises with $|\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta}|$. Separating long- and short-range flow decorrelations from nonflow gives access to the longitudinal initial structure and dynamics of the QGP.

title: Poisoned hunting weapons, megafauna, and plant use at a 125,000-year-old Arabian paleolakeshore
abstract: After the African origin of Homo sapiens , multiple dispersals radiated into Asia, yet the Saharo-Arabian archaeological record remains sparse. In this study, we report on ‘Uruq Aljelibah, a Middle Paleolithic site dated to ~125,000 years ago (marine isotope stage 5e) and located on the shore of Mundafan paleolake, Saudi Arabia. Levallois assemblages, refits, and megafaunal associations indicate in situ tool production and carcass processing. Stone tool residues, use-wear, and biomarkers reveal animal and plant processing, including palms, tubers, trees, and shrubs. Several points exhibit impact damage and poison residues (from Acokanthera schimperi ), indicating use as hafted weapon tips within composite hunting systems. Megafaunal remains include hippopotamus, buffalo, gazelle, ostrich, and camel, illuminating hominin use of freshwater and grassland ecosystems.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: Giant elastoresistance in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene
abstract: Strongly correlated and topological phases in moiré materials are exquisitely sensitive to lattice geometry at both atomic and superlattice length scales. Twist angle, pressure, and strain directly modify the lattice and thus act as highly effective tuning parameters. Here, we examined electrical transport in twisted bilayer graphene subjected to continuous uniaxial strain. Near the magic angle (≈1.1°), devices exhibited a pronounced elastoresistance that depended on band filling and temperature, with a gauge factor more than two orders of magnitude larger than that of conventional metals. In selected doping regimes, the elastoresistance exhibited a Curie-Weiss–like temperature divergence. We discuss possible microscopic origins, including nematic fluctuations and enhanced electronic entropy from fluctuating isospin moments. Our work establishes uniaxial strain as a versatile probe of correlated physics in a moiré material.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: Nuclear pasta in hot neutron-star matter and proto–neutron stars
abstract: We investigate nuclear pasta phases appearing in hot neutron-star matter based on the compressible liquid-drop model, where the matter consists of a dense liquid phase and a dilute gas phase separated by a sharp interface. The surface tension is calculated self-consistently from the Thomas-Fermi approximation, and it depends on temperature and isospin asymmetry. We employ relativistic mean-field models with different symmetry energy slopes to describe nuclear interactions. It is found that the TM1e model with a small symmetry energy slope of $L=40$ MeV predicts various pasta shapes at low temperatures, while the TM1 model with $L=110.8$ MeV yields only the droplet configuration up to the crust-core transition density. We examine the occurrence and influence of pasta phases in proto-neutron stars with a constant entropy per baryon. These pasta phases may occur in the inner crust with a thickness of about $1.2$ km, playing an important role in the thermal evolution of the star.

title: Is the Large Uncertainty of δ C P Fundamentally Encoded in the Neutrino Quantum State?
abstract: The precise measurement of the leptonic -violating phase δ C P remains one of the major open challenges in neutrino physics, as current experiments achieve only very limited accuracy. We address this issue through the lens of quantum estimation theory. A distinctive feature of neutrino oscillation experiments is that they cannot freely optimize the probe or measurement, since both are constrained by the production and detection of flavor eigenstates. We therefore examine whether the large uncertainty in δ C P originates from intrinsic properties—either of the neutrino quantum state or of flavor measurements—or if it instead stems from experimental limitations. By comparing quantum and classical Fisher information, we demonstrate that the limited sensitivity to δ C P originates primarily from the information content of flavor measurements. Furthermore, we show that, while targeting the second oscillation maximum, as in the ESS ν SB proposal, typically enhances δ C P information, this feature in fact strongly depends on the actual values of δ C P .

title: Relativistic medium effects and spectroscopic factor systematics in proton radioactivity near the drip line
abstract: Abstract Proton radioactivity provides a powerful probe of nuclear structure beyond the proton drip line and offers stringent tests for nuclear interaction models. We demonstrate that the relativistic density-dependent DDR3Y interaction, combined with Relativistic Hartree Bogoliubov (RHB) densities obtained with the DD-ME2 parameter set, yields the lowest MSE among the examined folding approaches in reproducing experimental proton-decay half-lives across 43 distinct measured states in the range 53 ≤ Z ≤ 83. Nuclear potentials are constructed within the single-folding model using Skyrme density distributions (SLy7, BSk14, and SkM*) folded with the M3Y–Paris interaction, alongside RHB densities folded with the density-dependent DDR3Y interaction. Proton decay half- lives are calculated using the WKB approximation. The role of the attractive component of the NN interaction in determining the depth of the potential pocket is analyzed in detail, with particular attention to high-angular-momentum (lp = 5) emitters for which the Bohr–Sommerfeld quantization condition provides a consistency check on independently assigned proton configurations and potential pockets, with renormalization defined relative to the adopted unscaled interaction and no universal upper bound of unity. A new empirical spectroscopic factor (Sp) formula incorporating four variables (decay energy, angular momentum, isospin asymmetry, and quadrupole deformation) is proposed as a principal result of this work. The formula is calibrated empirically within the DDR3Y(DD-ME2) framework and introduces a term coupling angular momentum to the decay-energy scale, with deformation dependence that may include omitted barrier effects. When applied to DDR3Y half-lives, the formula achieves training MSE = 0.1393 and SD = 0.3777; fixed-form leave-one-out cross-validation gives MSE = 0.1616, compared with 0.2304 for the Universal Decay Law for Protons (UDLP). The Qp-value sensitivity is reported for each measured state, spanning 0.63–2.37 decades per 0.1 MeV, identifying three sensitivity groups and the mass measurements most critical for improving predictive power. Half-lives for 12 unobserved or unquantified proton emitters near the drip line are predicted, with local barrier uncertainty estimates derived from Qp-value sensitivity.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: np ↔ dγ reactions calculated up to Eγ = 20 MeV
abstract: Abstract We calculate the electromagnetic dipole transition cross sections for the $np \rightarrow d\gamma$ and $ d\gamma \rightarrow np$ reactions over a broad range of energies.~We use the LENPIC nucleon-nucleon interaction obtained from chiral effective field theory ($\chi$EFT) up to next-to-next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N4LO) and effective electromagnetic dipole transition operators obtained from the same $\chi$EFT up to N2LO. Our results agree with existing experiments.~We get results at energies for which experimental data and/or modern theoretical calculations have not been reported. \color{black} In this study, we utilize a new approach, namely, our adaptation of the Efros [V.~D.~Efros, Phys. Rev. C \textbf{99}, 034620 (2019)] method that is prospective for future many-body applications in calculations of bound and continuum state wave functions.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Design of a multifunctional Doppler backscattering diagnostic for the Pegasus-III experiment
abstract: The Doppler backscattering (DBS) diagnostic measures flows and electron density fluctuations. Recent work indicates that DBS can also infer the magnetic pitch angle [Yeoh et al., Nucl. Fusion 66, 016052 (2026)]. We present the preliminary design of a DBS for the Pegasus-III experiment. This DBS will serve two objectives. First, it will advance diagnostic science by supporting understanding of the DBS instrumentation functions, using DBS to constrain the magnetic equilibrium, and data-driven inference of plasma properties from DBS signals. Second, it will support Pegasus-III’s research directions, such as solenoid-free plasma initiation and O–X–B mode conversion for heating and current drive, since density fluctuations can affect O–X mode conversion efficiency, while magnetic pitch angle measurements can help constrain the optimum O–X launch angle window. This ex-vacuum DBS system uses a single channel, tunable Ka-band source, a corrugated horn antenna, and a homodyne I/Q receiver with baseband digitization. For greater flexibility, which is especially important for pitch angle measurements, the quasi-optical elements include a rotatable spinner for O- and X-mode selection and a mirror with 2D steering. Using the Scotty beam-tracing code [Hall-Chen et al., Plasma Phys. Controlled Fusion 64, 095002 (2022)], we find that, for a range of poloidal launch angles of 8°–18° and a corresponding toroidal launch angle between 0° and 3° for maximal backscattered DBS power, the DBS system is capable of measuring ion-scale density fluctuations 1 ≲ |k⊥,c| ≲ 8 cm−1 at a range of normalized radial coordinates from the outer core (ρ ∼ 0.65) to just beyond the last-closed flux surface (LCFS), where ρ = 0 corresponds to the magnetic axis and ρ = 1 corresponds to the LCFS. The system is also designed with additional toroidal steering capability, −4° to 8°, to resolve the toroidal response needed for magnetic pitch angle measurements.

title: DC cryogenic modeling of open-source SkyWater 130 nm MOSFETs at 77 K using BSIM4
abstract: Abstract Cryogenic applications in high-energy physics (HEP) demand reliable, low-power CMOS electronics capable of operating at liquid nitrogen temperatures (77 K). The open-source SkyWater 130 nm (SKY130) CMOS process has previously been shown to operate at temperatures as low as 4 K making it a promising candidate for HEP applications. In this work, we characterize and model SKY130 low-threshold voltage transistors at 77 K, which is a temperature commonly used in modeling applications for liquid argon detectors. DC characteristic measurements were performed at both room temperature and liquid nitrogen temperature. We created a cryogenic modeling approach to produce a SPICE-compatible, isothermal BSIM4-based model for select transistor sizes at 77 K. The resulting model agrees with data at 77 K with an average error on the order of 20% (relative RMS). However, our models had a systematic overprediction specifically for the measured pMOS devices at the lowest measured drain bias. Due to the open-source nature of SKY130, we have made our models publicly available on Github. We hope this work will continue the trend for democratizing circuit design at cryogenic temperatures in high-energy physics by enabling open access to accurate CMOS device models at 77 K.

title: Accessing exotic hadronic states via charmed-meson femtoscopy in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
abstract: The two-particle correlation function measured in femtoscopic analyses provides access to the interaction potentials between emitted particles. This offers a unique opportunity to investigate interactions among charmed mesons and to explore the nature of possible exotic hadronic states. In this Letter, we study femtoscopic correlations of various charmed-meson pairs in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The dynamical evolution of the system and charm hadron production are described within the Parton-Hadron-String Dynamics (PHSD) transport approach, while the correlation functions are computed using the Correlation Analysis Tool using the Schrödinger equation (CATS). We demonstrate that heavy-ion collisions provide a significantly more favorable environment than $pp$ collisions for accessing charmed meson femtoscopic correlations. This arises from enhanced charm-quark production, reduced relative momenta due to in-medium energy loss, and a strong suppression of initial-state correlations. Our results indicate that femtoscopic measurements in heavy-ion collisions offer a sensitive probe of charmed meson interactions and possible hadronic molecular states.

title: Rotating neutron star migrations as a standardized test for 3+1 numerical relativity
Comparative investigation of temperature-dependent defect evolution and irradiation hardening in CVD and ITER-like tungsten
abstract: Abstract Chemical vapor deposited tungsten (CVD-W) is known for its high thermal stability of the microstructure and lower susceptibility to deuterium-induced blistering compared to ITER-like W (IL-W). However, it remains unclear whether these advantages extend to displacement damage tolerance. To address this, CVD-W and ITER-like tungsten (IL-W) were irradiated with 6 MeV copper ions up to 0.6 dpa at room temperature (RT), 773 K, and 973 K. Transmission electron microscopy, defect statistics, and nano-indentation revealed comparable damage accumulation and irradiation hardening in both materials across all investigated temperatures. At RT, both materials exhibited dense dislocation networks and loops, together with very sparsely distributed voids, resulting in comparable increases in hardness. At elevated temperatures, these networks disappeared, giving way to dislocation loop strings and dislocation lines, along with an increased density of voids, accompanied by further irradiation hardening. The dispersed barrier hardening model analysis indicates that the dominant contribution to irradiation hardening transitions from dislocation structures at RT to voids at elevated temperatures. In addition, differences in dislocation morphology and nature were observed between the two materials. Displacement damage defects in CVD-W exhibited higher mobility than in IL-W, as evidenced by an expanded damage layer, a higher degree of dislocation loop ordering into one-dimensional strings, a larger fraction of glissile 1/2<111> dislocation loops, and a greater proportion of loops exceeding 10 nm at ⩾773 K, mainly owing to its lower impurity content. This further supports void-dominated hardening at elevated temperatures, as different dislocation morphologies observed at elevated temperatures had minimal impact on the overall hardening. These findings provide valuable insights into the irradiation response of CVD-W under fusion-relevant conditions.

title: First beam demonstration of a conduction-cooled Nb 3 Sn superconducting rf photoinjector
abstract: We report on the first beam produced by the world’s first conduction-cooled superconducting radio frequency (srf) photogun. Over the past 5 years, Euclid, working in collaboration with Fermilab and Argonne National Laboratory, has been developing a continuous-wave (cw), 1.5-cell, MeV-scale, conduction-cooled srf photogun operating at 1.3 GHz. The primary objective of this effort is to demonstrate ultrastable electron beams for ultrafast electron microscopy/diffraction (UEM/UED) applications, enabled by the exceptional shot-to-shot stability achievable with srf technology compared to room-temperature rf photoguns. Although srf systems were historically too costly for industrial deployment, two recent advancements: Nb 3 Sn coatings and conduction cooling, have dramatically reduced system complexity and operating costs. This srf photogun is designed to deliver true cw rf operation while dissipating only ∼ 2 W of rf power, eliminating the need for a high-power rf system and significantly reducing facility footprint. This srf photogun also features a raised Nb 3 Sn backwall serving as the photocathode, removing the need for an external cathode insert. cw rf operation with limited repetitive beam has been demonstrated. In this paper, we present the first beam results from this system along with its cooldown performance, Q -slope behavior, synchronization characteristics, and initial beam parameters.

title: Noninvasive tuning of the parallel-coupled accelerating structures based on the bead-pull measurements
MeerKAT discovery of a high-redshift strongly lensed hydroxyl gigamaser
abstract: ABSTRACT At low redshifts, hydroxyl megamasers (OHMs) have been shown to trace galaxy mergers, obscured starbursts, high molecular gas densities, and candidate dual supermassive black hole systems. Given this astrophysical utility, exploring these sources at larger cosmological look-back times is therefore of key interest. While previous OHM surveys have been limited to redshifts of $z \lesssim 0.25$, the ability to expand the OHM frontier is significantly enhanced with new high-sensitivity radio facilities such as MeerKAT. In this letter, we report the discovery of an OHM in the gravitational lens system HATLAS J142935.3–002836 at $z = 1.027$, the most distant OHM source detected so far. The spectrum has blended 1667 and 1665 MHz emission and exhibits a highly complex profile, with spectral components ranging in widths from $\lt 8$ to ${\sim}300$ km s$^{-1}$. The integrated (magnification uncorrected) luminosity of log($L_{\rm OH}~/~L_{\odot }$) = 5.51 $\pm$ 0.67 makes this the most apparently luminous OHM known to date. In the same wide-band data set, we have also detected a previously unknown H i absorption line. The signal-to-noise ratio of over 150 with just a 4.7 h observation highlights the potential that MeerKAT and the future Square Kilometre Array mid-frequency array offer to explore the high-redshift OHM universe.
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

A Log-Uniform Initial Magnetic Field Distribution Explains Pulsar and Magnetar Populations through Magnetic Inclination Alignment
abstract: Abstract The origin of the gap in the observed magnetic field distribution between pulsars and magnetars raises a challenge to understanding these populations within a unified framework. We analytically show that the gap can be naturally explained by the alignment of the magnetic inclination angle between the magnetic and spin axes. Based on coupled evolution of spin-down and magnetic inclination angle in the plasma-filled magnetosphere, the alignment timescale follows τα∝B−2. Thus, strongly magnetized neutron stars including high-B pulsars and magnetars align more rapidly than pulsars with 1012 G, reducing their beaming fraction and thereby suppressing their observed numbers. However, magnetars are primarily identified through X-ray activity and are therefore relatively less affected by beaming. Taking into account both beaming fraction and luminosity corrections, we reconstruct the initial magnetic field distribution from the observed distribution. We show that pulsars and magnetars do not dictate intrinsically distinct initial distributions, but can instead be understood within a single continuous initial magnetic field distribution, such as a log-uniform distribution.
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

title: Suppression of the two-stream instability by quantum effects: numerical analysis with Wigner–Poisson and Nyquist method
abstract: Abstract The quantum two-stream instability in electrostatic plasmas is investigated through high-resolution numerical simulations of the Wigner–Poisson system. A fourth-order operator splitting scheme, which combines exact Fourier treatment of the free-streaming term with a semiclassical approximation of the quantum force, is implemented to achieve high temporal accuracy and minimal numerical dissipation. This approach enables precise extraction of linear growth rates and detailed characterization of the long-time nonlinear evolution. Systematic simulations demonstrate that quantum diffraction effects, parameterized by the dimensionless quantum parameter ℏ ¯ , significantly reduce the growth rate of the two-stream instability and lead to its complete suppression above a critical value ℏ ¯ c ≈ 0.78 . The stabilization mechanism is independently confirmed by high-resolution Nyquist diagrams constructed directly from the spatially averaged simulated Wigner function, showing excellent quantitative agreement (typically within 5 % (absolute difference Δ γ ≲ 0.001 )) with growth rates extracted from the time evolution of the electrostatic field energy E field ( t ) . While the semiclassical approximation remains accurate to within 2% for ℏ ¯ ⩽ 0.6 , its relative error increases to 10%–25% near the stabilization threshold. Simulations employing the full non-local quantum operator yield a slightly lower threshold, ℏ ¯ c ≈ 0.74 ± 0.02 . The combined effect of quantum diffraction and Bhatnagar–Gross–Krook collisions is also examined, revealing a synergistic stabilization that further lowers the critical quantum parameter. In the nonlinear regime, the Wigner function displays distinct quantum signatures, including smoother filamentation and reduced vortex formation compared to the classical case. A comparison with a properly formulated two-fluid quantum-hydrodynamic model based on the Bohm potential shows that the fluid description systematically overestimates the stabilizing effect of quantum diffraction, predicting complete suppression at a lower critical value ℏ ¯ c QHD ≈ 0.67 . This discrepancy of approximately 15% underscores the importance of full kinetic treatments over local fluid closures. These findings provide new benchmark values for quantum stabilization thresholds and highlight the limitations of fluid models based on the Bohm potential. Potential implications for inertial confinement fusion, high-energy-density plasmas, and nanoscale semiconductor devices are discussed.

title: First assessment of neutral gas transport in the EU DEMO low aspect ratio divertor
abstract: Abstract Efficient removal of neutral particles from the divertor region is essential for maintaining acceptable plasma conditions and ensuring reliable operation of future fusion reactors. In the present work, the neutral gas dynamics in the sub-divertor region of the DEMO low aspect ratio (LAR) divertor are investigated using three-dimensional Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) simulations. A 3D complex model of one divertor sector is employed to quantify particle exhaust through the pumping openings, neutral leakage through the toroidal and poloidal gaps, and the corresponding pressure and temperature distributions. The influence of the divertor entrance pressure and the effective pumping probability is systematically examined, together with the effect of asymmetric pressure conditions at the divertor entry gaps. The results show that the pumping probability is the dominant parameter controlling the exhaust performance, increasing the pumped particle flux while reducing neutral leakage, particularly through the toroidal gaps. Changes in the divertor entrance pressure mainly affect the absolute pressure levels, with only a limited influence on the overall flow field. Simulations with asymmetric injection pressures indicate that pressure imbalances between the two divertor entry gaps have moderate effect on the neutral transport. Over the investigated conditions, 57.9%–86.4% of the incoming neutral particles return to the plasma region through the divertor entry gaps, while the pumped fraction ranges from 1.74% to 22% of the incoming flux, increasing with both the pumping probability and the injection pressure. To complement the DSMC analysis, a reduced-order conductance model is developed for rapid engineering assessments. The model captures the overall pressure distribution and DSMC trends with an average absolute deviation of ∼29% in only a few seconds, making it suitable for preliminary design studies. Overall, these results quantify neutral gas transport and pumping performance in the DEMO LAR divertor and support particle exhaust development.

title: Screening effects in nuclear fusion processes: General treatment and exact solution for the Hulthen potential
Using neural posterior estimators to calibrate and propagate constitutive data uncertainties for resistive magnetohydrodynamic liner simulations
abstract: Electrical conductivity and equation-of-state (EoS) models are key inputs to magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations of imploding liners, but uncertainties in these constitutive data can strongly influence predicted current transport, heating, compression, and melt dynamics. We present a Bayesian simulation-based inference framework, based on neural posterior estimators, for calibrating and propagating uncertainties in constitutive data used in hydrodynamic simulations of liner implosions. The method proceeds in two stages. First, parametric uncertainties in conductivity and EoS models are calibrated against literature data assembled in First Light Fusion's Physics Assurance Database (PAD) to define physically informed priors. Second, these uncertainties are propagated through ensembles of coupled circuit-MHD simulations and conditioned against fiber-optic current-sensor and photonic Doppler velocimetry measurements from a pulsed-power-driven aluminum liner experiment. Neural posterior estimators are used to perform likelihood-free inference over both constitutive and load-coupling parameters. For the experimental case considered, including calibrated constitutive uncertainty reduces the inferred liner-current fraction by approximately 5% and delays the median melt-wave burnthrough time by approximately 90 ns, while broadening both posterior distributions. The aluminum constitutive parameters themselves are only weakly updated beyond the PAD-informed prior. These results demonstrate the importance of propagating independently calibrated constitutive uncertainty through integrated MHD inference, where it can materially influence inferred load coupling and melt dynamics even when the constitutive parameters themselves are only weakly updated by the experimental data.

title: Absolute calibration of fs two-photon absorption laser-induced fluorescence for atomic species measurements
abstract: An absolute calibration technique is employed in fs two-photon absorption laser-induced fluorescence (TALIF) measurements of O atoms. In this approach, most of the O2 molecules in a reference mixture (0.125% O2–Ar) dissociate into O atoms in a repetitive ns pulse discharge sustained in a heated plasma flow reactor, such that their mole fraction approaches twice the initial O2 mole fraction. The results are placed on the absolute scale using the gas temperature measurements by ns Rayleigh scattering. The present calibration is used to measure the absolute number densities of O atoms in 0.125%–20% O2–Ar mixtures excited by a ns pulse discharge over a range of temperatures. The results are compared with a conventional O TALIF calibration in Xe, using the two-photon absorption cross section ratio of σXe2σO2=0.73, based on the direct absorption measurements on 5p6 1S0 → 6p′[3/2]2 xenon transition and 2p4 3P2,1,0 → 3p 3P1,2,0 oxygen transitions, showing good agreement. The present method is not affected by the uncertainty in the cross section ratio. The use of the present approach is recommended for assessing the accuracy and range of applicability of Xe calibration for fs O TALIF.

title: Hyper-Nuclei $^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{He}$ Production in $\sqrt{s_{\rm{NN}}}$ = 3 GeV Au+Au collisions at RHIC
abstract: The STAR experiment reports the first measurement of the $^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{He}$ hyper-nuclei yield as a function of rapidity and transverse momentum in 0-50% central Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm{NN}}} =$ 3 GeV. The $^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{He}$ is reconstructed through its three-body decay channel, $^4_{\Lambda}\rm{He} \rightarrow {}^{3}\rm{He} + \rm{p} + \pi^-$, with a statistical significance of about 9.5 standard deviations. We find that the yield of $^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{He}$ as a function of rapidity is consistent with that of $^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{H}$, and the rapidity-dependent yield ratio of $^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{He}$/$^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{H}$ is consistent with that of $^3$He/t. All the measurements, as well as the transverse-momentum spectra, can be reasonably described by the JAM with a coalescence afterburner, suggesting a coalescence-based formation scenario for hyper-nuclei at this energy. The canonical thermal model reproduces the observed yield ratios but overpredicts the absolute hyper-nuclei yields.

title: Spurious Isospin Breaking in the In-medium Similarity Renormalization Group
abstract: The in-medium similarity renormalization group is a promising ab initio approach for computing the isospin-related theoretical correction $\delta_C$ to superallowed beta decay rates, relevant for tests of CKM unitarity. An essential requirement of such corrections is a properly quantified theoretical uncertainty. While isospin symmetry is explicitly broken by internucleon forces, approximations made in the solving the many-body problem can also spuriously break the symmetry, obscuring the desired signal. In this work, we use a toy model to identify the primary sources of spurious isospin symmetry breaking introduced by the IMSRG many-body framework, and provide mitigation strategies for application in large-scale calculations.

title: Precision Mass Measurements of \textsuperscript{130}Te, \textsuperscript{130}Sn, and Their Impact on Models for R-Process Nucleosynthesis
abstract: The astrophysical rapid neutron capture nucleosynthesis process (r-process) remains an active area of research due to the fact that it occurs in extreme conditions and involves reactions with exotic nuclei that are difficult to study experimentally. For the first time using the Phase-Imaging Ion Cyclotron Resonance (PI-ICR) technique, we measured the mass excesses of \textsuperscript{130}Te, \textsuperscript{130}Sn, and \textsuperscript{130}Sn\textsuperscript{m} with the Canadian Penning Trap (CPT). Our results show good agreement with previous Penning trap values obtained using the Time-of-Flight Ion Cyclotron Resonance (TOF-ICR) and the Fourier Transform Ion Cyclotron Resonance (FT-ICR) techniques, while being twice as precise for \textsuperscript{130}Sn. These new mass excesses were added to a SkyNet network calculation to determine their impact on r-process abundances and to find the best astrophysical conditions to reproduce the Solar System r-process abundance pattern. Finally, by treating lighter and heavier elements separately, we assess the relative frequency of events producing elements in a cold versus a hot r-process scenario.

title: Formation of superheavy elements 119 and 120 in the $^{50}$Ti+$^{249}$Bk and $^{50}$Ti+$^{249}$Cf reactions: dinuclear system dynamics, survival probability, and decay chains of the evaporation residues
abstract: The $^{50}$Ti+$^{249}$Bk and $^{50}$Ti+$^{249}$Cf reactions leading to the compound nuclei $^{299}$119 and $^{299}$120 are studied in the framework of the dinuclear system (DNS) model. The capture cross section has been calculated by solving the dynamical equations of motion for all orientation angles of the deformed target nucleus and for the zero-point vibrations of the projectile. The charge distribution of the DNS fragments has been obtained from the transport master equation with transition rates obeying detailed balance, and the compound nucleus formation probability has been calculated as the branching ratio of the level densities over the intrinsic fusion, quasifission, and symmetry barriers. The survival probability has been calculated in the Hauser-Feshbach formalism for every excitation energy and angular momentum of the compound nucleus, with the fission barriers of the macroscopic-microscopic model with triaxial saddle points. The normalization of the saddle-point level density has been fixed by the measured evaporation residue (ER) cross sections of the $^{48}$Ca+$^{244}$Pu reaction. The largest ER cross sections are obtained in the 3n channel, 18 fb at $E^*_\mathrm{CN}=32$ MeV for $^{50}$Ti+$^{249}$Cf and 27 fb at 33 MeV for $^{50}$Ti+$^{249}$Bk. At the energy of the GSI experiments, the calculated sums of the 3n and 4n cross sections, 4 and 6 fb, respectively, are well below the upper limits of 200 and 65 fb obtained there. With the normalization refitted, the alternative mass tables and fission barriers considered here give the maximum 3n cross sections smaller by up to a factor of 25. The $\alpha$-decay chains of the residues have been predicted; the isotopes of element 120 are expected to have half-lives of 1-12 $\mu$s and those of element 119 of 16-230 $\mu$s.

title: Are neutrinos Majorana? Fixed-target and high-energy astrophysical searches decide
abstract:
The original version of this paper proposed a new approach to determining whether neutrinos are Dirac or Majorana fermions, a fundamental open question in particle physics. Conventional searches rely on neutrinoless double beta decay, but this electron-only channel suffers from blind spots. We propose a new, complementary probe to overcome this limitation. A heavy neutral lepton (HNL) triggers a high-energy shift in how the active neutrino flavors ($
u_e$, $
u_\mu$, $
u_	au$) mix---but only if the neutrinos are Majorana. For GeV-scale HNLs, the upcoming beam-dump experiment SHiP can discover the HNL and measure how it mixes with the active flavors. However, the proposed signature of the Majorana nature of neutrinos does not exist. The reasons are explained here. The analysis has been superseded by Ref.~\cite{Barenboim:2026udr}. The original version is retained as v1 for the record.

title: The Alpha Clustering Model of the EMC Effect
abstract: For more than forty years, the EMC effect, the observation that nuclear structure functions in deep-inelastic scattering appear to be modified relative to the free-nucleon expectation, has resisted a consensus microscopic explanation. In this letter, we argue that the strength and $A$ dependence of the EMC effect may be governed by the phenomena of $\alpha$ clustering in nuclei and responsible for a majority of the partonic modification associated with the EMC Effect. We motivate the alpha clustering model of the EMC effect (ACME), and with a data driven approach, we demonstrate how such a model can reproduce the existing deep inelastic scattering data on nuclei. We make predictions for other nuclei such as $^{16}$O, $^{20}$Ne, and $^{48}$Ca and explore its consequences for a spin-dependent EMC effect and global analysis of nuclear parton distributions.

title: Element-specific, non-destructive profiling of two-dimensional dopant layers in silicon
abstract: Abstract Starting points for silicon-based quantum devices can be δ -layers of dopants from group V in the periodic table. Deterministic doping leading to few-atom devices requires these layers to be ultrathin. A recent breakthrough has been to use arsenic rather than phosphorous as dopant, which together with optimized heat treatments has yielded δ -layers acting as quantum wells with widths down to 0.5 nm inferred from magneto-transport and angle-resolved photoemission, techniques sensitive to the conduction electrons only. These widths are considerably smaller than the resolution-limited chemical thickness of 2 nm from the standard measurement technique, namely secondary-ion mass spectroscopy, and so leaves open the question of whether the dopant layers are indeed as thin as the extent of the conduction electron wavefunctions perpendicular to the layers. Here, we present resonant-contrast X-ray reflectometry experiments and analysis—including both full modeling and a simple perturbation approach—to demonstrate that the sub-nm electronic thickness of the δ -layers corresponds to sub-nm chemical thickness. We take advantage of the change in the scattering factor of atoms as their core level resonances are scanned by varying the X-ray energy. In combination with X-ray fluorescence imaging, this enables non-destructive three-dimensional elemental characterization of nano-structured quantum devices.

title: Measurement of the $^{169}$Tm$(\gamma,n)$$^{168}$Tm Cross Section and Implications for $\gamma$-Process Calculations
abstract: The $^{169}\mathrm{Tm}(\gamma,n)^{168}\mathrm{Tm}$ cross section has been measured at the Shanghai Laser Electron Gamma Source (SLEGS) using quasi-monoenergetic laser-Compton-scattering $\gamma$ rays over the energy range from the neutron threshold to 14.61~MeV. The photon flux and energy distribution were determined with a LaBr$3$(Ce) spectrometer, and monoenergetic cross sections were obtained using an iterative unfolding method. Below 12~MeV, the present cross sections agree well with the NewSUBARU data and the IAEA-2019 evaluations. However, near the maximum of the $(\gamma,n)$ excitation function, the present cross sections are significantly higher than both the NewSUBARU data and the IAEA-2019 evaluated values. The $E1$ $\gamma$-ray strength functions were derived by fitting the experimental cross sections measured at SLEGS and NewSUBARU. The stellar reaction rates for $^{169}\mathrm{Tm}(\gamma,n)$ and $^{168}\mathrm{Tm}(n,\gamma)$ were calculated by incorporating these constrained $\gamma$-ray strength functions into the TALYS code. The calculated $^{169}\mathrm{Tm}(\gamma,n)$ rates were adopted in a full $p$-process reaction network for the shock-heated O/Ne-rich layers of a $20 M\odot$ core-collapse supernova model to perform a sensitivity analysis. The updated rates have a negligible effect on the final $p$-nucleus abundances.

title: Machine Learning-Based Reconstruction for Resistive Silicon Sensors
abstract: Low-Gain Avalanche Diodes (LGADs) and AC-coupled Low-Gain Avalanche Diodes (AC-LGADs) are promising technologies for precision timing and four-dimensional tracking. In AC-LGADs, the AC pad is coupled to the resistive n$^{+}$ layer through a dielectric layer, while the gain layer remains unsegmented. This structure provides a 100\% fill factor and enables good spatial resolution with a relaxed readout pitch. The same signal-sharing mechanism that makes interpolation possible complicates the readout: charge spreads across multiple pads, the useful information can approach the electronic-noise threshold, and matrix-inversion approaches can become computationally challenging and sensitive to off-diagonal noise. In this work, we study machine-learning-based reconstruction and compression for resistive silicon sensors. We use full-waveform information from correlated pads to regularise the reconstruction and extract spatial information beyond what is available from binary readouts or reduced-amplitude summaries. We first introduce recurrent neural network models based on LSTM layers, which provide a proof-of-concept implementation for full-waveform reconstruction and have been tested for FPGA deployment using \hls. We also study routes towards bandwidth reduction with waveform rasterisation and window-selection methods, and extend the approach beyond the first model to topology-agnostic transformer-based architectures that use pad coordinates as part of the input. These models are designed to support arbitrary pad counts and geometries, mitigate edge distortions, preserve approximately $10~\mu\mathrm{m}$ position resolution for $500~\mu\mathrm{m}\times500~\mu\mathrm{m}$ pitched sensors, and guide future resistive-silicon sensor designs

title: Density dependence of effective Lambda-nucleon interactions
abstract: Orbital-dependent $\Lambda$ binding energies in hypernuclei such as $^{208}_{\Lambda}$Pb, $^{40}_{\Lambda}$K, and $^{48}_{\Lambda}$K are important objectives of planned experiments at J-PARC and JLab and provide information on the density-dependent features of effective $\Lambda N$ interactions. To investigate this relation we introduce the environmental density $\bar{\rho}_\text{env}$, defined as the overlap integral of the \Lambda and nuclear core densities, as quantitative measure of the nuclear environment experienced by the $\Lambda$ in each orbital. Calculations are performed within the deformed Skyrme-Hartree-Fock framework, comparing several phenomenological and microscopic $\Lambda N$ interactions. We find an approximately linear relation between the orbital-dependent binding energies and $\bar{\rho}_\text{env}$, offering a quantitative means to test and refine effective $\Lambda N$ interactions using future orbital-dependent binding-energy data.

title: Screen-printed inorganic perovskite thick-film sensor for clinical electron beam quality assurance
abstract: Abstract In the field of radiation therapy, inorganic perovskites, which exhibit excellent radiation responsiveness, are attracting attention as solid-state sensor materials for precise quality assurance (QA). However, conventional nano-scale perovskite thin-films have limitations due to insufficient active volume in measuring high-energy (high-E) radiation characterized by high penetrating power. To overcome these limitations, we fabricated a micro-scale CsPbI 2 Br thick-film sensor and irradiated it with high-E electron beams of 6, 9, and 12 MeV using a clinical linear accelerator under experimental conditions closely simulating a clinical QA environment. The experimental results demonstrated that the fabricated sensor exhibited excellent linearity ( R 2 > 0.999) and repeatability (CV< 1.6%) within the dose range of 10 to 1000 MU. Furthermore, it showed a dose-rate independent response against dose-rate variations from 100 to 600 MU/min. In a comparative evaluation of the percent-depth dose (PDD) against an ionization chamber, the difference in R 50 was less than 1 mm, satisfying the clinical QA tolerance criterion. However, at deeper depths, overestimations were observed due to the photoelectric effect induced by scattered low-energy photons, which was attributed to the high atomic number of the sensor material. Additionally, this study has a limitation in evaluating long-term reliability due to the lack of proper encapsulation. In conclusion, the thick-film sensor fabricated in this study demonstrated outstanding dosimetric response characteristics. With further studies, such as the development of robust packaging techniques and compensation layers, it is highly anticipated to be widely utilized as a next-generation dosimeter for clinical radiotherapy QA.

title: A machine-learning method for the estimation of the background from jets misidentified as hadronic tau lepton decays
abstract: Abstract Backgrounds arising from quark- and gluon-initiated jets misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons constitute a major experimental challenge for analyses involving tau leptons. The MUltivariate Fake-Factor INference (MUFFIN) approach, a machine-learning-based method for estimating this background directly from observed events, is presented. Boosted decision tree reweighting is used to learn multidimensional, per-object correction factors directly from observed data, thereby modelling the jet to hadronic tau lepton misidentification probability across the kinematic and topological phase space without relying on low-dimensional parametrisations. Performance studies are presented using proton-proton collision data collected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC at √ s = 13.6 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62.4 fb -1 . Compared to low-dimensional parametrisation methods, improved modelling of key kinematic observables is achieved, particularly in regions of high p T . The improved modelling leads to a reduction of up to 70% in the systematic uncertainty associated with jets being misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons. The MUFFIN method provides a robust and scalable method for background estimation in precision measurements and searches for beyond-the-standard-model physics involving tau lepton final states.

title: Spin Wandering of an Accreting Neutron Star near Torque Balance: Implications for Gravitational-wave Searches
abstract: Abstract Torque balance between gravitational radiation reaction and magnetocentrifugal accretion is one reason why accreting neutron stars rotate slower than centrifugal breakup. Random processes in the accretion disk, such as Rayleigh–Taylor instabilities and flicker noise, drive the spin frequency f * and gravitational wave frequency f gw ∝ f * to wander stochastically around their torque balance values. Here it is shown theoretically, in terms of an idealized Ornstein–Uhlenbeck model, that the standard deviation of f gw is given by σ f gw ( h 0 ) ∝ f gw h 0 D β T 1 / 2 , or equivalently σ f gw ( F X ) ∝ f gw 1 / 2 F X 1 / 2 D β T 1 / 2 , where h 0 is the characteristic wave strain, F X is the X-ray flux, D is the source distance, and β and T are the fractional amplitude and autocorrelation timescale of the stochastic torque. One can use σ f gw ( h 0 ) and σ f gw ( F X ) to check the physical consistency of a detection candidate in a gravitational wave search by comparing with σ f gw observed. Spin wandering impacts search design, because it sets the maximum time interval max ( T coh ) , during which the signal may be treated as coherent. The Ornstein–Uhlenbeck calculation predicts 1 0 − 1 ≲ max ( T coh ) / ( 1 day ) ≲ 1 0 3 , with 3 × 10 −2 ≲ βT 1/2 /(1 s 1/2 ) ≲ 4, for Rayleigh–Taylor instabilities and flicker noise. The predicted max ( T coh ) is typically shorter than the year-long observation runs of audio-band interferometers operating today, emphasizing the utility of semicoherent search algorithms, which divide the data into multiple coherent segments of duration max ( T coh ) .

title: Most probable fission configurations and symmetric-asymmetric fission competition in Hg isotopes
abstract: Abstract The most probable fission fragment configurations $(A_L, A_H)$, $(Z_L, Z_H)$, and $(N_L, N_H)$, together with the relative contributions of symmetric and asymmetric fission channels, are systematically studied over a range of excitation energies for $^{178,180,182,183,184,190,192,194,195,196,198}\mathrm{Hg}^*$ isotopes using the dynamical cluster-decay model. The model uses updated bulk and neutron-proton asymmetry coefficients of the mass formula, adjusted to the AME2020 and/or FRDM(2012) mass evaluations, along with the temperature-dependent surface energy coefficient and nuclear deformations. The calculations show a consistent preference for charge-asymmetric configurations near the deformed shell closures $(Z_L, Z_H = 36, 44)$ at lower excitation energies throughout the isotopic chain. The neutron partition $(N_L, N_H)$ shows weaker isotopic dependence in the light fragment than in the heavy fragment, with the calculated light-fragment neutron number remaining near $N_L \approx 50$, while the heavy fragment accommodates a larger fraction of the isotopic neutron excess. For the lighter isotopes, $^{178-184}\mathrm{Hg}^{*}$, the asymmetric channel contribution is dominant at low excitation energies, associated with the deformed shell closures $(Z_L, Z_H = 36, 44)$ and at higher excitation energy the symmetric-fission channel contribution dominates, which is associated with $(Z_L= Z_H = 40)$. The transition toward predominantly symmetric fission occurs at an excitation energy of approximately 50 MeV. For the heavier isotopes $^{190-198}\mathrm{Hg}^{*}$, the asymmetric fission channel contribution likewise decreases with excitation energy, while the symmetric fission channel contribution increases, resulting in a near balance between the two fission channels at higher excitation energies. The increase in the calculated symmetric-fission channel cross-section with excitation energy is consistent with the increasing trend observed in the available experimental cross-sections.

title: Structure of correlations for the single-$j$ model using quantum information theory
abstract: We say that a system undergoes a quantum phase transition when the mean-field ground state of a given Hamiltonian spontaneously breaks its symmetries depending on the Hamiltonian parameters. It is a widely accepted view that this phenomenon enables the mean-field state to absorb the maximum amount of correlations without losing its mean-field structure. However, it is still uncertain how those correlations are incorporated within the mean-field state and how the correlation structure changes when we get closer to the exact ground state by restoring the symmetries. In this work, we answer these questions by studying the single-$j$ model, which is a realistic fermionic nuclear model with abelian and non-abelian broken symmetries. We find that both types of symmetries have very different effects for the correlations within the mean-field state. This makes unclear the concept of the symmetry breaking process as a mechanism to absorb the maximum amount of correlations. Moreover, the symmetry restoration redistributes existing `fake' correlations between paired orbitals to more complex subsystems.

title: Stable and causal frames for BDNK hydrodynamics
abstract: We establish the existence of families of linearly stable and causal Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun (BDNK) frames for arbitrary equation of state and set of physical transport coefficients. By developing a method based on simplification of Routh-Hurwitz criteria and telegrapher factorisation of polynomials, we provide six concrete examples of such families, three of which admit conformal limits, for both neutral and charged fluids. These frames have adjustable characteristic speeds and can serve as a starting point for numerical implementations of relativistic hydrodynamics in various settings. In the process we uncover a map between stable and causal frames in neutral fluids and stable and causal frames in charged fluids. We also develop an AI research protocol that can be used to search for such frames in any hydrodynamic theory.

title: Real-time data acquisition and instrumentation framework for load frequency regulation in an islanded microgrid under energy storage failures with electric vehicle impacts
abstract: Abstract This research presents a real-time instrumentation and data acquisition framework for load frequency regulation (LFR) in an islanded AC Microgrid (MG). A novel cascaded FOPTID-PTID controller with a noise-resilient derivative filtering technique has been proposed. The newly developed Chaos-Based Artificial Rabbits Optimization (CARO) algorithm has been used to fine-tune the controller parameters. The suggested technique successfully reduces frequency variations brought on by measurement noise, energy storage system (ESS) malfunctions, and uncertainty in renewable energy sources (RES). Additionally, the effect of EV integration on the LFR response under ESS failures and measurement noise has been examined. Sensitivity analysis is carried out under internal parametric uncertainties to evaluate the robustness of the controller. The performance of the system is tested using MATLAB/Simulink under different operating conditions. Real-time validation has been carried out using an OPAL-RT platform. The results confirm the effectiveness and practical feasibility of the proposed instrumentation and control framework.

title: Pseudoscalar meson masses in magnetic fields at zero temperature from lattice QCD
abstract: We study neutral and charged pseudoscalar meson masses in background magnetic fields in $(2+1)$-flavor QCD at zero temperature and physical quark masses. Using the highly improved staggered quark action at four lattice spacings, we obtain continuum-extrapolated masses from connected correlators for pions, kaons, and the fictitious $s\bar s$ pseudoscalar $\eta^0_{s\bar s}$. Neutral pseudoscalar masses decrease with increasing magnetic field, with the largest relative reduction for the neutral pion. In contrast, charged pion and kaon masses initially rise but tend to level off or decrease at stronger fields, departing from the point-particle lowest-Landau-level expectation. To investigate the origin of this field dependence, we compare neutral and charged pion masses at finite lattice spacings with the field included only in valence propagators or only in the sea-quark determinant. Valence-only masses approximately reproduce the full results, while sea-only masses remain close to their corresponding zero-field values.

title: Negative-Power Density of States in Chiral-Orthogonal Disordered Systems and the IR Phase of QCD
abstract: The recently discovered IR phase of QCD is characterized by an infrared (IR) sector of Dirac modes that separates and dynamically decouples from the bulk of the spectrum, becoming scale invariant in the process [1]. Among key features of this IR sector is the negative power-law behavior of Dirac spectral density near zero with power close to $-1$. Here we start investigating to what extent can this behavior be mimicked by chiral Anderson models. In particular, we study 3-D chiral-orthogonal systems with logarithmic off-diagonal disorder where negative-power ``spikes'' have been observed [2]. We find that for disorders of moderate strength $W$, these models in fact do not have a power-singular density of states (DOS) at zero energy in the thermodynamic limit. Rather, the corresponding power vanishes but the spectrum features a very accurate negative-power behavior on an interval around $E=1$, spreading increasingly closer to $E=0$ and $E=\infty$ with increasing $W$. We connect this to the fact that random hoppings $t$ in these quantum systems are drawn from a scale-invariant $1/t$ distribution regularized via $t \in [e^{-W/2}, e^{W/2}]$, and DOS with negative power can naturally arise inside that range. In fact, we find that power $p$ in the vicinity of energy $E$ satisfies $\lim_{W \to \infty} p(W, E) = -1$ for all $E$ we access. This indicates that, upon removing the cutoff $W$, quantum mechanics transforms the scale-invariant $1/t$ noise into a scale-invariant $1/E$ distribution of eigenstates, which mimics the interpretation of scale-invariant Dirac spectral densities in the IR phase as being due to scale-invariant glue backgrounds [1]. Our results imply that, when modeling the IR phase, the IR cutoff in chiral Anderson systems needs to be tied to their randomness strength $W$ rather than to their lattice size $L$.

title: Gibbsian Entropy for General Wigner Distributions
abstract: We propose a definition of non-equilibrium Gibbsian entropy applicable to general quantum systems, computable from Wigner functions, for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian states. We show that while the Wigner function is a quasi-probability distribution, fundamental results linking observables in repeated observations to the function, such as the law of large numbers, the central limit theorem and, crucially, the relation between the entropy and the cumulant generating function continue to apply. This ideas are the core of the large deviation theory, which allow to formulate a positive-definite definition of entropy based on our ignorance of the underlying state structure after repeated measurements of cumulants. This new definition is a parallel to the Gibbs entropy formulation, but it can also be used in out-of-equilibrium regimes. Some important properties of this entropy are discussed. In addition we derive some information theory quantities such as relative entropy, conditional entropy, mutual information and R\'enyi entropy. We then compare the results with Wehrl entropy for the 1D harmonic oscillator, for pure and mixed states. We conclude the the work discussing potential applications of this new formalism, ranging from quantum correlations beyond entanglement to thermalization in closed quantum systems.

title: Coherent control of quadrupolar order in solid spin-1 systems:\ majorization bounds, orientation-indexed adiabatic inversion, and order lifetime
abstract: Tensor polarization $\Pzz=1-3p_0$ of spin-1 nuclei in dynamically polarized solid targets is limited, under a single spin temperature, to $\Pzz^{\rm eq}=2-\sqrt{4-3P^2}$ ($\Pzz\simeq0.20$ at vector polarization $P=0.5$). Radio-frequency (rf) semi-saturation of one quadrupolar Pake-doublet branch, with and without slow sample rotation, has reached $\Pzz\simeq0.36$. Using the first-order quadrupole Hamiltonian, spin temperatures of the Zeeman and alignment (quadrupolar-order) reservoirs, and single-transition operators, we analyze these manipulations. Five results follow. (i) Under unital operations (rf pulses, rotation, saturation), $1-3\lambda_{\max}\le\Pzz\le1-3\lambda_{\min}$, where $\lambda_{\min,\max}$ are the smallest and largest initial populations. Saturation achieves at most half the available transfer; selective $\pi$ inversion reaches either bound ($\Pzz=-0.85,+0.65$ at $P=0.5$). (ii) In a powder, the two single-quantum transitions overlap except in the pedestal region. Adiabatic frequency sweeps confined there invert one transition per bond. Inverting each bond exactly once requires packing antipodal caps on the orientation sphere. The optimal single-axis arrangement has four stops at the magic angle $54.74\degree$ (cube body diagonals; 73\% coverage); six icosahedral axes give the global optimum (90\%). (iii) Rotation-induced Landau--Zener crossings of deuteron pairs are adiabatic at current rates and scramble the inversion pattern; transits must be fast for the strongest, geminal CD$_2$, pairs. (iv) A parity theorem determines the inverted bonds solely from the endpoints of continuous adiabatic passage: rf during rotation yields at most two caps, and a full turn none. (v) The enhanced state decays by dipolar flip-flops, with $T_{1Q}\le T_{1Z}/3$ and a duty-cycle break-even of $\simeq35$~min. Magic-angle spinning cannot replace this scheme.

title: Why Most Neutron Star Low-mass X-Ray Binaries Accrete Transiently: An Evolutionary Study of Transient and Persistent Phases
abstract: Abstract A neutron star (NS) low-mass X-ray binary (LMXB), in which an NS accretes matter from a low-mass donor star, is an ideal source for probing some fundamental aspects of physics and astronomy, such as strong gravity, superdense matter, and the accretion-ejection processes. However, to reliably achieve these goals, one must adequately understand NS LMXBs, including why some accrete persistently and others transiently. Focused models, such as those based on a thermal-viscous instability in the accretion disk, are considered to explain transient accretion. However, broader perspectives, including which LMXB parameter values and phases cause transients and why there are more transients than persistents, remain poorly understood. Here, our computation of the long-term evolution of NS LMXBs addresses these questions, providing insight into LMXB parameters and phases, naturally producing more transients than persistents, and being partially consistent with the known properties of observed sources. For example, we typically find a greater fraction of the persistent phase at lower orbital periods from the LMXB evolution computation, which is somewhat consistent with observations. However, a lack of full consistency calls for improving the aforementioned focused models, and our computations provide a new way to discriminate among these models.

title: Two-stage Cooling in the Protoplanetary Disk Governs the Chemical and Isotopic Signatures of Carbonaceous Chondrites
abstract: Abstract The thermodynamic evolution of the solar protoplanetary disk fundamentally governed the chemical makeup of accreting planetesimals. While the chondrule–matrix complementarity in carbonaceous chondrites has long been used to trace these processes, its origin—whether from a single closed reservoir or the mechanical mixing of independent components—remains highly debated. Here, we combine in situ chemical analyses of matrices across six major carbonaceous chondrite groups with high-precision silicon isotope data for paired chondrules and matrices to resolve this dichotomy. We demonstrate that moderately refractory elements (Mg/Si, δ 30 Si) strictly follow closed-system complementarity, whereas matrices are systematically depleted in moderately volatile elements (MVEs), necessitating open-system gas loss. Furthermore, the subequilibrium chondrule–matrix δ 30 Si offsets point to kinetically suppressed, nonequilibrium condensation rather than pure equilibrium gas–solid exchange. To unify these contradictory constraints, we propose a two-stage cooling model driven by transient heating events in dynamically confined dust-enriched disk regions. An initial rapid cooling stage drives kinetically controlled condensation, locking in the chemical and isotopic complementarity of refractories while accommodating localized alkali recondensation. A subsequent slower cooling stage retains MVEs in the gas, allowing disk turbulence to physically separate and strip away the volatile-rich gas prior to local accretion. This semiopen framework permits inherited dust to mix with locally formed condensates during late-stage cooling, producing a composite matrix reservoir that can reconcile local component-specific complementarity with bulk-scale binary mixing trends. This fractionation mechanism establishes a primordial chemical heterogeneity in the protoplanetary disk that might be further inherited by accreting planetesimals, shaping the bulk volatile depletion of terrestrial planets.

title: Kinematically Resolving the Fe K Complex in Her X-1: The Accretion Disk and Ionized Wind across X-Ray Eclipses
abstract: Abstract We present the XRISM/Resolve spectroscopy of Her X-1 across three X-ray eclipses observed in 2024 September, resolving its iron K complex through the ingress, mid-eclipse, and egress phases. The 5 eV high energy resolution of Resolve enabled us to disentangle and detect all the primary components of the iron K complex: neutral iron fluorescence (Fe K α and K β ) and highly ionized emission lines (Fe XXV He α and Fe XXVI Ly α ). The neutral Fe K α emission is not significantly detected during mid-eclipse, indicating a compact origin near the neutron star. At ingress and egress, the line centroid exhibits red- and blueshifts of ∼200 km s −1 after correcting for the systemic velocity and the neutron star’s orbital motion. This residual shift corresponds to Keplerian rotation at a characteristic radius of r disk ∼ 6.6 × 10 6 km, suggesting an association with the outer accretion disk. In contrast, the highly ionized Fe XXV He α and Fe XXVI Ly α lines remain visible during eclipses, indicating an extended origin. Photoionization modeling (SPEX pion model) yields log 10 ( ξ / erg cm s − 1 ) ∼ 3.4 and N H ∼ 3.1 × 10 22 cm −2 , consistent with the ionized disk wind of Her X-1. Flux-ratio diagnostics constrain the geometric inner boundary of the clumpy disk wind to R in = 3 − 2 + 5 × 1 0 10 cm (1 σ ), consistent with the Compton-heated thermal winds. The inferred mass outflow rate is M ̇ out ≈ 3.2 × 1 0 − 9 M ⊙ yr − 1 (half the supplied mass), consistent with absorption line measurements of the disk wind obtained out of eclipse.

For each phase interval, spectra from the three eclipses were co-added. Colored points represent the observed spectra and the solid lines indicate the best-fit models. Vertical dashed lines indicate the rest-frame energies of Fe K α \alpha (6.404, 6.391 keV), Fe XXV He α \alpha (6.700 keV), Fe XXVI Ly α \alpha (6.952, 6.973 keV), and Fe K β \beta (7.058 keV) lines. title: Characterization of CRYO ASIC for charge readout in the nEXO experiment
abstract: nEXO is a proposed next-generation experiment searching for the neutrinoless double beta decay of $^{136}$Xe using a tonne-scale liquid xenon (LXe) time projection chamber (TPC). To image the ionization signals from events in the liquid xenon, the detector will employ metallized fused-silica charge collection tiles instrumented with cryogenic application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), referred to as CRYO ASIC, which are designed to operate directly in LXe to minimize input capacitance and pick-up noise. Here we present the performance of the CRYO ASIC mounted on an auxiliary printed circuit board and evaluated both in a cryogenic environmental chamber and in a dedicated LXe test stand. We demonstrate that the ASICs achieve the desired performance at liquid xenon temperatures, showing a gain stability better than 0.2% over 24-hour operation and reliable in-situ calibration using an on-chip pulser. In the LXe test stand, we show that boiling caused by the chip heat dissipation can be mitigated by operating the system above ~0.1 MPa. The in-LXe noise measured agrees with simulation, which indicates it the $150~e^-$ design requirement can be satisfied. These results establish CRYO ASIC as a viable low-noise in-LXe charge readout solution for nEXO.
