title: Thermal $CP$ dynamics in a four-fermion model: mean-field and functional renormalization group analyses
abstract: We investigate a one-flavor four-fermion model with scalar, pseudoscalar, and mixed scalar-pseudoscalar interactions at finite temperature and vanishing chemical potential. Our analysis combines the mean-field approximation, which determines the equilibrium condensates, with the functional renormalization group (FRG), which describes the scale dependence of the interactions and the fermion mass phase. Within the mean-field approach, we find that, in the absence of explicit symmetry-breaking sources, the dominant interaction determines the direction of condensation. In particular, a pseudoscalar condensate spontaneously breaks the ordinary $P/CP$ symmetry and disappears through a continuous thermal phase transition. For regular high-temperature FRG trajectories, the dimensionless mixed coupling tends to zero in the infrared, while its dimensionful counterpart remains finite. Increasing temperature also suppresses the scale evolution of the fermion mass phase. Together, these results clarify the distinct roles of thermal fluctuations in suppressing spontaneous symmetry breaking and fermionic instabilities, without necessarily eliminating explicit symmetry breaking effects.

title: Production Effects and Final-state Interactions in $\pi_1 \to 3\pi$
abstract: We investigate the $\pi_1(1600)$ signal channel of $3\pi$ in the $J^{PC} = 1^{-+} \,[\pi\pi]_{1^{--}}\pi~P$-wave. This channel has recently been analyzed by the COMPASS collaboration using the ``freed-isobar" technique which provides direct experimental access to the lineshape modifications of the $P$-wave $\pi\pi$ sub-channel arising from both final state interactions and production processes such as the Deck mechanism. We motivate a unified formalism combining production effects and final state interactions using the Khuri-Treiman formalism, which is consistent with low-energy unitarity, analyticity, and crossing symmetry, seeded by an initial production amplitude. We demonstrate that the precise lineshape of the $\pi\pi$ mass spectrum can be used to determine the relative strength and complex phase of different production mechanisms contributing to the $3\pi$ final state. We conduct a global fit of the $\pi_1$ freed-isobar data set, yielding a multi-dimensional parameterization of the $\pi_1\to3\pi$ decay amplitude at COMPASS as a function of both decay and production variables. We identify the contributions from short-range production and the Deck mechanism and extract the total $3\pi$ invariant mass dependence which will be important for a future extraction of the $\pi_1$ pole position in the $\rho\pi$ channel.

title: Nuclear medium and final state interaction effects in $\eta$ production induced by $\nu_\mu(\bar\nu_\mu)$ at SBN and DUNE energies
abstract: We investigate nuclear-medium modification and final-state interaction in charged- and neutral-current $\nu_\mu(\bar{\nu}_\mu)$-induced $\eta$-meson production on $^{12}\mathrm{C}$ and $^{40}\mathrm{Ar}$. The nuclear medium is described within a local density approximation, incorporating in-medium modifications of the $N^*(1535)$ resonance, which is known to play the dominant role in $\eta$ production through its $N \eta$ decay channel. The subsequent propagation and absorption of the $\eta$ meson in the nucleus are simulated using a Monte Carlo approach. We find that nuclear-medium modifications and final state interaction lead to substantial suppression of the production cross section, highlighting the importance of nuclear effects in interpreting $\eta$ production data. Our results provide valuable theoretical input for the analysis of $\eta$-production at the ongoing SBND and MicroBooNE experiments and the forthcoming DUNE experiment.

title: Nuclear geometry under external magnetic field in the Skyrme-Maxwell model
abstract: We find static solutions of the U(1) gauged Skyrme-Maxwell model in a constant external magnetic field, for baryon numbers $B \leq 6$. The field acts as an isospin-breaking source, stretching the skyrmion along its direction, while its size grows and then shrinks as the induction increases. We obtain the energy minimizers with a GPU implementation of the arrested Newton flow (ANF) algorithm. Gauged skyrmions have less energy and are more strongly bound than their ungauged counterpart. At weak magnetic field, the solutions are small deformations of the ungauged skyrmions, including regions of negative baryon density in sectors $B = 3, 5, 6$. For intermediate field, novel geometries appear, notably a $(B-1)$-toroidal chain. High field values lead to axially symmetric toroidal structures for all $B$.

title: Pellet induced transition from low to high confinement in separatrix phase spaces of ASDEX Upgrade
abstract: Abstract The Separatrix Operational Space (SepOS) concept (Eich and Manz 2021 Nucl. Fusion 61 086017) describes the operational space of tokamaks with respect to MHD, density limits and the L-H transition in terms of density and temperature at the separatrix. It has been inspired by the phase space developed by Rogers et al (1998 Phys. Rev. Lett. 81 4396) Rogers, Drake, and Zeiler (RDZ). Their idea was contested by pellet-induced L-H transitions (Gohil et al 2001 Phys. Rev. Lett. 86 644) evaluated inside the pedestal and subsequently this theory was widely dismissed. Whether the SepOS concept face similar challenges when applied to a pellet-induced L-H transition is studied. On the low-density branch of the L-H transition, the separatrix density is temporarily increased by pellet injection, thereby lowering the L-H power threshold in agreement with the SepOS model. The results will also be discussed in RDZ’s phase space. We conclude that the basic idea of the plasma edge phase space proposed by RDZ, more precisely that an increase in plasma beta at low collisionalities has a beneficial effect on confinement and at high collisionalities has a detrimental effect on confinement, was discarded unjustly.

title: Integrated simulation and instability analysis of drift wave turbulence for the hot ion mode on HL-3 tokamak
abstract: Abstract A hot ion mode with T i (0) > 10 keV, T i (0)/T e (0) ≈ 2.4, and fusion triple product 0.65 × 10 20 m −3 · keV · s has been achieved on HL-3. Integrated OMFIT modeling across three time slices (pre-H-mode, H-mode, L-mode) reproduces experimental profiles and reveals two distinguishing physics features. First, the ITB foot extends beyond qmin, in contrast to conventional strong reversed shear regimes where the barrier is confined within qmin, here it is sustained by the strong E × B flow shear, the decisive stabilization mechanism. Second, the complete H–L back transition exhibits pronounced ITB hysteresis: the edge transport barrier collapses while the core ITB persists with only 4% width reduction and 3.6% stored energy loss, indicating strong core-edge decoupling. Toroidal rotation dominates the radial electric field (∼−120 kV/m in H-mode, exceeding the diamagnetic term by a factor of 3–6), with its peak aligned with the ITB mid-radius. Within the ITB, E × B shear surpasses the ITG growth rate, suppressing ion transport to near neoclassical levels; at the foot (ρ ≈ 0.6) an ITG to ETG transition occurs near k y ρ s ≈ 1. A T i /T e scan confirms the radial contrast and opposite growth rate scalings. These results establish a validated simulation platform for the HL-3 hot ion mode and support the planned deuterium–tritium campaign.

title: Impact of energetic alpha particles on core turbulence in an ARC-class fusion power plant
abstract: Abstract In this work, we investigate the impact of fusion-born alpha particles on core turbulence and transport in the ARC tokamak fusion power plant (Hillesheim et al 2026 J. Plasma Phys. 92 E69) using linear and nonlinear gyrokinetic CGYRO (Candy et al J. Comput. Phys. 324 73–93) simulations. A significant reduction in ion-scale turbulent heat and particle fluxes is observed in the inner core ( r / a ⩽ 0.5), which is associated with multiscale interactions between fast ion-destabilized modes, zonal flows, and the background turbulence. A nonlinear upshift in the ITG critical gradient is observed in the simulations with fast alphas compared to those with artificially thermalized alphas. The turbulence reduction is found to scale beneficially with alpha particle density and plasma β e , and the radial extent of the turbulence suppression is limited to the volume containing a significant density of fast particles. The suitability of local gyrokinetics and potential impacts of fast ion effects on fusion performance are discussed.

title: High Precision Fundamental Physics Experiments at JLab with Spin-transparent Storage Rings of Low-energy Polarized Electron Beams
abstract: A breakthrough in fundamental physics experiments measuring particle spin precession may happen if spin-transparent storage rings become adopted tools for such experiments. We present a new design of highly specialized table-sized storage rings, which use low-energy polarized electron beams and Mott polarimetry. Based on the spin transparency ansatz, the spin precession stemming from the magnetic dipole moment is canceled at any beam energy after an electron's turn along the periodic orbit in the ring. Meanwhile, a spin precession induced by the fundamental physics of interest, e.g., the electron's permanent electric dipole moment (EDM) and/or ultralight-dark-matter-mediated forces such as axions, will accumulate. However, capitalizing on such types of rings is not only desirable for measurements of EDMs and axion searches relevant to $CP$ violation and matter-antimatter asymmetry in the Universe, but may also find very promising applications in quantum computing.

title: DLS-Extended: a reduced model to assess the impact of impurity radiation location on optimal magnetic geometry choices for the STEP divertor
abstract: Abstract Alternative Divertor Configurations (ADCs) often make use of high total flux expansion ( f R ) and connection length ( L ∥ ) to improve the access to and the controllability of detachment, a regime vitally important for reactor-class tokamaks such as the Spherical Tokamak for Energy Production (STEP). Achieving detachment on such high-power devices is enabled through radiation from seeded impurity species such as argon and neon, which can lead to radiative losses throughout the flux tube, altering the impact of magnetic geometry on detachment. The detachment location sensitivity (DLS) model analytically predicts detachment access and sensitivity based on upstream conditions, the magnetic geometry and seeded impurity radiation. It assumes the radiation region to have no spatial extent. In this work, we relax this assumption and introduce DLS-Extended, a new reduced 1D model which can capture the effects of the spatial distribution of impurity radiation along the field line. The prediction of radiation extent was verified against SOLPS-ITER simulations of an initial STEP design with a good match. DLS-Extended predicts that the radiation extent found in STEP weakens the detachment access benefit of f R and strengthens the benefit of L ∥ , while the detachment stability of the inner and outer legs is increased and decreased, respectively. This is due to a number of novel radiation-driven effects and has implications for the optimum strike point position in reactor-scale devices. These findings highlight the need for more experimental studies in the presence of broad-radiating impurities. DLS-Extended is distributed under the LGPL-3 open source license and is publicly available on GitHub.

title: Development of a versatile modular system to study the ablation and plume expansion in a thin film
abstract: Time-resolved investigation of laser ablation of thin films requires stable, repeatable, and efficient experimental environment. Conventional approaches often rely on multiple laser-ablation shots acquired at different delay times to reconstruct the temporal evolution of the process, thereby assuming shot-to-shot reproducibility. This work presents a novel modular experimental setup that addresses these challenges and enables a systematic pump--probe study of laser--matter interaction. The setup provides reliable single-pulse measurements with controlled sample positioning inside the high vacuum chamber, as well as integrated data recording, which improves redundancy and ease with which experiments can be performed. Further, the setup serves as an advanced diagnostic tool for investigating the time evolution of laser--matter interactions, ablation dynamics and laser-produced plasmas in a single laser shot, in various configurations with a temporal resolution better than 15 ns. Using this capability, we show that for a fixed ablation geometry, the transient reflectivity and transmission response depends strongly on the probing side, indicating that probing direction is an independent diagnostic variable whose omission can lead to incomplete or misleading picture of the ablation dynamics. This experimental technique can advance the understanding of surface modification and plume expansion, which are relevant to fundamental studies and also for range of applications, including laser cleaning of tokamak viewports and mirrors, pulsed laser deposition (PLD), surface structuring and laser-induced forward transfer (LIFT), among others. The present setup is versatile enough to perform these studies under different ablation configurations without implementing major changes in the experimental configuration.

title: Chromoelectric and chromomagnetic quarkonium couplings to scalar and spin-two nucleon structure
abstract: The chromoelectric and chromomagnetic polarizabilities of compact heavy quarkonium weight the scalar and spin-two structure of the nucleon differently. We derive the corresponding finite-momentum-transfer elastic response kernels, retaining the physical quarkonium velocity and nucleon spin dependence. Their correlated uncertainties are determined using lattice quark and gluon gravitational form factors. For $\Upsilon(1S)N$ at $100\,\mathrm{MeV}$ above threshold and $Q^2=0.20\,\mathrm{GeV}^2$, the electric non-spin-flip kernel is $1.316\pm0.100_{\rm GFF}\,\mathrm{GeV}$. The electric and magnetic kernels exhibit distinct momentum-transfer and spin dependence. These kernels describe the nucleon response to the local operators. Their contributions to elastic scattering are weighted by the independent quarkonium polarizabilities.

title: SiPM optical readout of a PICOSEC Micromegas precise timing detector
abstract: By combining a Cherenkov radiator with a semi-transparent photocathode and a two-stage Micromegas amplification element, PICOSEC Micromegas detectors have achieved <20 ps charged-particle time resolution with electronic readout of induced signals. Building upon this performance, we describe SiPM-based optical readout as a novel technique for PICOSEC Micromegas detectors. Single-channel detector prototypes based on glass Micromegas technology were read out with an array of SiPMs. To allow operation in a strongly quenched gas mixture, a solid wavelength shifter is integrated in the glass Micromegas to convert UV scintillation to the visible range and maximise scintillation light output. Timing performance of glass Micromegas in electronic and optical readout modes is compared and <150 ps time resolution is achieved by optically read out scintillation light signals. The achievable spatial resolution from centre-of-gravity reconstruction of event positions from the amplitudes of signals on multiple SiPM channels is {\sigma} = 1.25 mm. This demonstrates the possibility of dual-readout of PICOSEC glass Micromegas: electronic signals and optical signals. Finally, camera-based optical readout is presented to demonstrate imaging as another avenue for position reconstruction.

title: Renormalization-group flow of nucleon--$\Delta$ contact interactions with an explicit $\Delta$: decoupling and the scale dependence of large-$N_c$ relations
abstract: We study the leading-order (LO) contact interactions among nucleons and $\Delta$ isobars under a Wilsonian renormalization-group flow with a sharp momentum cutoff, keeping the $\Delta$ as an explicit coupled channel, and determine which large-$N_c$ relations among the couplings are invariant under the flow. The two-channel flow with the $\Delta\Delta$ threshold inside the cutoff range is solved exactly, and the closed channels decouple with relative corrections of order $\Lambda^2/\kappa_{\Delta\Delta}^2$, where $\kappa_{\Delta\Delta}=\sqrt{2M_\Delta(M_\Delta-M_N)}$ is the closed-channel momentum. Applying the $1/N_c$ expansion of the Hartree Hamiltonian to the $N$--$\Delta$ system, we find that a generalized time reversal removes all corrections of relative order $1/N_c$, that the LO fixes eleven of the 18 S-wave couplings in terms of seven, and that the exact-SU(4) two-parameter form used in the literature differs from the LO by an operator of relative order $1/N_c^2$ with matrix elements of order one in the $\Delta$ channels. The eight spin--isospin flip relations are exact invariants of the flow, also when the central part of one-pion exchange is iterated in the S waves. The eigenchannel relations of the $NN$--$\Delta\Delta$ sectors hold only at the scale at which they are imposed. Their running is controlled by $\kappa_{\Delta\Delta}$, which is of order $N_c^0$, and by a parameter that the $NN$ data do not fix, so that the $1/N_c$ expansion does not remove it. Large-$N_c$ relations between open and closed channels therefore constrain the potential at one scale. The flip relation between the $(S,I)=(3,0)$ and $(0,3)$ channels of $\Delta\Delta$ scattering predicts equal scattering lengths at LO, which lattice QCD at heavy pion masses can test.

title: Reconstructing High-Fidelity Light Yield Maps for Surface LArTPCs Using Crossing Cosmic Muons
abstract: Photon detection systems in liquid argon time projection chambers provide prompt scintillation light information that can improve triggering, timing, calorimetry, and interaction reconstruction. These applications require an understanding of the spatial dependence of the detected light yield (LY), which is not adequately described by a single detector-wide average. We present a method for reconstructing voxelized 3D light yield maps in surface LArTPCs using crossing cosmic muons. For each selected muon, the path length through every crossed voxel is converted to deposited energy using a minimum ionizing particle approximation, producing a linear system relating the unknown voxel light yields to the total detected photon signal. The resulting inverse problem is solved using nonnegative least squares, with an additional $L_2$ smoothness penalty used to stabilize weakly constrained voxel values. The method is studied in simulation using the ProtoDUNE-VD detector geometry and photon detection system. Reconstructed maps recover the dominant spatial structure of a visibility-based truth reference and respond as expected to changes in the photon detector configuration. Smoothness regularization reduces zero-valued voxels and localized fluctuations while leaving the detector-average light yield approximately unchanged at the selected regularization strengths. The voxel-wise RMSE relative to the truth reference is reduced by approximately 44% for the regularized reconstruction.

title: Optical characterization of microcellular PET and crystallized PEN reflectors in liquid argon for LEGEND-1000
abstract: Efficient collection of liquid argon (LAr) scintillation light is essential for background rejection in the LEGEND experiment. We investigate microcellular polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and crystallized polyethylene naphthalate (PEN) as candidate reflector materials for LEGEND-1000. Their optical responses to 450 nm light and 128 nm LAr scintillation are measured in LAr and complemented by room-temperature reflectance measurements in air. Under scintillation illumination, PET coupled to a PEN foil and crystallized PEN increase the detected photoelectron yield by factors of $2.36\pm0.11$ and $1.75\pm0.10$, respectively, relative to a black-metal-velvet reference. A Geant4-based optical model yields reflectivity estimates at $450~\mathrm{nm}$ in LAr of $(90\pm4)\%$ for PET and $(81\pm5)\%$ for crystallized PEN, compared with $(80\pm5)\%$ for the Tetratex reference. These results motivate further investigation of both materials for LAr instrumentation, including their radiopurity, long-term cryogenic stability, and performance under matched detector conditions.

title: Optical characterization and ionizing-radiation response of the BCF-20XL scintillating fiber
abstract: We report optical characterization and ionizing-radiation measurements of the BCF-20XL scintillating fiber from Luxium Solutions, which also wavelength-shifts externally incident blue light (referred to here as Sci-WLS). Attenuation lengths were obtained from transmitted emission spectra using a 3.0 m fiber with a spectrophotometer and described with a two-component attenuation model, yielding a long attenuation length of 6.70 m and a short attenuation length of 0.16 m. The spectral measurements also reveal wavelength-dependent attenuation, with the long component increasing with wavelength and the short component becoming less significant at longer wavelengths. The scintillation response was also characterized under radioactive alpha, beta, and gamma irradiation using SiPM-based readout, providing a benchmark of the detected photoelectron response of BCF-20XL.

title: Nucleon sigma terms in lattice QCD at physical pion mass and in the continuum
abstract: We determine the light, strange and charm $\sigma$-terms of the nucleon in lattice QCD using four $N_f=2+1+1$ twisted-mass gauge ensembles simulated at physical pion masses and with approximately the same spatial volumes. The four lattice spacings ranging from $0.080$ fm to $0.049$ fm, with an action that has O(a) improvement, enable extrapolating the results to the continuum limit. Both valence and sea quark contributions are analysed accounting for excited-state contamination from low-lying multihadron states. We perform global fits to all ensembles, that yield $\sigma_{\pi N}=53.0(7.4)(1.6)$ MeV, $\sigma_s=58.2(17.0)(2.1)$ MeV and $\sigma_c=112(28)(25)$ MeV, with statistical and systematic uncertainties, respectively.

title: Investigation of the timing performance of double-sided $p$-type 3D silicon sensors produced by CNM
abstract: We investigate the timing performance and spatial uniformity of double-sided $p$-type 3D silicon sensors produced by the Centro Nacional de Microelectr\'onica (CNM). Three sensor layouts are studied: hexagonal and square geometries with an inter-electrode spacing of \SI{30}{\micro\meter}, and a hexagonal geometry with an inter-electrode spacing of \SI{50}{\micro\meter}. The sensors are characterized using a \SI{1064}{\nano\meter} infrared laser and a custom two-stage wide-band readout. Measurements with a $^{90}$Sr source are used to establish a minimum-ionizing-particle-like reference for the laser signal. The timing resolution improves with increasing bias voltage for all three layouts. Two-dimensional laser scans are used to study the position dependence of the timing response and to quantify its uniformity. Among the investigated devices, the square \SI{30}{\micro\meter} geometry shows the best overall timing performance at the highest measured bias voltage.

title: Development of a Long-Term Stable Three-Axis Single-Beam Vector Optically Pumped Magnetometer Using a Buffer-Gas-Free Rubidium Vapor Cell and Direct Absorption Frequency Locking for Unshielded Geomagnetic Monitoring
abstract: Optically pumped magnetometers (OPMs) achieve ultra-high sensitivity, yet sustaining long-term stability in unshielded, dynamic geomagnetic environments remains challenging. Here, we present the design and unshielded validation of a three-axis vector OPM achieving sub-nanotesla accuracy using an off-the-shelf rubidium (Rb) ampoule and a vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL). Unlike conventional sensors, this system operates without high-pressure buffer gases, mitigating wall-collision relaxation via a single-beam geometry combined with active zero-field nulling and adiabatic 70 kHz AC heating. To suppress VCSEL thermal wavelength drift without sub-Doppler optics, active frequency stabilization based on direct absorption spectroscopy (DAS) was implemented across a wide capture range. Continuous evaluation in an unshielded laboratory in Okayama against synthetic geomagnetic records from the Kakioka and Kanoya observatories demonstrated exceptional horizontal tracking fidelity. Concurrently, the vertical transfer matrix resolved the regional geomagnetic coast effect, extracting Parkinson induction vectors reflecting regional conductivity contrast, with high robustness against DC electric railway interference. Spectral characterization showed an intrinsic white noise floor of 10-20 pT above 1 Hz, enhanced by digital oversampling beyond the 12-bit DAC quantization limit, while residual overlapped Allan deviation revealed a 0.1 nT bias instability at 100-200 s integration times. These results prove that a compact, low-cost OPM platform based on commercial components can suppress long-term drift and serve as a reliable instrument for geophysical surveys and unshielded magnetic sensing.

title: Characterization of BNLs 20 and 30 micrometer thick LGADs for the Electron Ion Collider
abstract: The 20 and 30 micrometer thick Low-Gain Avalanche Detectors (LGADs) produced at Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL) were evaluated. Detailed electrical measurements indicate well-formed and stable gain layers with consistently low leakage currents. Transient Current Technique (TCT) was used to evaluate the gain. Fast-laser timing studies demonstrate time resolutions at the level of a few tens of picoseconds. To assess operational longevity under realistic conditions for Electron-Ion Collider sub-detector systems, devices were irradiated with 30 MeV and 60 MeV protons to fluences of 10^13 to 10^14 neq/cm^2, enabling a focused study of radiation-induced effects on gain stability and timing performance.

title: Angle-Resolved Reflectance Measurements in the Vacuum Ultraviolet for Metallic Samples
abstract: The light yield of noble-element scintillation detectors depends strongly on the reflective properties of detector materials in the vacuum ultraviolet (VUV), where optical measurements are scarce. For this reason, we built a custom rotary setup at IFIC, equipped with a monochromator and operated in a gaseous argon atmosphere, to perform angle-resolved reflectance measurements in the specular reflection plane. We describe the setup and its extensive characterization, together with the procedure used to measure the bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) of materials at various angles of incidence, for wavelengths from 128 to 500 nm, covering both the argon (128 nm) and xenon (175 nm) scintillation wavelengths. To illustrate the capabilities of the setup, we present results for rough aluminum and stainless-steel surfaces as reference materials. Fitting the measured angular profiles with the analytical GGX microfacet model allows us to extract the real and imaginary parts of the refractive index and the surface roughness parameter of each sample. These parameters are then used to extrapolate the in-plane measurements to the full hemisphere and from gaseous argon to liquid media, enabling the inference of the hemispherical reflectance in gaseous argon, liquid argon and liquid xenon.

title: Will a supernova explode in CD-30°11223?
abstract: Context. Accretion of He-rich matter onto a low-mass carbon-oxygen white dwarf in a binary system with a He-rich donor may lead to an explosive event at the level of a type Ia supernova (SN Ia), albeit with a low peak luminosity and peculiar nucleosynthesis. Recently, the possibility of this occurring in the context of certain binaries with He-accreting white dwarfs has been questioned, with the suggestion that if the effects of rotation are accounted for in the evolution of the accretor, the latter would not explode. It could instead become a white dwarf with a massive He-buffer. Aims. We investigate the expected evolution of the currently detached binary CD-30°11223 harboring a 0.74 M ⊙ carbon-oxygen white dwarf and a 0.47 M ⊙ donor with a He-burning core and a very thin H-envelope (Δ M H = 6 × 10 −4 M ⊙ ). Methods. We used the stellar evolution code FuNS to compute the evolution of CD-30°11223 up to the epoch when the two components come into contact and through the RLOF phase of the donor. With respect to our earlier study of the system PTF J2238+743015.1, we also included the transport of angular momentum due to magnetic instabilities in the accretor interiors (‘magnetic model’). Results. During the H-accretion phase, the effects of rotation in the accretor are negligible. In the ‘magnetic model’, the angular momentum deposited by the accreted matter is very efficiently redistributed along the whole WD due to magnetic instabilities, so that the angular velocity of the accreted layers remains very low. During the He-accretion phase, the accretor experiences two very strong He-flashes, which result in the ejection from the binary system of a large part of the matter previously accreted. The system ends its life as a carbon-oxygen core capped by a massive He/C/O-envelope (Δ M env ≃ 0.194 M ⊙ ) and an extremely low-mass companion that is remnant of the donor, as in the ‘rotating model’ not including the effects of magnetic field. Rotating model is the label we adopt to design our model computed including the effects of rotation-induced instabilities but neglecting the effects of magnetic field. Conclusions. The system CD-30°11223 cannot be regarded as the potential progenitor of an SN Ia. This conclusion is equally applicable to all detached binary systems having similar component masses and orbital periods.

title: Pulse profile modelling of accreting millisecond pulsars with disc occultation and its impact on parameter inference
abstract: Abstract Pulse profile modelling is a relativistic ray-tracing technique used to infer neutron star mass, radius, and surface hotspot properties from X-ray pulsations. Pulse profile modelling has been widely applied to rotation-powered millisecond pulsars, where the local environment is relatively empty. Application to accreting millisecond pulsars is complicated by the geometry of the local accretion flow, including disc occultation of surface emission. In this work, we extend an established pulse profile modelling code, X-PSI, to incorporate accretion disc occultation in accreting millisecond pulsar pulse profile modelling. We quantify how disc occultation depends on system geometry and evaluate its impact on parameter inference. We find that disc occultation is primarily governed by the viewing inclination and can significantly reshape pulse profiles at moderate to high inclinations. Using synthetic Neutron Star Interior Composition Explorer datasets, we investigate parameter recovery for two representative hotspot configurations. For hotspots close to the rotational poles, statistically acceptable fits can yield posteriors that deviate noticeably from the true parameters. In contrast, in a case with hotspots located closer to the equator we find more reliable parameter recovery. We further find that neglecting disc occultation can introduce spurious posterior modes with comparable statistical support, potentially affecting the interpretation of inferred neutron star parameters, suggesting that this effect should be included in accreting millisecond pulsar pulse profile modelling.
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

title: Non-monotonic oxygen ion escape during the transition from an induced to an intrinsic Martian magnetosphere
abstract: Understanding the evolution of the global dipole magnetic field on ancient Mars is critical for reconstructing its paleo-environment. However, the effectiveness of this intrinsic dipole field in protecting the atmosphere and the relationship between magnetic shielding and ion escape rates remain subjects of debate. In this study, we utilize a three-dimensional multi-fluid magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) model incorporating the Hall effect, with equatorial dipole field strengths ranging from 0 to 120 nT, to simulate the transition from an induced to an intrinsic magnetosphere. To understand the underlying ion escape mechanisms, we conduct an in-depth analysis of the variations in the driving electric fields (convection, Hall, and ambipolar) and evaluate the trans-terminator and radial O^+ fluxes across different altitudes and solar zenith angle ranges. Our results reveal that as the dipole field strengthens, the increased magnetic pressure significantly extends the magnetopause standoff distance. This effectively displaces the driving electric fields away from heavy-ion-rich regions, which significantly suppresses and spatially deflects the dayside plume escape channel at lower altitudes. Notably, despite this localized shielding, the total O^+ escape rate exhibits a distinct non-monotonic trend, reaching a pronounced global peak at an intermediate magnetization state of approximately 45-60 nT. By evaluating the trans-terminator and radial fluxes, we suggest that this peak reflects a dynamic competition between the progressive suppression of the dayside plume channel and the enhanced redistribution of O^+ toward the nightside and tailward escape channel under the reconfigured magnetic topology. This finding demonstrates that the ancient Martian magnetic field does not strictly follow a "stronger field equals better protection" paradigm, offering new insights into how planetary magnetic field evolution controls heavy-ion loss.

title: IViS: Interferometric Visibility-domain inversion Software
abstract: Wide-field spectral-line imaging with modern radio interferometers remains challenging when the emission is extended, multiscale, and distributed over many overlapping pointings. In this regime, accurate reconstruction requires a joint treatment of the calibrated visibilities, control of image-domain regularity, and, when necessary, recovery of missing short spacings from single-dish data. We present IViS (Interferometric Visibility-domain Inversion Software), a GPU-accelerated Python framework for visibility-domain joint deconvolution, and assess its performance for wide-field H I imaging with the Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP). The current model, Classic3D , reconstructs a nonparametric sky cube directly from calibrated visibilities by minimizing a regularized least-squares criterion. The forward model relies on a nonuniform fast Fourier transform (NUFFT), supports joint deconvolution across all mosaic pointings, and allows positivity constraints through bounded optimization. Short-spacing information can be incorporated through a fusion term that models single-dish data from the same sky estimate. We validate the method using synthetic point-source, noise-only, and multiscale diffuse-emission simulations, and apply it to ASKAP full-survey observations toward the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC). The simulations show that IViS recovers point-source flux accurately in the absence of regularization and that the regularization strength sets the trade-off between noise suppression and effective resolution. Relative to linear mosaicking of independently deconvolved pointings, joint deconvolution can recover more large-scale power. When single-dish information is included, the reconstructed power spectra closely reproduce the input sky statistics over a broad range of spatial frequencies. Applied to ASKAP data, IViS yields 10 h mosaics with an effective resolution of 22″ of Galactic foreground emission and LMC emission with reduced residual side-lobe structure and realistic multiscale morphology. A comparison with ASKAPSoft using multiscale CLEAN shows that, for this specific target and a single observing block, Classic3D exhibits fewer residual side-lobes and recovers substantially more power at low spatial frequencies. IViS provides a flexible visibility-domain framework for joint deconvolution of large spectral-line mosaics, and illustrates the potential of regularized inverse-problem approaches as an alternative to traditional CLEAN-based imaging for next-generation radio surveys.

title: A bright X-ray flaring event from the intermediate supergiant fast X-ray transient IGR J00370+6122 observed with NuSTAR
abstract: We present an analysis of a long NuSTAR observation of the intermediate supergiant fast X-ray transient (SFXT) IGR J00370+6122, obtained around the peak of its orbital modulation. The observation has a net exposure ∼93 ks. During the observation, the source displayed a bright flaring event that was resolved into numerous short flares with durations of 10 − 10 3 s. The 3 − 70 keV luminosity spanned a dynamic range of ∼200, from ∼10 34 to ∼1.8 × 10 36 erg s −1 ; the maximum was reached for only ∼40 s in total. The spectrum is well described by an absorbed double-Comptonisation model, with parameters consistent with those found in other X-ray pulsars accreting at similarly low luminosities. This is the first detection of a double-hump continuum in IGR J00370+6122, which extends this spectral state to the class of intermediate SFXTs. We searched for the previously reported ∼346 s and ∼674 s periodicities and find no significant signal at either period, which makes their interpretation as the neutron star spin period less likely. Using ∼21 yr of Swift /BAT monitoring, we refine the orbital period of the system to P orb = 15.6654 ± 0.0008 d. Finally, we discuss the observed flaring activity in the framework of quasi-spherical settling accretion, which is expected at the observed luminosities.

title: Comparative evaluation of future collider options
abstract: In anticipation of the completion of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC) programme by the end of 2041, CERN is preparing to launch a new major facility in the mid-2040s. According to the 2020 update of the European Strategy for Particle Physics (ESPP), the highest-priority next collider is an electron-positron Higgs factory, followed in the longer term by a hadron-hadron collider at the highest achievable energy. The CERN directorate established a Future Colliders Comparative Evaluation working group in June 2023. This group brings together project leaders and domain experts to conduct a consistent evaluation of the Future Circular Collider (FCC) and alternative scenarios based on shared assumptions and standardized criteria. This report presents a comparative evaluation of proposed future collider projects submitted as input for the Update of the European Strategy for Particle Physics. These proposals are compared considering main performance parameters, environmental impact and sustainability, technical maturity, cost of construction and operation, required human resources, and realistic implementation timelines. An overview of the international collider projects within a similar timeframe, notably the CEPC in China and the ILC in Japan is also presented, as well as a short review of the status and prospects of new accelerator techniques.
journal_ref: Comparative evaluation of future collider options, Future Colliders Comparative Evaluation Working Group. CERN Yellow Reports: Monographs, CERN-2025-011 (CERN, Geneva, 2025)

title: A non-perturbative framework for ion stopping in partially ionized warm dense matter with a physics-informed neural-network solver
abstract: Abstract Ion energy deposition in dense plasmas is of central importance to ion-beam-driven inertial confinement fusion and high-energy-density physics. In the Bragg-peak regime, the stopping power governs the spatial distribution of deposited energy and therefore strongly affects the formation of warm dense states and the efficiency of ion fast ignition. In this regime, the projectile velocity becomes comparable to the characteristic velocity of target electrons, and the beam–plasma interaction may enter a nonlinear, non-perturbative scattering regime in which Born-based perturbative treatments are no longer adequate. For partially ionized warm dense matter, additional complexity arises from charge-state distributions, bound-electron response and dynamic screening. Here, we develop a physically constrained, self-consistent non-perturbative framework for ion stopping in warm dense matter. The approach combines formal quantum-scattering relations, a charge-state-resolved collisional–radiative model and multiscale effective interaction potentials. In the strong-scattering regime, non-perturbative phase shifts are obtained from the Calogero equation using a variable-phase physics-informed neural-network solver, while the Born limit is recovered naturally in the weak-coupling asymptotic regime. This provides a unified description in which deviations from perturbative stopping can be quantified and the onset of perturbative breakdown can be identified. The framework is validated against time-resolved proton energy-loss measurements in a hydrogen discharge plasma and against FCDF benchmarks in the classical and strongly degenerate limits. For partially ionized warm dense carbon, the calculated stopping power remains close to TD-KS-DFT and TD-OF-DFT reference data, while conventional phenomenological and average-atom models tend to overestimate the Bragg-peak region. These results indicate that higher-order phase-shift corrections are essential in the strongly coupled regime and that the present framework provides a consistent non-perturbative description of ion energy loss in partially ionized warm dense plasmas.

title: Probing Majoron Dark Matter with Gravitational Wave Detectors
abstract: Abstract The Majoron is a hypothetical (pseudo) Nambu-Goldstone boson arising from the spontaneous breaking of a global lepton number symmetry, and is known as a candidate for dark matter in our Universe. In this paper, we investigate the possibility of probing the Majoron dark matter with a linear optical cavity used in the interferometric gravitational wave detectors. We consider a scenario in which the Majoron dark matter couples to photons through a QED anomaly, leading to an oscillatory photon birefringence induced by the coherent dark matter background. The anomaly coefficient is fixed by requiring the model to simultaneously reproduce the electroweak Higgs scale and a typical right-handed Majorana neutrino mass scale, and the resulting dark matter-photon coupling naturally falls within the sensitivity range of optical interferometers. By incorporating additional optics to extract the birefringence signal, we find that ground-based laser interferometers such as Advanced LIGO, KAGRA, as well as future detectors, can probe a region of the parameter space of Majoron dark matter.

title: Triangular and fourth-order flow of D mesons in Pb-Pb collisions with event-by-event fluctuations
abstract: Charm quarks are valuable probes of the transport properties of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP), yet the role of event-by-event medium fluctuations in shaping their observables remains to be quantified. We study this problem in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02$~TeV by coupling the iEBE-VISHNU event-by-event viscous hydrodynamic framework to a Langevin transport model with instantaneous coalescence hadronization. We find that fluctuations have little effect on the azimuthally averaged $D$ meson nuclear modification factor $R_{AA}$, which remains close to the smooth-background baseline with only modest momentum-dependent deviations. In contrast, the anisotropic flow coefficients $v_n$ are increasingly sensitive to fluctuations with rising harmonic order $n$. In particular, the triangular flow $v_3$, which vanishes in the smooth background, is entirely generated by initial-state fluctuations, and our results reproduce the main features of the available CMS measurements. We further present predictions for the $D$ meson $v_4$, which provide a quantitative benchmark for future measurements of higher-order heavy-flavor flow and help elucidate the interplay between event-by-event QGP fluctuations and charm quark dynamics.

title: Correlations between $\ensuremath{\mit{\Upsilon}(n\text{S})}\xspace$ production and the underlying event in $\ensuremath{p\!p}\xspace$ collisions with the ATLAS detector
abstract: Recent studies from various experiments at the LHC and RHIC suggest that small collision systems exhibit quark-gluon plasma (QGP) like signatures that were typically observed in large systems. While QGP like signatures have been observed in the soft sector, strong constraints on possible partonic energy loss were established in the hard sector. At the same time, there are multiple pieces of evidence pointing to correlations between hard and soft particle production in proton-proton collisions. The correlations between hard and soft particle production in $pp$ collisions are studied in events with $\Upsilon$ mesons, which provide a valuable hard probe to study such effects. The multiplicity and distributions of kinematic variables of charged particles produced in association with an $\Upsilon$ meson are measured using 139 fb$^{-1}$ of data at $\ensuremath{\sqrt{s}}\xspace = 13$~TeV collected by the ATLAS experiment at the LHC. The measurement is performed separately for the first three $\Upsilon$(nS) states in intervals of their transverse momentum. At low transverse momentum, the associated charged-particle multiplicity is observed to be systematically lower in collisions where $\Upsilon$(2S) or $\Upsilon$(3S) is produced compared to $\Upsilon$(1S), with the difference decreasing as the $\Upsilon$ transverse momentum increases.
authors: Baidyanath Sahoo (On behalf of the ATLAS Collaboration)

title: Weinberg Angle, Neutron Abundance in BBN, and Lifetime
abstract: We present state of the art kinetic theory determination of the neutron abundance available for the Big-Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN). Our work is motivated by the study of the neutron lifespan measured in the laboratory and the unknown strength of weak interactions coupling constant $G_\mathrm{F}$ at finite temperature in the primordial Universe. We draw attention to the relevant dependence of $G_\mathrm{F}$ on the symmetry breaking Weinberg angle $s^2_\mathrm{W}$, a free parameter in the standard model of particle physics. We establish how the value of $s^2_\mathrm{W}$ by way of $G_\mathrm{F}$ modification influences neutron abundance available for BBN and neutron lifetime.

title: Two-Fluid Radial Stability of Dark-Matter-Admixed Compact Objects: Dark Compact Planets, Dark White Dwarfs, Dark Neutron Stars, and Dark Oysters
abstract: We investigate the equilibrium structure and stability against radial oscillations of a variety of two-fluid compact objects containing ordinary baryonic matter admixed with cold dark matter coupled through the background spacetime. For the ordinary fluid, we employ a QCD equation of state compatible with chiral effective field theory at nuclear densities (supplemented by the BPS and Negele-Vautherin models at extremely low densities) and with perturbative QCD in the high-density regime while also satisfying also current astrophysical data. For the dark fluid, we assume self-interacting fermionic matter with particle masses of $m_f=$ 2, 5, 10, and 100 GeV and two self-interaction strengths of $y=0.1$ and $10^3$. By scanning a large range of central pressures for both fluids, we identify the presence of dark compact planets, dark white dwarfs, dark neutron stars and the so-called dark oysters. Importantly, these objects are not only in two-fluid hydrostatic equilibrium, but they are also stable against two-fluid radial oscillations. We find that the relative representation of each class in the radially stable sample is strongly sensitive to the combinations of $m_f$ and $y$, with some combinations entirely suppressing some of these object classes within the sampled domain while favoring others. In addition to these classes, strong self-repulsion supports stable, dark-matter-dominated branches with compact ordinary-matter cores and extended dark halos, approaching the self-interacting fermion-star limit. Finally, we calculate the gravitational redshift at the ordinary-matter surface, $z_{\rm OM}$, including the contribution of extended dark-matter halos for which we found radially stable configurations with $z_{\rm OM}>2$.

title: Renormalized dynamical tidal response of neutron stars in binary dynamics
abstract: We present the relativistic dynamical tidal response of a neutron star computed using stellar perturbation theory and matched to a worldline effective field theory via the tidal scattering phase. This phase is defined as the difference between the Compton/Raman scattering phase of gravitational-waves from a neutron star and the real part of the black hole scattering phase. The gravitational corrections to the response function are obtained using self-energy corrections up to fourth post-Minkowskian order. The response function for neutron stars obeying the BSk22 equation-of-state from Brussels-Skyrme family, is then consistently matched to an effective theory of relativistic quadrupolar harmonic oscillators to model the fundamental-mode ($f$-mode) and low-frequency gravity-modes ($g$-modes). This matching includes the frequency and tidal coupling of each mode and the post-adiabatic dynamical tidal Love number, and once matched this model is in excellent agreement with the full neutron star response. With the external tidal field up to third post-Newtonian order, we also analyse the tidal coupling of the induced quadrupole on the neutron star in a circular binary system, and the adiabatic binding energy.

title: Implementation of a five-wave approximate Riemann solver for general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics in AthenaK
abstract: We present an implementation of an HLLD approximate Riemann solver for the AthenaK astrophysics code with support for full general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics via a tetrad frame transformation. Our implementation uses an initial guess for the HLLD iterative solve which eliminates the need for an additional conserved-to-primitive inversion, which greatly accelerates performance without affecting accuracy. Additionally, by coupling the method with a first-order flux correction, we are able to use the method reliably even when the magnetization exceeds $10^4$, which we achieve in a SANE accretion disk. Our SANE disk shows that HLLD leads to a more strongly magnetized funnel and more accurate horizon fluxes when compared with HLLE. We further apply the new HLLD implementation to an equal-mass binary neutron star merger. For our long-lived remnant, HLLD enhances the magnetic shear stresses in the outer layers and leads to weaker differential rotation. However, due to weaker gravitational wave emissions in the post-merger phase, the remnant is consistently less compact while producing more dynamical ejecta and a more massive disk. The cost of this new solver is relatively modest thanks to the improved initial guess: our accretion disk tests are only ${\sim}10-25\%$ slower than HLLE, and for our binary neutron star runs with a microphysical equation of state, we find that HLLD is only ${\sim}3\%$ slower than HLLE across all runs.

title: Impact on Inferred Neutron Star Equation of State due to Nonlinear Hydrodynamics, Background Spin, and Relativity
abstract: Tidal interaction is a unique, detectable signature in gravitational wave signals from inspiraling binary neutron stars (BNSs), which can be used to constrain the neutron star (NS) equation of state (EoS). The tidal interaction is resonantly amplified as the orbital frequency approaches the NS fundamental mode (f-mode) frequency. It has been shown that the exclusion of tidal resonance in parameter estimation leads to a significant bias in the inferred NS tidal deformability and hence the NS EoS [Pratten et al. PRL 129, 081102 (2022)]. The strength and location of tidal resonance depend sensitively on the f-mode frequency, which is typically modeled using its universal relation with the tidal deformability that is derived for an isolated, non-spinning NS assuming only linear fluid perturbations. In a BNS inspiral, the f-mode frequency can be corrected by at least three known effects: nonlinear hydrodynamics, background spin, and relativity. We use Hamiltonian Monte Carlo simulations to estimate the systematic bias on tidal deformability when each frequency correction is ignored. Our study considers both loud, individual events and the stacking of a population of detections. Both scenarios are expected when the next-generation detectors are available with a sensitivity level increased by about an order of magnitude.
journal_ref: Classical and Quantum Gravity, Volume 43, Number 12, Pages 125011, 2026

title: High-quality electron beam generation from laser wakefield accelerators for driving compact free electron lasers
abstract: Despite the successful demonstration of compact free electron lasers (FELs) driven by laser wakefield accelerators (LWFAs), the pursuit of further enhancements in high-gain compact FELs presents a challenge due to the limitations in electron beam quality. In this work, we pinpoint the pivotal physics and optimization strategies for high-quality single-stage LWFAs that are crucial for high-gain FELs. We have delved into the synergistic injection mechanism, where the self-evolution injection threshold is far from reached at the injection position, with both the shock front and self-evolution of the laser playing a role in the injection process. A thorough discussion has been provided on the beam-quality degradation and optimization strategies, in terms of global (slice) energy spread and projected (slice) emittance. With the goal of achieving high-gain FELs driven by LWFAs, we have also explored the synthesis quality of the electron beam to determine an optimized power gain length. A comprehensive start-to-end simulation has been conducted, demonstrating the effectiveness of compact FELs powered by these high-quality electron beams. The resulting radiation reaches the saturation regime after a 4.5-meter-long undulator, with an energy of 17.4 {\mu}J and a power of 6.0 GW at a wavelength of 23.9 nm. This proposed scheme offers not only a framework for optimizing beam quality in LWFAs, but also a promising path for future compact LWFA-driven FELs to achieve saturated regimes, opening up new possibilities for widespread applications.

title: Design and Operation of a 3-Crystal Multi-Volume Reflection Array for Loss Reduction in CERN SPS Slow Extraction
abstract: The flux of protons slow-extracted from the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) to the North Area experiments is limited by the induced radioactivity of the beam lost on the electrostatic septum during third-integer resonant extraction. Crystal shadowing, in which a thin bent silicon crystal deflects the protons that would otherwise hit the septum wires, has been in operation at the SPS since 2021; a single crystal at a non-local position halved the extraction losses relative to the local crystal alone, short of the fourfold reduction that future high-intensity operation requires. In this paper, the design, deployment and operation of a 3-crystal Multi-Volume Reflection Array (MVRA) at the non-local position in the fourth long straight section (LSS4) are presented. The array geometry was designed by Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization (MFBO), combining a multilayer-perceptron surrogate with full particle tracking; it predicts a fourfold loss reduction with three crystals and up to tenfold with an ideally aligned array of four to five. At its optimum the as-built array reaches, and at its best point exceeds, the predicted factor of four, and beam dynamics simulations matched to the measured position and angle scans reproduce their shape to within 0.04 of the crystals-retracted loss. In physics production an extremum-seeking controller has held the array on its operating plateau, with a median loss reduction by a factor of 3.6 over 1.14 x 10^5 extraction cycles relative to the pre-shadowing baseline. The remaining margin to the target, the limitations of the present installation and the upgrade to a 4- or 5-crystal array are discussed.

title: Compact plasma-based extreme compression of relativistic electron beams
abstract: Accelerated particle beams are essential tools of modern science and technology with applications ranging from medicine [1], to light sources [2], to high-energy physics [3]. Over time, as accelerator-based experiments become more sophisticated and probe natural phenomena with greater temporal resolution, there is an increasing demand on beam parameters, in particular on bunch duration. Experiments have been proposed that require beams with 1-2 orders of magnitude shorter durations than what is possible with current state-of-the-art technology. However, state-of-the-art temporal bunch compressors force a trade-off between how short an electron bunch can be made and how well its transverse quality survives the strong bending magnets required to do so -- a limitation that stands as a grand challenge for accelerator physics to-date [4]. In this experiment, we demonstrate a new, compact compression technique for generating ultrashort, high-peak-current electron bunches that circumvents this trade-off using plasma wakefield acceleration. Just as chirped pulse amplification unlocked ultrashort, high-power laser pulses and the technologies that followed from them, here we demonstrate an analogous chirp-and-compress strategy applied to relativistic electron beams by using the extreme electric fields of a plasma wakefield in place of a stretcher-amplifier, thereby unlocking the path to ultrashort, extremely high-current electron beams. We demonstrate the first application of this plasma-compressed bunch using it to drive single-microbunch free electron lasing at optical wavelengths in a single, meter-scale undulator module, producing radiation pulses roughly four orders of magnitude more energetic than the first beam-driven, plasma-based free electron laser demonstration at the same accelerator facility [5, 6].

title: M-SHIVA 1.0: A Relativistic Resistive MHD Code for Heavy-Ion Collisions, with Applications to Momentum Anisotropy and Joule Heating in QGP
abstract: We present M-SHIVA 1.0 (Magneto-resistive Solver for Heavy Ions with finite-Volume Algorithms), a (2+1)-dimensional relativistic resistive magnetohydrodynamics code for heavy-ion collisions in Cartesian and boost-invariant Milne coordinates. The present implementation treats inviscid dynamics and employs an implicit-explicit (IMEX) Runge-Kutta scheme for the stiff conductivity-dependent terms, together with complementary primitive-variable recovery procedures and generalized Lagrange multiplier (GLM) divergence cleaning. The code reproduces standard shock-tube, cylindrical-blast-wave and relativistic-rotor benchmarks. We use the framework to investigate the momentum anisotropy and electromagnetic energy transfer in an expanding quark-gluon plasma (QGP). In a controlled elliptic-fireball setup, the electromagnetic field modifies the total momentum anisotropy mainly through its direct contribution to the transverse stress tensor, while the matter anisotropy is only weakly affected. We further separate the electromagnetic work into mechanical Lorentz-force work and irreversible Joule heating. Applications to Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 62.4$ and $200$ GeV and Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 2.76$ TeV employ optical-Glauber matter profiles, spectator-generated electromagnetic fields, and a temperature-dependent electrical conductivity motivated by lattice-QCD results. The ratio of Joule heating to expansion cooling is approximately $10^{-14}$-$10^{-11}$ for Pb+Pb collisions at $2.76$ TeV, $10^{-8}$-$10^{-5}$ for Au+Au collisions at $200$ GeV and $10^{-7}$-$10^{-4}$ at $62.4$ GeV, with no appreciable conductivity dependence of the matter or total momentum anisotropy. Resistive heating thus grows by orders of magnitude with decreasing collision energy but remains negligible compared with longitudinal expansion cooling for all systems considered.

title: r-Process Abundance Variations in Globular Clusters as Fossils of Turbulent Mixing
abstract: Several metal-poor Galactic globular clusters exhibit substantial star-to-star $r$-process abundance variations at nearly fixed [Fe/H], with the ensemble suggesting smaller variations toward increasing metallicity. We investigate whether this chemical structure can be inherited from incomplete mixing in the galactic environments in which the clusters formed. Using parsec-scale simulations of rare-element transport in a supernova-driven turbulent disk, we follow the redistribution of $r$-process ejecta and characterize the abundance structure of gas selected to trace star-forming environments. Rare enrichment events generate strong [Eu/Fe] inhomogeneities that persist across a range of physical scales. As chemical evolution proceeds, the available abundance variance decreases, while spatial averaging over larger regions reduces the differences between their characteristic abundances. The simulations provide substantial pre-collapse $r$-process variance at low [Fe/H] and show the same broad decline toward higher metallicity suggested by the globular-cluster measurements. Our results support an interpretation in which at least some of the observed $r$-process variations are inherited from pre-existing chemical structure in the natal environment, allowing globular clusters to preserve a fossil record of the mixing history between rare enrichment and star formation.

title: Perturbative QCD Constraints on Hot Neutron-Star Matter
abstract: Perturbative QCD, supplemented only by thermodynamic consistency, causality, and mechanical stability, constrains the equation of state of dense matter far below the densities at which the perturbative expansion itself converges. Until now, however, such constraints have been established only for cold, catalyzed matter. We show that this model-independent bound generalizes to finite temperature along adiabats labelled by the entropy per baryon $\hat{s}$, with the specific enthalpy $h=(\varepsilon+p)/n_{\mathrm{B}}$ assuming the role played by the baryon chemical potential at $T=0$. We find that increasing the temperature shrinks the allowed region monotonically in a form that is universal across structurally distinct mean-field families. For DD2, the density at which the equation of state becomes inconsistent with perturbative QCD decreases from $1.0$ to $0.74\,\mathrm{fm}^{-3}$ as $\hat{s}$ increases from $0$ to $5$, falling below the central density of the heaviest cold star. By $\hat{s}=4$, seven of eleven relativistic mean-field models are excluded at $6\,n_{\mathrm{sat}}$; approximately half of the equations of state drawn from two Bayesian posteriors are excluded by $\hat{s}\simeq3.4$--$4.4$. When mapped onto the QCD phase diagram, the bound becomes active at temperatures of $100$--$150$ MeV, precisely the regime transiently realized in neutron-star mergers and proto-neutron stars.

title: Numerical solution of the time-independent-wave-packet form of the Lippmann–Schwinger equation: Nystrom method vs Chebyshev expansion of the resolvent operator
abstract: Abstract This paper computationally explores some lesser-known results from the quantum scattering theory that gives the S-matrix in terms of the resolvent operator through the mediation of time-independent wave packets (TIWP). The S-matrix at a given energy is given by the ratio of the interacting and free TIWP’s evaluated at the corresponding on-shell momentum. This expression can also be expressed as the ratio of full and free resolvents at a given energy acting on the pre-collision wave packet. Another expression involves the ratio of the matrix elements of the interacting and free resolvents between post- and pre-collision wave packets. Computational implementations of these formal results involve the solution of the so-called TIWP form of the Lippmann–Schwinger equation (TIWP-LS). In the present contribution, the partial-wave TIWP-LS equation is solved using two schemes: (i) Direct numerical solution of the TIWP-LS equation via the quadrature discretization, and (ii) Construction of the resolvent operator by an expansion in Chebyshev polynomials of the scaled Hamiltonian. Computational performances of these procedures to compute the S-matrix are tested on a model potential for the p-wave case.

title: Neutron stars nearly close the window for muon-induced baryon-number violation
abstract: Baryon-number violation that needs a muon in the initial state can evade proton-decay searches and be observed in muon capture at Mu2e and COMET. Neutron stars contain muons, so the same interaction converts their protons into dark baryons, but the rate of this conversion in dense matter and its consequences have not been computed. In this paper we compute the conversion rate, the heat it deposits, and the evolution of a star under fast conversion. The coldest known neutron stars exclude conversion rates far below laboratory reach for every dark-fermion mass that capture in aluminium can produce, and faster conversion burns stars down or, unless conserved dark baryons repel each other strongly enough, collapses them. The repulsion they need follows a scaling law in the baryonic mass headroom of the nucleonic equation of state, which applies to any process that puts dark baryons in equilibrium with neutrons.

title: Leveraging Lensing-driven Early Warnings: Joint Detectability of lensed Gravitational Waves and their LSST Optical Counterparts
abstract: Gravitational lensing of gravitational waves (GWs) can be leveraged to provide early-warning times of $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{hours})$ to $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{days})$ prior to the mergers of binary neutron stars (BNSs) and neutron star-black holes (NSBHs). This capability could, in turn, enable electromagnetic (EM) observatories to capture transient emissions surrounding the time of the merger. In this work, we demonstrate the viability of jointly detecting gravitationally lensed BNS and NSBH mergers via GWs during the O5 observing run, alongside their associated kilonova counterparts using the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST). We simulate a population of lensed BNS and NSBH mergers detectable during O5 and utilize current benchmark forward models to generate the corresponding lensed kilonova light curves. We then assess the detectability of these light curves across LSST bands under various exposure limits. We find that among the detectable lensed mergers in O5, approximately 60\% of the BNS kilonova and 10\% of the NSBH kilonova will be observable within a single LSST exposure, with mostly quads dominating the detectable population. Furthermore, we define a detectability index ($\rm DI$), which determines the EM-detectability in optical of lensed GW-detectable BNS and NSBH mergers. We demonstrate the robustness and generalizability of the $\rm DI$ on our lensed BNS and NSBH population. Our work demonstrates that lensing-driven early warnings will be highly applicable in the near future, enabling the LSST to effectively follow up on BNS and NSBH triggers within GW localization areas during the O5 observing run.

title: Heavy-element dust as an explanation for the late-time kilonova spectra
abstract: Neutron star mergers are a leading site of r-process, producing radioactively powered optical and infrared transients known as kilonovae. Observations of the kilonovae AT2017gfo, associated with the gravitational-wave event GW170817, and AT2023vfi, associated with GRB 230307A, have enabled measurements of the mass of ejected r-process material and identification of heavy elements in the ejecta. However, late-time observations reveal strong infrared emission with temperature below 1000 K, which is difficult to explain by atomic absorption and emission processes alone. In this paper, we propose that kilonova ejecta provide conditions favorable for the formation of dust grains composed of refractory r-process elements including Zr, W, and Os. Assuming a simplified, empirically derived single power-law temperature evolution and using W reaction rate coefficients as a proxy, our kinetic dust formation calculations indicate that dust could form efficiently, particularly in slow ejecta. This stands in contrast to a previous study that relied on a classical nucleation framework. By performing radiative transfer simulations that incorporate dust formation, we demonstrate that, if formed, r-process dust could naturally explain the observed late-time infrared emission, although refining ejecta parameters and geometry will be necessary to match specific observational cases. The formation and abundance of r-process dust are highly sensitive to ejecta mass, composition, and expansion velocity. Infrared emission from r-process dust may therefore potentially serve a new probe of heavy-element production in neutron star mergers.

title: Flux Variation of the Crab Pulsar Observed Using Fermi LAT and NuSTAR
abstract: The flux of pulsed emission from the Crab pulsar, just like most of other pulsars, is considered to be steady over time scales much larger than the pulsation period, except for a smooth, secular decrease related to the aging of pulsars. Such a steady assumption prevails in all theoretical investigations of pulsar emission models. However, here we report the discovery of stochastic fluctuation in the flux and photon index of the Crab pulsar gamma-ray and X-ray emissions utilizing archival data of Fermi LAT (0.1 -- 100 GeV, spanning 17 years) and of NuSTAR (3.0 -- 79.0 keV, spanning 13 years) observations. The origin of such fluctuation is intriguing. It might be related to possible configuration adjustment of magnetic fields in neutron stars' superconducting and superfluid interiors.

title: Role of interchange and mixed modes in magnetic Rayleigh–Taylor instability dynamics: A 2D vs 3D study
abstract: The magnetic Rayleigh–Taylor instability (MRTI) governs plasma mixing and transport in diverse systems. Owing to computational constraints, two-dimensional (2D) MRTI simulations are common. It is intuitive that 2D and three-dimensional (3D) counterparts differ significantly. One of the crucial differences is the types of wave modes admissible in the two systems. Perturbations in 3D MRTI facilitate the coexistence of interchange, undular, and mixed modes. Such rich physics is not possible in 2D, where the perturbations can only have undular modes. This raises the question, “How do the interchange and mixed modes change the MRTI dynamics?” To address this aspect, we simulate MRTI in 2D and 3D, across different magnetic field strengths. Consequently, this paper provides, currently lacking, a rigorous qualitative and quantitative evaluation of the similarities and differences between 2D and 3D MRTI. The 2D MRTI is characterized by large-scale plumes with inefficient mixing and significant fluid interpenetration, while the 3D is characterized by significant mixing and small-scale plumes. Consequently, higher gravitational potential energy is extracted in 2D. The small-scale vortices and large current sheets lead to higher energy dissipation in 3D. Extending to the fundamental nature of evolution, 3D simulations tend toward a self-similar state due to interchange and mixed modes. But such behavior was not observed in our 2D simulations, due to the persistent influence of the magnetic field. Surprisingly, the reconnection-driven magnetic-to-kinetic energy conversion is similar in 2D and 3D. Overall, the work concludes that interchange and mixed modes influence the dynamics significantly, leading to stark differences between 2D and 3D MRTI. The work thus guides the extent to which one can extrapolate the 2D simulation results to understand MRTI in astrophysical and fusion energy systems.

title: Robustness analysis of laser pulse designs in direct-drive fusion
abstract: The robustness of laser pulse shaping is a critical issue for direct-drive inertial confinement fusion, as realistic laser systems exhibit temporal fluctuations that can affect implosion performance. In this work, a robustness analysis of target designs is performed with respect to physically realistic perturbations of a reference pulse, including temporal jitter, correlated noise, and power-dependent variations. The method is applied to one-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations to assess the impact of these perturbations on the target performance. The analysis of robustness of power plant scale designs highlights strong sensitivity of implosion performance to early-time pulse shaping and reveals a trade-off between gain and robustness. Although limited to one-dimensional simulations, this approach provides a useful framework for preliminary pulse design and robustness assessment.

title: Projected sensitivity of the ANUBUIS detector to tau-coupled Heavy Neutral Leptons
abstract: Heavy Neutral Leptons (HNLs) provide a minimal and well-motivated extension of the Standard Model neutrino sector, and are naturally long-lived for small mixing angles between SM neutrinos and HNLs. A previous ANUBIS study determined the projected sensitivity to a single Majorana HNL coupled exclusively to the electron or to the muon, corresponding to the BC6 and BC7 benchmark scenarios of the Physics Beyond Colliders initiative. The present article extends that work to the complementary BC8 scenario, in which the HNL couples exclusively to the tau lepton. As the tau lepton is itself unstable and because charged-current HNL decay modes become available only above the kinematic tau lepton production threshold, the production, decay and event-selection characteristics of this scenario cannot be obtained by rescaling the electron- or muon-coupled results in flavour. The analysis is carried out end to end, from signal-sample generation through acceptance evaluation to sensitivity extraction, with the released SET-ANUBIS~v1.0.0 framework.
authors: Oleg Brandt for the ANUBIS Collaboration

title: Magnetic field-induced enhancement and quenching of Urca emission in quark matter
abstract: Using first-principles field-theoretic methods, we investigate neutrino emission from strongly magnetized dense quark matter under conditions relevant to compact stars. We account for Landau-level quantization of both electron and quark states and show that it strongly modifies the kinematics of Urca processes. In particular, quark quantization restricts the available phase space in which both quark and electron energies can simultaneously lie near their respective Fermi surfaces. At moderately strong magnetic fields, before pronounced quark quantization sets in, the emission rate tends to increase on average with increasing field strength. In the regime of very strong fields, however, the increasingly restricted phase space first gives rise to Shubnikov--de Haas-type oscillations and then to resonance-like spikes near a discrete sequence of Urca-resonant magnetic field values, separated by regions of strong suppression. Finally, the emission rate becomes nearly completely quenched once $|eB| \gtrsim 6\mu_{e}\mu_{u}$, corresponding to approximately $B\gtrsim 1.5\times 10^{19}~\mbox{G}$ for the representative set of model parameters considered. We also find significant anisotropy in the longitudinal momentum emission near the Urca-resonant magnetic field values.
