title: Standalone Validation of a Pulsar Evolution Subroutine for NBODY6++GPU: Seven Test Scenarios
abstract: Pulsars in globular clusters provide critical constraints on the evolution of compact objects. However, the treatment of neutron stars in standard N-body codes is outdated, and requires a better implementation of magnetic field decay, spin evolution, and accretion driven recycling that shape their observable properties. We present a standalone validation of a pulsar evolution subroutine for NBODY6++GPU, systematically tested across seven controlled scenarios prior to integration into full cluster simulations. These scenarios isolate distinct evolutionary regimes, including young pulsar spin down, millisecond pulsar weak torque evolution, accretion driven recycling in X-ray binaries, environmental torques in dense cores, wide binary systems, and compact binaries in the dipole spin-down regime. Through two separate numerical implementations, we achieve cross validation demonstrating better than 0.1% agreement across all physical quantities and timescales. Our validation confirms that analytical solutions are reproduced with high precision for isolated pulsars, gigayear scale evolution (tau_c ~ 1.0 Gyr) matches observations of millisecond pulsars in clusters like 47 Tucanae, and accretion driven recycling operates with physically realistic timescales, yielding a final period of 1.0 ms and a period derivative of approximately -5.9e-19 s/s, with accretion dominance by a factor of about 14. We demonstrate that environmental torques remain negligible even in the densest cluster environments, while compact binary spin down is validated; gravitational wave orbital decay is deferred to future work. All validation codes, test suites, and integration instructions are publicly available to support future applications.

title: Search Method for Continuous Gravitational Waves from Rotating Neutron Stars in Highly Eccentric Wide Orbits
abstract: Recent results from the Gaia third data release have highlighted 21 potential neutron stars candidates in wide, highly-eccentric binary systems and provide estimates of their orbital parameters. We present a feasibility study for a directed search for continuous gravitational waves (CWs) tailored for these and similar systems. To this extent, we have computed a frequency metric to place templates in the parameter space accounting for uncertainties on the orbital parameters. We have built upon the FastTracks infrastructure to efficiently tackle the high-dimensional search space, leveraging a combination of downsampling and interpolation to reduce the computational cost of generating the binary Doppler correction. We performed an injection campaign to demonstrate the performance of this procedure and showed that a search using this approach is viable. Such a search would represent the first combination of Gaia observations and CW analysis.

title: Relativistic tidal response and mode excitation in neutron-star binaries
abstract: Tidal excitation links gravitational-wave emission to the internal dynamics of neutron stars. We study the dynamical tidal response of nonrotating stars with composition stratification, elastic crusts and possible first-order phase transitions. Using analytical Mano--Suzuki--Takasugi exterior solutions, we match stellar perturbations to an effective field theory and extract the poles and residues of the relativistic tidal response. Over the inspiral band, this response is accurately approximated by a sum of harmonic oscillators, as in Newtonian theory, each specified by a frequency $\omega_\alpha$ and a mode-specific tidal deformability $\lambda_\alpha$, or equivalently a tidal overlap $I_\alpha$. We couple these oscillators to relativistic effective-one-body dynamics, including gravitational redshift and frame dragging, to follow mode excitation and gravitational-wave emission. A decomposition into driven and free oscillations gives analytical mode amplitudes accurate to a few percent during inspiral. We also reconstruct the time-dependent crustal strain. In a representative $1.20+1.50\,M_\odot$ hadronic--hybrid binary, gravity, interface and shear modes produce a gravitational-wave phase shift of $\lesssim10^{-2}\,{\rm rad}$. Despite this small phase shift, gravity-mode excitation can overstrain the crust near its base, while the lowest shear mode produces widespread overstrain.

title: Nanosecond-LIBS-induced deuterium outgassing, diffusion, and surface modification in tungsten coatings
abstract: Abstract Tritium retention in plasma-facing components (PFCs) must be strictly controlled to ensure the safe operation of fusion devices. In ITER, compliance with the tritium inventory limit and assessment of fuel-removal strategies require in situ monitoring of fuel retention in PFCs. Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) is a diagnostic technique that can be implemented via remote handling to investigate fuel retention during maintenance shutdowns at ITER. In LIBS diagnostics, the selection of laser parameters plays a critical role in determining the ablation characteristics and thermal perturbation of the target. Used nanosecond (ns) laser pulses deliver energy on timescales that allow substantial thermal diffusion into the target, which could result in surface heating and melting. Under multi-pulse LIBS operation, these cumulative thermal effects can alter deuterium quantification, as deuterium may diffuse or outgas due to heating induced by earlier pulses. Such laser-induced perturbations can compromise accuracy of quantitative deuterium measurements if they are not properly accounted for in modelling. In this study, subsequent in situ ns-LIBS and in situ nuclear reaction analysis (NRA) measurements were performed in Magnum-PSI on compact and porous tungsten coatings using a defocused, millimetre-scale laser spot ( 2.5 × 2.5 mm ). Deuterium retention and depth profiles were determined in and outside the LIBS crater. Under the investigated laser conditions, NRA measurements indicated a 66%–79% reduction in retained deuterium within the sampled region of the LIBS crater, whereas pure material removal by ablation would account for only 21%–42%, demonstrating additional laser-induced outgassing. Compact coatings further exhibited melting and intermixing with the underlying substrate. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for defocused ns-LIBS-induced perturbations in retention measurements. Further experimental and modelling studies are needed to assess the dependence of these effects on laser spot geometry and to determine whether picosecond (ps) LIBS, together with consideration of cumulative multi-pulse effects, could improve the reliability of fuel-retention diagnostics in future fusion devices.

title: Precise measurements of the 3H/3He charge form factor ratio and their impact on the 3H-3He charge radius difference
abstract: Nuclear form factor measurements can be used to extract the nuclear charge radius. These can be compared to ab initio nuclear structure calculations, with the difference between 3H and 3He charge radii providing information on the spatial distribution of protons vs neutrons in these nuclei. Extractions of the 3H-3He charge radius difference are limited by the modest amount of data for tritium elastic scattering at low momentum transfer. The experiment made a precise measurement of the 3H/3He form factor ratio at low momentum transfer which is combined with the absolute 3He measurements to provide improved 3H data. This provides an improved determination of the absolute normalization corrections of world data sets, giving improved precision for the low-Q^2 measurements that are most sensitive to the radius. We extract the elastic cross sections and the 3H/3He ratio at Q^2=3.03 fm^{-2} and evaluate the impact of this point on a global fit of previous form factor extractions. We examine both the impact on the normalizations of the other data sets and the fit parameters, including the charge radius and its uncertainty. Our sensitivity study shows that the new precision data points constrain the normalization of previous data sets, reducing the uncertainties by up to 12% and yielding a 4% improvement in the radius. Including projected data based on an approved experiment yields improvements in the normalization factors of up to 20% and a 27% improvement in the 3H RMS charge radius extraction, allowing for an improved extraction of the 3H-3He radius difference from a direct fit to the form factor ratios over a range in Q^2.

title: Asymptotically causal metamodel for neutron star equations of state
abstract: Nuclear metamodels---phenomenological parametrizations of the energy of nuclear matter---are convenient tools to explore the space of realistic neutron star configurations constrained by astrophysical and nuclear data. While much recent work has focused on composition-agnostic barotropic models, the metamodel approach is designed to describe the composition dependence of the relevant thermodynamic potential. We revise a previously proposed nonrelativistic metamodel by introducing a more controlled high-density behavior, improving both its causal properties and its accuracy in reproducing the pressure and the $\ensuremath{\beta}$-equilibrium composition of microscopically motivated equations of state. Since asymptotic causality is enforced by construction, the fraction of discarded models due to superluminal sound speeds is substantially reduced, facilitating metamodel-based explorations of equilibrium neutron star configurations. We further assess our framework by performing a Bayesian inference of neutron star properties beyond standard observables such as masses and radii, exploiting the metamodel's ability to probe composition-dependent quantities including the dUrca threshold and the Ledoux criterion for g-mode stability.

title: Spin entanglement in $pp$ and $pA$ collisions: high-energy TMD effects and fragmentation probes
abstract: Spin-spin correlations of a quark-antiquark pair produced in proton-proton or proton-Ion collisions are investigated in $k_T$-factorization within the shockwave formalism. We construct the full spin-density matrix of both inclusive and diffractive channels in the limit in which the two quarks are back-to-back. In the inclusive channel, due to linearly polarized gluons, we show that a $\cos (2 \phi)$-modulation of the concurrence, stabilizer R\'enyi entropy, and quantum discord emerges and depends on the interplay between six small-$x$ gluon TMDs. The modulation is predicted to be maximally strong and independent of the transverse momentum imbalance, $q$, from a dilute (BFKL) perspective, while it is considerably suppressed by saturation effects. In diffraction, we observe that the pair is always entangled and exhibits the same properties found in diffractive DIS. We explain how these properties follow directly from the exclusive and eikonal nature of the Pomeron exchange. We trace this behavior to a spin-density matrix of rank at most two with maximally mixed marginals. For this class of states, entanglement and Bell nonlocality coincide even when the state is mixed, while the explicit form of the light-front helicity amplitudes ensures that both persist in the whole phase space. We suggest accessing the spin correlations in unpolarized hadron collisions through the Collins and dihadron fragmentation functions. We point out that, in inclusive production, for massless quarks, suitably chosen double-Collins asymmetries provide promising entanglement witnesses.

title: Receiving Exoplanet Messages with Gravitational-wave Carriers: The Gravitational-wave Radial Velocity Method
abstract: Abstract Gravitational-wave (GW) radial velocity (RV) may offer a new method for detecting exoplanets, one that would primarily target planets orbiting GW-emitting, ultracompact, post-main-sequence stellar objects such as white dwarfs, neutron stars, and black holes. In this work we show that while similar to electromagnetic-based RV, this GW-based method depends on the “phase modulation index” (PMI), a parameter that is more sensitive to high-mass, long-period exoplanets. We investigate the potential of GW RV for GW sources in both the mid-frequency spectrum (where the upcoming LISA mission will operate) and the high-frequency spectrum (where the current LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA (LVK) observatories operate). Remarkably, we find that the PMI increases by a factor of ∼ O 1 0 4 − 1 0 6 going from the mid-frequency to the high-frequency GW spectrum, which results in a greater redistribution of observed power due to the exoplanet’s presence. By analyzing the power content of the observed GW signal, we derive analytic expressions to predict the GW carrier frequency power loss due to the exoplanet and the signal-to-noise ratio of the GW source and the exoplanet. We also explore the effects of the additional Doppler effect caused by the motion of the GW observatory and the potential for GW source parameter bias introduced by the presence of an undetected exoplanet. All of this helps us better understand where the GW RV method may work best in the exoplanet mass–period discovery space.

title: Pion and kaon electromagnetic form factors in a flavor-dressed contact interaction: the role of Nf-screening on dynamical chiral symmetry breaking
abstract: We compute the electromagnetic form factors of the pion and the kaon in a symmetry-preserving contact interaction whose effective coupling depends on the number of active light flavors Nf , so that dynamical chiral symmetry breaking is screened as Nf grows toward the chiral transition. The calculation uses the rainbow-ladder truncation of the Schwinger-Dyson and Bethe-Salpeter equations with proper-time regularization, and it includes the dressed quark-photon vertex obtained from its own inhomogeneous Bethe-Salpeter equation in the same truncation. At Nf = 2 the model reproduces the established contact interaction values of the meson masses, decay constants and condensates, and the charge radii rpi = 0.447 fm and rK = 0.417 fm, which undershoot experiment by about one third, as is known for this class of interactions. We therefore restrict every comparison to Q2 less then or equal to 0.6 GeV2, confront it with the NA7 data and with one-loop chiral perturbation theory, and focus on the response to Nf . Both radii grow monotonically with Nf , and the growth survives every variation of the screening function and of the infrared confinement scale that we test. The growth is carried by the quark core rather than by the vector-meson dressing: between Nf = 2 and 6 the bare-vertex contribution to rises from 0.097 to 0.226 fm2, while the dressing contribution moves from 0.102 to 0.127 fm2 even though the rho pole drops from 0.93 to 0.70 GeV. The finite strange mass slows the kaon response only moderately.

title: Low-lying states of $^{115}$Cd modeled as a valence neutron coupled to $^{114}$Cd
abstract: $^{114}$Cd has historically been regarded as an ideal quadrupole vibrator due to its near-canonical level spacings, though this interpretation is disputed due to electromagnetic transition data from the two- and three-phonon states. In this paper we investigate whether, with the extension of including the single-phonon octupole state, the model is still useful in describing the coupling of a neutron to a cadmium-114 core to model the lowest- energy cadmium-115 states, as the triplet states have small to no influence in the calculation. The results thus provide supporting evidence for the tentatively-assigned $J^\pi$ values of the lowest-energy $^{115}$Cd states. A more- rigorous derivation than often used for the vibrational B(E{\lambda}) is used, in conjunction with the $^{115}$Cd structure calculation, to provide a theoretical prediction of the $^{114}$Cd octupole deformation.

title: HEART: a resonance-cascade model of soft hadron production in p+p collisions at 158 GeV/c
abstract: Fischer and co-workers interpret the NA49 identified-hadron spectra in p+p collisions at 158 GeV/c as the sum of a target and a projectile component, each the decay of an excited hadronic system. This paper supplies an event-level realization of that picture, the HEART model (Hadronic Excitations And Resonance Transitions), and tests it on the published NA49 data. Single diffraction, double diffraction, and non-diffractive exchange produce color-singlet excited systems. Each system is a catalogued resonance below a duality boundary of 1.7 to 2.2 GeV or a member of a resonant continuum above it. It de-excites by successive two-body transitions with exact conservation laws, and one-pion exchange produces the leading neutrons. Fourteen parameters are fitted to 1,254 points of the $\pi^\pm$, $K^\pm$, $p$, and $\bar{p}$ double-differential cross sections and eight neutron points. Under an error model that profiles the correlated systematic uncertainties, with a declared 5% model floor, the fit yields $\chi^2 = 2263$ on 1248 degrees of freedom. On the same points, EPOS-LHC, UrQMD, and PYTHIA 8 at their published tunes give $\chi^2$ values 4.2 to 14.4 times higher. The model needs no central source. The forward $K^+$ deficit, the forward $K^*(892)^0$ excess, and the flat $\Lambda$ $x_F$ distribution point to the momentum sharing at the vertex where the leading baryon turns into a hyperon. The $\Xi^-$ reaches 0.61 of the NA61/SHINE yield. The charged multiplicity of a heavy excited system grows linearly with its mass, faster than in $e^+e^-$ annihilation. The observables that distinguish a cascade from string and fireball models lie in the fragmentation region, where wide-acceptance fixed-target spectrometers can measure them.

title: Evidence for quark+quark pairing in proton formation
abstract: The question of pairing between quarks inside baryons is addressed by calculating the fragmentation functions that describe production of nucleons (protons and neutrons) in high-energy collisions and comparing attendant predictions with phenomenological global fits to available data and directly with data on hadron multiplicities. The fragmentation functions are obtained from nucleon parton distribution functions using the Drell-Levy-Yan relation and subsequently solving a coupled set of pion, kaon, and nucleon jet cascade equations. Strong empirical evidence is found for the presence of diquark correlations. In comparison with global fits, $d$ (down) quark to proton fragmentation ($d\to p$) exhibits the clearest signals. The strongest evidence is found in comparisons with the momentum-dependent proton multiplicity distribution: FFs built from a proton wave function that contains diquark correlations deliver a $z$-profile that is fully consistent with available data, whereas that obtained from a no-pairing wave function is disfavoured by data at the $9\sigma$ level.

title: Dissipative properties of isoscalar collective excitations in heavy nuclei
abstract: The dissipative properties of isoscalar collective motion in heavy nuclei are studied within a kinetic model of collective excitations in finite Fermi systems with a free moving surface. The model includes both the one-body damping produced by the interaction of nucleons with the dynamic surface of nucleus and the Landau damping mechanism. In this paper, we study the damping and dissipative properties of the isoscalar dipole collective modes and the isoscalar vortex octupole mode, which are formed due to dynamic effects of the nuclear surface. To study the damping mechanism of the considered collective modes, a multipole strength function is used in various approximations. It is shown that the damping of the considered isoscalar collective modes is due to a one-body damping mechanism. An analytical expression for the dissipation coefficient at finite frequency for the collective variable describing multipole oscillations of nuclear surface is obtained. It was found that the dissipation coefficient in the energy region of the considered isoscalar collective modes does not exceed the wall formula friction coefficient derived in the one-body dissipation theory. This result confirms the understanding of friction in the wall formula as a macroscopic limit of the one-body nuclear dissipation.

title: A universal probe of QCD spin physics from fragmentation energy correlator
abstract: We study the fragmentation energy correlator (FEC), which combines the nonperturbative fragmentation function with the infrared-safe energy correlator, as a new probe of the three-dimensional dynamics of QCD hadronization. We demonstrate, both theoretically and numerically, that FEC applies universally to inclusive hadron production in lepton-lepton, lepton-hadron, and hadron-hadron collisions, without requiring jet algorithms or simultaneous measurements of other heavy objects. Through the nontrivial transverse-spin dependence, FEC provides a sensitive probe of the chiral-symmetry-breaking scale in QCD via its variation with the energy-correlator scale.

title: diffhydro : Inverse Multiphysics Modeling and Embedded Machine Learning in Astrophysical Flows
abstract: Abstract We present the extension of the differentiable hydrodynamics code, diffhydro , enabling scalable partial differential equation-constrained inference and integrated hybrid physics–machine learning (ML) models for a wide range of astrophysical applications. New physics additions include radiative heating/cooling, Ornstein–Uhlenbeck–driven turbulence, and self-gravity via multigrid Poisson. We demonstrate good agreement with the Athena++ code on standard validation tests like Sedov–Taylor, Kelvin–Helmholtz, and driven/decaying turbulence. We further introduce a solver-in-the-loop neural corrector that reduces coarse-grid errors during time integration while preserving stability. The addition of custom adjoints facilitates efficient end-to-end gradients and multidevice scaling. We present simulations up to 1024 3 elements, run on distributed GPU systems, and we show gradient-based reconstructions of complex initial conditions in turbulent, and self-gravitating, radiatively cooling flows. The code is written in JAX, and the solver’s modular finite-volume components are compiled by Accelerated Linear Algebra into fused accelerator kernels, delivering high-throughput forward runs and tractable differentiation through long integrations.

title: Spin Asymmetries for Twisted-Neutron Capture by Polarized $^3$He Nuclei
abstract: We provide a theoretical analysis of a nuclear reaction caused by twisted neutrons that carry an additional Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) along the propagation direction. Angular momentum selection rules are derived for the thermal-neutron capture reaction on a spin-polarized $^3$He nucleus. We demonstrate that noticeable novel spin effects due to OAM are limited to the region of the size of de Broglie wavelength around the phase singularity of the beam. Spin asymmetries are predicted for a range of experimental constraints.

title: Sensitivity of jet and dijet observables to medium effects in pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV using X-SCAPE/JETSCAPE
abstract: Establishing jet quenching in small collision systems, such as high-multiplicity proton-proton collisions at the LHC, is challenging because the expected modifications are small and can be obscured by event-selection effects, multiparton interactions, and multijet production. We examine the response of several jet and dijet observables to medium-induced changes in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV using the JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE framework. First, a simplified Bjorken-expanding brick medium is compared with a vacuum reference for several brick lengths and strengths of transport coefficients. Second, separately generated realistic vacuum and medium samples with fluctuating initial conditions and event-by-event hydrodynamic evolution are compared after selecting the highest-activity 20% of events. Full anti-$k_T$ jets are reconstructed with $R=0.2$ and $R=0.4$. The observables are dijet invariant mass, leading- and subleading-jet transverse momentum, folded azimuthal separation, dijet asymmetry, Soft-Drop groomed jet radius, and groomed mass. In the brick calculation, the dijet-mass spectrum shows the clearest ordered response: departures from the vacuum reference generally increase with brick length and strength of transport coefficient and are more visible for the narrower jet radius, while the jet-$p_T$ and dijet-asymmetry changes are smaller and no clear azimuthal broadening is resolved. In the selected realistic events, the ungroomed medium-to-vacuum ratios remain close to unity but contain localized kinematic differences, together with a modest increase of the mean dijet asymmetry. The groomed-radius and groomed-mass ratios show localized differences but do not exhibit a persistent angular narrowing or mass redistribution. These findings quantify the sensitivity of the studied observables to medium-induced jet modifications in the present pp calculations.

title: Role of the scission-line structure in the formation of the fragment-mass distribution in $^{180}$Hg fission
abstract: The fission of $^{180}\mathrm{Hg}$ is investigated by studying the stochastic evolution on the potential energy surface calculated within the multidimensionally constrained relativistic Hartree--Bogoliubov (MDC-RHB) model. The MDC-RHB model provides the zero-temperature potential-energy surface in the $(\beta_{20},\beta_{30})$ plane and self-consistent density distributions, from which scission configurations are identified using a geometrical neck criterion. The evolution toward scission is described by a master equation on the same deformation mesh, with transition rates determined by deformation-dependent microscopic level densities. The level densities are obtained in a finite-temperature BCS treatment using the MDC-RHB single-particle spectra and zero-temperature pairing gaps as input. The effective barrier-top region is found to lie close to the scission line, making the detailed energetic structure of the scission boundary particularly important for the fragment distribution. The potential-energy landscape and scission-line structure strongly favor reflection-asymmetric configurations with pronounced prefragment deformations and lead to fragment-mass distributions centered close to the experimentally observed $A_{\mathrm L}/A_{\mathrm H}\simeq80/100$ division. An additional constrained $\beta_{40}$ analysis indicates that fluctuations beyond the $(\beta_{20},\beta_{30})$ collective space can generate an additional spread of the fragment masses. With increasing excitation energy over the range $E^*=34.0$--$65.5$ MeV, the symmetric component is enhanced, while the asymmetric fission mode remains dominant.

title: Properties of states in $^{19}Ne$ important for the $^{18}F(p,\alpha)^{O}$ reaction rate
abstract: Observation of the 511-keV positron-annihilation line would be a powerful probe of classical novae, with the primary source of positrons likely from the $\beta^+$ decay of $^{18}F$. We have determined the properties of important resonances in $^{19}Ne$ which govern the $^{18}F(p,\alpha)^{15}O$ reaction rate and the production of $^{18}F$ in novae. Measured $\alpha$ and proton angular distributions from states populated in the $^{19}F(^{3}He,t)^{19}Ne$ reaction identified six near-threshold proton $s$-wave $^{18}F+p$ ($L_p=0$) states, and the asymptotic normalization of these states was studied using the symmetry-adapted no-core shell model. We have improved our understanding of states contributing to the $^{18}F(p,\alpha)^{15}O$ reaction rate and show that earlier studies significantly underestimated the uncertainties.

title: Impact of ICRH-driven beta-induced Alfvén eigenmode on fast-ion redistribution and ion heating in EAST plasmas
abstract: Abstract In magnetically confined plasmas, energetic-particle (EP)-driven instabilities can induce redistribution and losses of energetic ions, thereby affecting plasma heating and confinement. In this work, fast-ion-driven beta-induced Alfvén eigenmode (BAE) excited by ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH) was investigated in low-density EAST plasmas using experimentally reconstructed equilibria and profiles. Experimentally, strong ICRH led to a significant increase in ion temperature and plasma stored energy, accompanied by the excitation of an Alfvén eigenmode at 64kHz under 1.6 MW heating power, while no such mode was observed at reduced power. Continuum analysis identified this mode as a core-localized BAE. To interpret these observations, integrated simulations combining TORIC, ASCOT, and GTC were performed. A modified fast-ion distribution function was implemented to capture the strong velocity-space anisotropy of ICRH-generated fast ions. Linear gyrokinetic simulations reproduced the observed BAE frequency and identified a threshold in fast-ion pressure for mode excitation. Orbit-following simulations with realistic wall geometry demonstrated that the BAE induces significant phase-space redistribution and enhances the loss of high-energy fast ions (energy >600keV). Separately, the ASCOT power-deposition analysis shows that the strong BAE reduces the collisional power transferred from fast ions to thermal ions, thereby suppressing the fast-ion contribution to ion heating and limiting the increase in ion temperature. As the measured BAE activity decreases in Phase B, recovery of this ion-heating channel explains the subsequent rise in ion temperature. These results clarify the interplay between ICRH-generated fast ions, BAE activity, and ion heating, and provide insights into optimizing fast-ion confinement and heating efficiency in future burning plasma devices.

title: Unpolarized proton PDF with physical quark masses and large momenta
abstract: We present a lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) calculation of the proton isovector ($u-d$) unpolarized parton distribution function (PDF) at physical sea and valence quark masses, using Coulomb-gauge-fixed quark bilinears within the large-momentum effective theory framework. The calculation is performed on a (2+1)-flavor ensemble with a lattice spacing of $a=0.076$ fm and proton momenta up to $2.3$ GeV. We combine kinematically enhanced nucleon interpolating operators, the Coulomb-gauge method, and high-statistics measurements to improve the signal quality at large momenta and quark separations. We use the static regularization-independent momentum subtraction and hybrid schemes to renormalize the bare matrix elements. The light-cone PDF in the $\overline{\rm MS}$ scheme is obtained from the quasi-PDF through next-to-leading-order (NLO) perturbative matching supplemented by next-to-leading-logarithmic renormalization-group resummation. With reduced uncertainties, the resulting PDF is consistent with our previous calculation on a similar lattice ensemble with $a=0.06$~fm and a valence pion mass of 300 MeV. Notably, despite the reduced uncertainties, the agreement with the phenomenological PDF persists over the longitudinal momentum fraction range $0.25\lesssim|x|\lesssim0.75$, where the lattice calculation is expected to be reliable. This agreement is further supported by a comparison in coordinate space, where our short-distance lattice matrix elements are consistent with those obtained from the phenomenological PDF through NLO matching. In particular, we observe close agreement in the imaginary part for the first time. Together, these results represent an encouraging step toward precision benchmarking of lattice QCD calculations of PDFs.

title: Linking solar flare observations to a series of impulsive solar energetic particle events measured with Solar Orbiter at 0.5 au. A case study to explore linkage capabilities, limitations, and potentials
abstract: Impulsive solar energetic particle (SEP) events are often associated with solar flares, but a detailed quantitative understanding of the underlying particle acceleration and injection process into interplanetary space is still lacking. We aim to identify the solar sources of a series of four impulsive SEP events measured with Solar Orbiter at a close solar distance of 0.51,au between March 5-6, 2022. By linking and analyzing remote sensing and in situ observations of these events, we aim to provide new constraints for the acceleration of flare-associated SEPs. We analyzed the energetic electron, proton, and heavy ion data measured with the Energetic Particle Detector (EPD) suite on Solar Orbiter. We estimated the injection times of the SEPs from the Sun and compared these times to the occurrence of solar flares, related extreme ultraviolet (EUV) brightenings, and type-III radio bursts. The flares and their source region were observed with remote sensing instruments from Solar Orbiter and the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO), with the two spacecraft radially aligned on March 5-6, 2022. We find that all four SEP events in the observed series can be plausibly linked to the same activated filament in the flaring active region AR12961. Although the combined flare and filament activity did not trigger a coronal mass ejection (CME), the produced energetic particles were able to escape into interplanetary space, possibly along open fan loops in the vicinity of the flare sites. All four linked SEP events show typical in situ SEP composition of impulsive flare-associated events with enhanced 3He/^4He and Fe/O ratios. Most interestingly, we find that the two SEP events associated with larger flares and (failed) filament eruptions show about five times stronger ^3He/^4He enhancements compared to the other two events. Since all four SEP events originate from the same repeatedly flaring filament and the heliospheric particle transport conditions are generally comparable, the differences in the measured SEP spectra among the events are likely related to the details of reconnection at the flare site or the associated (failed) filament eruptions. In particular, the precisely measured differences in 3He / ^4He ratios could be used to test model mechanisms for preferential ^3He acceleration in solar flares, such as particle beam-driven ion-cyclotron waves.

title: Determining the NJL Coupling and AMM in Magnetized QCD Matter via Machine Learning
abstract: In this study, we investigate the phase structure of magnetized QCD matter by determining the field-dependent parameters of the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model through a physics-informed machine learning framework. Specifically, we focus on extracting the optimal functional forms for the running coupling constant $G(eB)$ and the quark anomalous magnetic moment (AMM) ratio $v_2(eB)$, using lattice QCD computation on the chiral transition and condensate behavior. By embedding the NJL gap equation as a differentiable physics-constrained module, our neural network pipeline identifies continuous parameter functions that accurately reproduce the inverse magnetic catalysis (IMC) effect. Our results demonstrate that the magnetic field smoothly suppresses both $G$ and $v_2$. This approach not only bridges the gap between effective models and lattice data but also provides new microscopic insights into the response of the QCD vacuum to strong magnetic fields. As an independent test, the neutral-pion mass is calculated with the mean learned parameters and reproduces the decreasing trend of recent lattice results without a pion-data refit.

title: Automated optimization of microbunching for seeded free-electron laser schemes
abstract: Seeded free-electron lasers (FELs) have become indispensable tools across numerous scientific fields, owing to their high coherence and stability. Unlike self-amplified spontaneous emission, seeded FELs require a prebunched electron beam to be formed upstream of the radiator, enabling the subsequent generation of fully coherent radiation. This bunching process can be numerically calculated based on the specific components and their parameters used. To facilitate the discovery and optimization of such FELs, in this paper we present an automated optimization method for the microbunching process in seeded FEL schemes. It is demonstrated that the method can automatically reproduce established seeded FELs, such as echo-enabled harmonic generation, eliminating the need for prior physical analysis. Moreover, the method yields new findings in seeded FELs that go beyond mere replication. By incorporating more kinds of components and exploring a broader set of optimization objectives, the optimization can be extended to explore more possibilities.

title: Untangling flow-harmonic correlations in OO and Pb--Pb collisions at the LHC using event-shape engineering
abstract: Symmetric cumulants $\mathrm{SC}(m,n)$ measure the correlation between the event-by-event fluctuations of the flow harmonics $v_m$ and $v_n$, which, for higher harmonics, is influenced by the nonlinear response to the elliptic ($v_2$) and triangular ($v_3$) flow. Event-shape engineering, which selects events by the reduced flow vector $q_n$, is expected to control this contribution. However, its power is limited by the small forward multiplicity in light-ion collisions. In this work, we study the effect of the $q_2$ and $q_3$ selections on the symmetric cumulants in OO and Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.36$~TeV using EPOS4 with an ATLAS-like acceptance. Using the law of total covariance, the symmetric cumulant is separated into a selected part, which follows the differences between the $q_n$ classes, and a residual part within them. It is observed that in OO collisions the correlations of $v_2$ with $v_3$ and $v_4$ remain almost entirely within the $q_2$ classes, unlike in Pb--Pb collisions. Nevertheless, events with the smallest $q_2$ in central OO collisions show weaker correlations of $v_2$ with $v_3$ and $v_4$, which is attributed to $v_4$ approaching its linear response. In Pb--Pb collisions, the $q_2$ and $q_3$ selections act separately on the two factors of the nonlinear coupling of $v_5$, which establishes a way to isolate them experimentally.

title: Radial Oscillations of Viscous Stars at Finite Temperature
abstract: We study the radial oscillation spectrum of relativistic stars within Israel-Stewart and Navier-Stokes theories, extending previous analyses to include heat diffusion and a thermodynamically consistent finite-temperature equation of state. The inclusion of heat flux gives rise to a distinct thermal sector in the mode spectrum, whose structure closely mirrors the dispersion relations of an infinite dissipative fluid. Within Israel-Stewart theory, the thermal modes transition from purely damped to propagating behavior above a critical overtone number, providing a finite-size realization of relativistic second sound in compact stars. Remarkably, the finite stellar geometry can push even the fundamental thermal mode into the propagating regime -- a feature with no continuum analogue. For the class of equations of state considered here, where finite-temperature corrections enter as controlled, Sommerfeld-type perturbations of a cold polytrope, the thermal sector couples only weakly to the ordinary fluid oscillation spectrum, with the coupling being of second order in a suitable temperature parameter. We further show that the discrete stellar spectrum is well captured by an analytic ansatz constructed from the flat-spacetime dispersion relations, with the star's finite radius discretizing the continuous mode structure. Our results complete the analysis of radial oscillations of viscous stars by incorporating the last remaining dissipative degree of freedom within the Israel-Stewart framework.

title: No Einstein Relation, No Problem: How Relativistic Weakly Coupled Heavy Quarks Equilibrate Beyond Leading Logarithm Anyway
abstract: Relativistic heavy quarks equilibrate even when their microscopic drag and momentum diffusion violate the Einstein relation. We investigate how equilibration proceeds as a function of the coupling and compared to simplified Fokker-Planck models. To do this, we present a detailed calculation of the momentum-transfer kernel in weakly coupled non-Abelian plasmas through strict $\mathcal{O}(g^4)$, and study the resulting dynamics at leading order in the inverse heavy-quark mass. Beyond leading logarithm, its non-Gaussian structure plays a crucial role in equilibration. We examine closely the analytic structure of the evolution kernel, determine the large-order asymptotics of the momentum-transfer cumulants, and show how the kernel's bounded analytic domain fixes asymmetric exponential tails at the level of the momentum transfer probability. Strongly coupled $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM also features an approximately Gaussian core and exponential tails, but differs in the nature of the kernel's singularities and the velocity dependence of the transport coefficients and tail exponents. These differences have distinct dynamical consequences: for the parameters studied, the persistence of the relativistic population in steeply falling spectra is largely explained by drag alone at very weak coupling, whereas fluctuation-induced survivor bias produces a large relative enhancement at strong coupling. Nevertheless, the shared qualitative structure between weak and strong coupling points the way towards a practical phenomenological description of heavy quarks anchored in first-principles field theory.

title: Hadronic final-state effects on open-charm production at LHC energies
abstract: We investigate the influence of hadronic final-state interactions on open-charm observables in pp and Pb+Pb collisions at LHC energies within the microscopic Parton-Hadron-String Dynamics (PHSD) transport approach. Calculations with and without charm-hadron rescattering are compared with ALICE measurements and predictions of the Statistical Hadronization Model for charm. The relative integrated $D$-meson multiplicities are essentially insensitive to hadronic interactions. PHSD reproduces the weak system dependence of the nonstrange $D$-meson ratios and the increase of $D_s^+/D^0$ from pp to Pb+Pb collisions, consistent with the statistical-model trend from strangeness undersaturation towards equilibrium. In contrast, hadronic rescattering redistributes the transverse momentum spectra at low and intermediate momenta and enhances the elliptic flow. These results demonstrate the importance of accounting for the hadronic evolution when extracting QGP properties from differential open-charm observables.

title: Flavor decomposition of the nucleon axial and tensor charges from lattice QCD
abstract: We determine the nucleon axial and tensor charges using four ensembles of twisted-mass clover-improved fermions with approximately equal physical volumes of about 5.5~fm and four lattice spacings, $ a=0.05$~fm, 0.06~fm, 0.07~fm, and 0.08~fm. The mass of the degenerate up and down, strange and charm quarks are tuned to approximately their physical values. We compute both connected and disconnected contributions to determine the isovector and isoscalar charges and their flavour decomposition. For the nucleon isovector axial charge we find $g_A^{u-d}=1.263(34)(26)$, in agreement with the experimental value. For the isoscalar axial charge we find $g_A^{u+d}=0.458(16)(1)$, while for the corresponding tensor charges we find $g_T^{u-d}=0.951(21)(5)$ and $g_T^{u+d}=0.556(16)(5)$.

title: Effects of the momentum-dependent mean-field on collective flow in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC-STAR beam-energy scan energies
abstract: Abstract Au+Au collisions at s N N = 3 and 4.5 GeV are simulated with the AMPT-HC transport model to examine how momentum-dependent nuclear interactions affect hadronic observables. Compared to the default momentum-independent potential, the momentum-dependent potential (MDI) suppresses Λ , π + , and K + production and increases proton yields at larger absolute rapidities within 0.4 < p T < 2.0 GeV c − 1 . The directed and elliptic flows of mesons appear to be more sensitive to MDI than those of baryons. This greater sensitivity may partly arise from MDI-induced changes in participant-spectator momentum exchange and the associated spectator-shadowing effects. The MDI effect on proton elliptic flow weakens systematically with increasing beam energy. These results indicate the importance of momentum-dependent interactions for describing collective flow at the collision energies investigated here.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: SuperSNEC: Fast and Accurate Light-curve Production for Large Hydrodynamic Model Grids Using Adaptive Gridding
abstract: Abstract We present SuperSNEC, an accelerated version of the SuperNova Explosion Code (SNEC) designed for rapid production of large radiation-hydrodynamic model grids using low-zone-count simulations (∼100 zones). The main advance is adaptive gridding of the computational grid, which preserves light-curve fidelity relative to a high-resolution SNEC baseline (∼1000 zones) while delivering a runtime improvement of ∼420 × . SuperSNEC also includes solver optimizations, optimized radioactive-energy deposition and ray-tracing, and improved 56 Ni mixing controls. We quantify the speed-accuracy trade-off for a 100-zone configuration against a 1000-zone reference and define baseline settings for efficient large-grid inference of stripped-envelope supernovae. Our optimized 100-zone setup achieves an rms light-curve residual of 0.022 mag relative to the 1000-zone reference, at a runtime of < 2 s per model. Applied to SN 2011dh (Type IIb), SN 1993J (Type IIb), and SN 2020oi (Type Ic), SuperSNEC recovers light-curve parameters consistent with the literature. In particular, SN 2020oi is well reproduced by a model powered by 56 Ni decay and the standard hydrodynamic evolution, with no clear evidence that an additional power source such as interaction with circumstellar meterial or a central engine is required.

title: Symmetry-preserving higher-derivative formulation of non-relativistic baryon chiral effective field theory
abstract: A symmetry-preserving higher-derivative formulation of the non-relativistic baryon chiral effective field theory is introduced. Integral equations for the two-nucleon scattering and the deuteron structure functions are derived and numerical solutions at leading order are obtained.

title: Short-range dynamics of $X(3872)$ and $T_{cc}(3875)^+$ in a coupled-channel framework
abstract: We study the short-range dynamics in the coupled-channel description of the $S$-wave $D \bar{D}^*$ and $DD^*$ systems for $X(3872)$ and $T_{cc}(3875)^+$, respectively. Contact interactions are related through scalar- and vector-meson exchange saturation, while pion exchange is included explicitly with its local term subtracted. The coupled Lippmann-Schwinger equations incorporate the self-energy of the unstable $D^*$ mesons, thereby accounting for the three-body $D \bar{D} \pi$ ($D D\pi$) dynamics. Fixing the contact interaction from the $T_{cc}(3875)^+$ pole, we trace the predicted $X(3872)$ pole as the local magnetic dipole term from vector-meson exchange is varied. Retaining this term in full produces the shallowest poles, which remain approximately $5$--$12~\mathrm{MeV}$ below the observed $X(3872)$ mass. It is found that the pion exchange has a moderate effect on the binding energy and a stronger effect on the isospin violation for the $X(3872)$ state. The residual tension between the pure-molecular bound descriptions of $X(3872)$ and $T_{cc}(3875)^+$ is analyzed with the Feshbach projection. This analysis indicates a $DD^*$ interaction weaker than that implied by the purely molecular fits, and shows that the $T_{cc}(3875)^+$ state instead arises from the mixing of the $DD^{*}$ channel with a compact $cc\bar{u}\bar{d}$ state. We further examine the spatial structure using Born--Oppenheimer effective field theory. For separation radii of $0.5$--$1.5~\mathrm{fm}$, the combined charmonium and short-distance tetraquark weight in $X(3872)$ is $3.0$--$9.7\%$, while the short-distance weight in $T_{cc}(3875)^+$ is $1.3$--$14.4\%$. These results favor retaining the local vector-exchange contribution within the saturation framework and motivate a joint treatment of molecular and compact dynamics for the $T_{cc}(3875)^+$.

title: Role of Wigner SU(4) Symmetry in Low-Energy Spin-Isospin Transitions of Three-Valence-Nucleon Systems on LS Closed Cores
abstract: We investigate low-energy Fermi (F) and Gamow--Teller (GT) transition strengths in three-valence-nucleon systems from the viewpoint of Wigner SU(4) symmetry. For $^{19}{\rm F}$--$^{19}{\rm Ne}$, shell-model calculations show that the ground states contain a large component of the SU(4) representation whose spin-isospin wave function is fully antisymmetric. By varying the spin--orbit splitting in the shell-model Hamiltonian, we demonstrate clear correlations of the SU(4) overlap with both the GT strength to the ground state and its fraction of the total GT strength. For $^{7}{\rm Li}$--$^{7}{\rm Be}$, shell-model calculations show that the $3/2^-_\mathrm{g.s.}$ and $1/2^-_1$ states both belong predominantly to the same supermultiplet as the $^{19}{\rm F}$--$^{19}{\rm Ne}$ ground states. The observed strong GT transitions to these states are therefore interpreted as transitions within the same SU(4) multiplet, split by the spin-orbit interaction. Thus, Wigner SU(4) symmetry provides a unified interpretation of low-energy GT strength concentrations in three-valence-nucleon systems. In particular, the concentration of both F and GT strengths in the same $^{19}{\rm F}$--$^{19}{\rm Ne}$ ground-state transition is naturally understood as a three-valence-nucleon extension of the SU(4) mechanism underlying the low-energy strong GT peak in $^{18}{\rm O}$--$^{18}{\rm F}$.

title: Relativistic corrections and high-energy resummation for exclusive heavy quarkonium photoproduction
abstract: The $O(v^2)$ correction to the high-energy resummed coefficient function for the exclusive photoproduction of vector ($1^{--}$) heavy quarkonia off hadrons is computed, thereby taking into account corrections of $O(v^2 \alpha_s^n \ln^{n-1}(x/\xi))$. When expressed in terms of the physical vector-meson mass ($M_V$) and the relative heavy-quark velocity ($\langle v^2 \rangle$) using the Gremm-Kapustin relation, the computed correction turns out to be negligible at the scale $\mu_F=M_V$. However, it partially cancels the $\mu_F$ dependence of the $O(v^2)$ correction to the LO coefficient function in $\alpha_s$, thereby improving the robustness of the predictions.

title: Proton Number Fluctuations in Au+Au and Ag+Ag Collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=2.4\ \mathrm{GeV}$: A JAM Model Study
abstract: Proton number fluctuations in low-energy heavy-ion collisions are sensitive to nuclear interactions, baryon-number conservation, and fluctuations of the collision volume, all of which can complicate searches for critical phenomena. We investigate proton-number cumulants and factorial cumulants up to fourth order in Au+Au and Ag+Ag collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=2.4\ \mathrm{GeV}$ using the JAM hadronic transport model in cascade and mean-field modes. We employ the Centrality-Independent Genuine Cumulant Analysis fRamework (CIGAR) to suppress the initial-volume fluctuations and compare its results with those obtained using conventional centrality-bin-width corrections. CIGAR closely reproduces the participant-number-based reference, whereas the multiplicity-based analysis exhibits substantial deviations. In both collision systems, the ratios $C_{2}/C_{1}$, $C_{3}/C_{1}$, and $C_{4}/C_{2}$ generally decrease toward more central collisions and with increasing rapidity acceptance, while the mean field modifies their magnitudes. A simplified treatment of light-nucleus formation through probabilistic proton removal shifts $C_{4}/C_{2}$ toward less negative values. These results establish a hadronic-transport reference without an explicit QCD critical contribution and highlight the importance of controlling centrality fluctuations, acceptance, and light-nucleus formation when interpreting experimental measurements at high baryon density.

title: On-shell renormalization in NREFT: a simplified description of resonances, bound states, and coupled channel effects
abstract: We discuss several issues regarding the modern generalization of Weinberg's compositeness criterion. In particular, we demonstrate that the on-shell renormalization in NREFT reproduces Weinberg's result and provides a simple description of resonances, bound states, and coupled channel effects. Additionally, we present the complete propagator, including the charged channel for the near-threshold p-wave states.

title: On the Method of Projection onto Localized States for Describing Reactions and Clustering
abstract: The method of projection onto localized states intended for describing reactions and clustering is examined. In particular, the method offers a simple extension of the no-core shell model to continuum- and clusterized bound states. A critical analysis of a previous realization of the method is provided. A way to minimize the number of basis functions required for convergence is given. An easy way to obtain exactly unitary and symmetric $S$ matrix from calculations is pointed out. The method is tested in one- and two-channel $np$ scattering problems with the Daejeon $NN$ interaction. It is shown that excellent convergence can be reached even when only oscillator states with low number of excitation quanta are retained.

title: Emerging of massive gauge particles in inhomogeneous local gauge transformations
abstract: A generalized theory of gauge transformations is presented on the basis of the covariant Hamiltonian formalism of field theory, for which the covariant canonical field equations are equivalent to the Euler-Lagrange field equations. Similar to the canonical transformation theory of point dynamics, the canonical transformation rules for fields are derived from generating functions. Thus---in contrast to the usual Lagrangian description---the covariant canonical transformation formalism automatically ensures the mappings to preserve the action principle, and hence to be {\em physical}. On that basis, we work out the theory of inhomogeneous local gauge transformations that generalizes the conventional local SU(N) gauge transformation theory. It is shown that massive gauge bosons naturally emerge in this description, which thus could supersede the Higgs mechanism.

title: Collective Signatures of Pionic Correlations at High Momentum Transfer
abstract: High-momentum-transfer reactions have provided experimental evidence for enhanced pionic correlations in nuclei, yet the microscopic connection between the low-energy pionic response and the delta-hole excitation spectrum remains unresolved. Here we identify hybrid pion-delta collective modes that emerge through the coherent coupling of nucleon-hole and delta-hole excitations. By evaluating the full delta-hole Lindhard function within the random-phase approximation, we find a robust low-energy hybrid pion-delta mode and a higher-energy collective delta-hole mode. The low-energy mode is strongly enhanced as the Landau-Migdal parameter is reduced, exhibiting behavior characteristic of a precursor to pion condensation. We further show that these modes may be probed through high-momentum-transfer charged-pion production reactions. Because the same collective pion-delta function governs both the response and the RPA correlation energy, our results connect experimentally observable collective excitations with microscopic many-body correlations.

title: Anomalous charge conjugation and parity in (2+1)-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics
abstract: We present a hydrostatic and first-order constitutive description of a mixed anomaly that involves $U(1)_Q$, $U(1)_F$, charge conjugation symmetry (acting only on $U(1)_Q$), and parity symmetry in $2+1$ dimensions. It is represented by a mutual Chern-Simons level $k_{QF}=\frac12 \,(\mathrm{mod}\ \mathbb Z)$. Adopting the already established multi-charge anomaly sector, we explicitly provide the information that this response is $odd$ under $\mathsf{C}$ and $\mathsf{P}$ symmetries separately, but $even$ under combined $\mathsf{CP}$ symmetry. We also provide a global inflow representative and compute the equilibrium cross-charge response which includes $\partial n_Q/\partial B_F=\partial n_F/\partial B_Q=1/4\pi \bmod 1/2\pi$. Using an analytic neutral-fluid example we show that this response is non-vanishing whereas the source-free hydrodynamic poles are invariant.

title: Amplitudes separation and strong-electromagnetic phases determination in the $\boldsymbol{J/\psi}$ decays into baryon-antibaryon pairs
abstract: We extract the relative phase between strong and electromagnetic amplitudes of the decays of a vector charmonium into spin-$1/2$ baryon-antibaryon pairs. Starting from a flavour-SU(3) effective Lagrangian with vector and tensor currents, we construct a parametrization in terms of partial waves coefficients. The electric and magnetic phases, the phase of the integrated complex overlap and the effective rate angle are derived from the same source amplitudes. We retain two possible solutions and both of them describe the scalar $\Sigma^+\bar\Sigma^-$ scan phase within its uncertainty, while presenting tension with several electric-magnetic production phases.

title: NuSTEC Review: Current Experimental and Theoretical Challenges of Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering
abstract: The precise measurement of neutrino properties is among the highest priorities in fundamental particle physics, involving many experimental and theoretical efforts worldwide. Since the experiments rely on the interactions of neutrinos in the nuclear environment, the planned advances in the scope and precision of these experiments require a commensurate effort in understanding and modeling the hadronic and nuclear physics of these interactions, as incorporated in neutrino event generators. This modeling is essential to every phase of the experimental analyses, and the theoretical uncertainties play an important role in interpreting experimental results. In this Review of current challenges, we summarize the open questions in neutrino-nucleus interactions at GeV-scale energies, and discuss in detail the potential impacts of these unknowns on the measurement of neutrino properties, using the determination of oscillation parameters as a central example. After an Executive Summary and a concise Overview of the issues, we address how the neutrino event generators treat these challenges, how electron-nucleus interactions can help understanding these challenges and the important unanswered questions for each underlying physics process---from quasi-elastic to deep-inelastic scattering. Across every topic, we find that current challenges can be met only through active support and collaboration among specialists in strong interactions and electroweak physics, including theorists and experimentalists from both the nuclear and high-energy physics communities.

title: Luminosity Signatures of Dark Sector Particles from Black Hole Evaporation in Neutron Stars
abstract: Microscopic black holes may form at the centers of neutron stars through the accumulation and collapse of dark matter. While Standard Model particles produced by Hawking evaporation are efficiently absorbed by the dense stellar medium, sufficiently weakly interacting and long-lived particles can escape and subsequently decay into high-energy neutrinos, photons, or charged particles, providing an indirect probe of Hawking radiation. We examine the joint energy--angular distribution of these secondary particles, incorporating mediator propagation, energy-dependent decay, and relativistic decay kinematics. For relativistic mediators, the normalized energy-integrated angular profile becomes approximately independent of the black hole temperature, with its characteristic extent controlled primarily by the combination $c\tau_S/D$ of the mediator lifetime and source distance, as the boost enhancement of the decay length is compensated by relativistic beaming. We demonstrate the viability of this mechanism and illustrate its phenomenology with gravitationally coupled scalars, axion-like particles (ALPs), dark photons, and heavy neutral leptons. Comparing with monochromatic mediator production from dark matter annihilation, we find that the energy-integrated angular profiles can be nearly degenerate, while the energy spectra and energy-resolved angular distributions remain distinct. Although the predicted signals may lie beyond the reach of current observatories, these complementary spectral and angular signatures provide potential targets for future high-energy neutrino and gamma-ray searches.

title: Isospin violation and the neutron weak magnetic moment
abstract: The recent measurement of weak magnetism in neutron beta decay [1] obtained a value that is consistent with the conserved vector current hypothesis requiring the assumption of isospin conservation. The influence of the quark-mass difference and electromagnetic effects that violate this conservation law are examined using non-relativistic constituent quark models and estimated to be of the order of at most 1%.

title: Machine learning assisted $\nu/\bar{\nu}$ discrimination in atmospheric neutrino events for CPV sensitivity in a 20-kton liquid scintillator detector
abstract: Atmospheric neutrinos span a broad range of energies and baselines, offering a complementary probe of leptonic CP violation. However, a JUNO-like liquid scintillator detector without a magnetic field cannot directly separate neutrino and antineutrino interactions, reducing CP violation sensitivity. This study investigates whether machine learning based statistical separation can improve CP violation sensitivity in a 20-kton detector. $\nu_{\mu}$ and $\nu_e$ charged current events are generated with GENIE (using Honda flux) in a JUNO-like detector geometry and are reweighted using OscProb three flavor oscillation probabilities incorporating Earth matter effects and NuFIT parameters. Detector response is approximated by smearing lepton and hadronic energies, neutrino direction, and neutron multiplicity. Logistic regression, XGBoost, and multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifiers are trained on inelasticity, neutron multiplicity, and charged lepton energy, with XGBoost selected for the analysis. CP violation sensitivity is evaluated for a 200 kton-year exposure using a Poisson likelihood with systematic nuisance parameters and marginalization over five oscillation parameters within their respective $3\sigma$ ranges. XGBoost achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of approximately 0.83 for both flavor samples. Under the square root approximation, peak CP violation sensitivity improves from 1.49 $\sigma$ to 1.96 $\sigma$ for normal mass ordering and from 1.14 $\sigma$ to 1.61 $\sigma$ for inverted mass ordering. Machine learning based statistical neutrino-antineutrino separation can recover part of the CP violation sensitivity lost in charge blind detectors. These preliminary results motivate further studies incorporating validated detector response and systematic uncertainties.

title: Tritium release and defect evolution in neutron-irradiated Li 2 Pb x Ti 1− x O 3 ceramic pebbles
abstract: Abstract Achieving tritium self-sufficiency remains a key challenge for future fusion reactors, creating a strong need for breeder materials with efficient tritium release. In this study, neutron-irradiated Li 2 Pb x Ti 1− x O 3 ( x = 0, 0.05, and 0.1) ceramic pebbles were investigated by tritium thermal desorption spectroscopy (T-TDS) and electron spin resonance (ESR). Tritium release was examined at different heating rates and under isothermal conditions, and the corresponding kinetic parameters were determined. All samples exhibited a single tritium desorption peak that shifted to higher temperatures with increasing heating rate, confirming a thermally activated release process. Pb introduction broadened the desorption peak and lowered the apparent activation energy for tritium release. Under isothermal heating, the tritium diffusion activation energy ( E d ) and pre-exponential factor ( D 0 ) increased simultaneously, following the compensation effect and suggesting multiple migration pathways. ESR isochronal and isothermal annealing showed that irradiation-defect annihilation occurs in two stages: a fast stage associated with electron migration and a slower stage governed by oxygen diffusion. The defect-annihilation range overlaps strongly with the main tritium-release range, indicating that tritium release is jointly controlled by diffusion and defect evolution. Increasing Pb content modifies irradiation-defect annealing behavior and influences tritium-release kinetics.

title: The diocotron instability in the trapped electrons experiment T-REX and its relevance to electron clouds in gyrotron guns
abstract: Abstract Efficient operation of gyrotrons is crucial for electron cyclotron resonance heating in fusion reactors. Electron clouds trapped within the magnetron injection gun (MIG) region of high-power gyrotrons can induce disruptive leakage currents that degrade operational stability. While previous investigations utilizing the TRapped Electrons eXperiment established the foundational mechanics of cloud formation in the kHz regime (Romano et al 2024 Rev. Sci. Instrum. 95 103511), the high-frequency non-linear dynamics governing cloud saturation and cross-field transport remain uncharacterized. This work focuses on characterizing the underlying diocotron instability responsible for this transport and the resulting bursty plasma behavior within a Penning–Malmberg-like configuration. To resolve the high-frequency evolution, we present time-resolved current measurements on key experimental components—specifically the outer electrode and the top flange (TF)—complemented by a newly developed fast current probe array installed at the TF to capture multi-mode azimuthal structures. To address early discrepancies between experiments and low-frequency models, the particle-in-cell (PIC) code FENNECS was upgraded to 3D (Le Bars et al 2022 Phys. Plasmas 29 082105; Le Bars et al 2023 Phys. Plasmas 30 030702; Le Bars 2023 PhD Thesis (EPFL); Le Bars et al 2024 Comput. Phys. Commun. 303 109268; Giroud-Garampon et al 2025 Phys. Plasmas 32 053903) enabling the self-consistent simulation of the space-charge fields. The experimental measurements highlight rotating structures in the electron cloud and a periodic collapse and reformation driven by the instability. The 3D PIC simulations show remarkable agreement with these experimental findings, accurately reproducing the cloud build-up and collapse frequencies, as well as the rotation frequency and direction of the diocotron modes. These results significantly advance the understanding of non-neutral plasma dynamics in environments mimicking gyrotron MIGs, providing a predictive framework to mitigate parasitic currents and improve gyrotron reliability in fusion energy systems.

title: Retained fuel removal from plasma-facing materials: effects of baking methods and hydrogen isotope exchange
abstract: Abstract Tungsten (W) is a prominent plasma-facing material for deuterium-tritium (D-T) fusion reactors, yet T fuel retention in W poses critical challenges to safety and operational viability. This study systematically compares three baking methods—vacuum baking, H2 gas atmosphere baking, and hydrogen (H) plasma baking—for removing D retained in W at 513 K, simulating realistic conditions for T removal in reactors. Experimental results demonstrate that D removal efficiencies reach 75% for vacuum baking after 16 h, 83% for H2 atmosphere baking after 16 h, and 99% for H plasma baking after 1 h. The superior performance of H2 atmosphere and H plasma baking is primarily driven by hydrogen isotope (HI) exchange, with efficiency strongly dependent on the concentration of H introduced into W. Higher H concentrations promote more complete exchange, leading to significantly reduced D retention. A multi-isotope Fill Level model was developed to simulate the end-to-end H plasma exchange process. The simulation reproduces the experimentally observed D removal kinetics and the emergence of HD desorption, with the D retention in good agreement with measurements. The pronounced disparity between H2 atmosphere baking and H plasma baking is fundamentally governed by the quantity of H entering W: H plasma promotes significantly greater H ingress, thereby enhancing HI exchange and resulting in a drastic reduction in D retention. This work provides both experimental validation and modelling support for HI exchange as an efficient T removal strategy.

title: Numerical investigation of helium leakage and transport from in-vessel cooling-circuit in fusion reactor using DSMC method
abstract: Abstract Early detection of micro-leaks is essential for fusion reactors because such leaks precede a large-break loss-of-coolant accident (LOCA), which can seriously threaten vacuum-vessel structural integrity and reactor safety. In high-vacuum vessels, micro-leak identification depends on the transport characteristics of the plume released from the leak, making plume simulation and feature analysis important for leak detection. However, micro-leak plumes evolve across transitional and free-molecular regimes, where conventional continuum methods become limited. The direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) method provides a promising approach for resolving cross-regime rarefied plume transport. In this work, DSMC is used to investigate helium leak plumes in the CFEDR vacuum vessel. Representative leak locations at the inboard blanket, outboard blanket and lower divertor, together with different leak intensities, are analyzed in terms of plume morphology, pressure distribution, affected volume and probe response. The results show that the plume evolves within 1–100 ms from a directional jet into a vessel-scale diffusive field, while pressure decays by approximately two to three orders of magnitude across the chamber. The pressure responses differ among the three representative leak locations, indicating that poloidally distributed probes can provide location-dependent signal features for the future development of leak-localization methods. At a leak intensity of 5 × 10 − 5 kg s − 1 , representative window probes reach the 10 − 4 Pa threshold within 4.35–8.50 ms, whereas lower-intensity leaks remain confined near the source and require more sensitive or cumulative detection. These findings provide preliminary guidance for multi-probe, multi-threshold monitoring strategies for early in-vessel LOCA warning in fusion reactors.

title: Linear and nonlinear benchmark of gyrokinetic simulation of energetic particle driven toroidal Alfven eigenmodes in ITPA TAE benchmark case
abstract: Abstract A new gyrokinetic code, TEK, was benchmarked in simulating energetic particle (EP)driven toroidal Alfven eigenmodes (TAEs) in the simple tokamak configuration chosenby the ITPA-EP group for code benchmarking purposes. Linear benchmark has beenwell established by other codes, whereas nonlinear benchmark for this case is lacking.This paper presents, besides the linear benchmark, nonlinear results for both single-nand multiple-n simulations (n is the toroidal mode number). The nonlinear resultsare in good agreement with an analytical theory on zonal field beat-driven by Alfveneigenmodes, partially verifying the correctness of the nonlinear simulations. Thesaturation level and the resulting EP transport are examined. This provides data forfuture inter-code nonlinear benchmarking.In TEK, all species (electrons, thermal ions, EPs) are treated on the same footingusing the gyrokinetic model (with electrons in the zero Larmor radius limit). Theelectromagnetic cancellation problem is mitigated by using the mixed-variable pull-back method. Numerical details related to electromagnetic gyrokinetic simulationare discussed.

title: Investigation of the inverse plasma sheath via BIT1 PIC modelling
abstract: Abstract In a classical plasma sheath, the potential decreases from the upstream towards the wall. The absolute value of the potential drop depends on a number of parameters, such as the electron temperature and the flux of electrons emitted from the surface. The question then is whether the wall potential can ever exceed the plasma potential—whether there is a realistic access to the so-called inverse sheath in tokamaks. We start our investigation from the work of Campanell and Umansky, reproduce their regime, and determine whether it is applicable to fusion-relevant conditions. Afterwards, we explore the theoretical conditions for accessing the inverse sheath.

title: Damping and accumulation characteristics of flow driven by fishbone instability
abstract: Abstract The persistence of fishbone-driven flows across successive bursts is critical to their potential role in regulating turbulence and improving core confinement, yet the damping characteristics of such flows have not been experimentally characterized. Here we report the first direct measurement of the damping rate of fishbone-driven flows using Doppler reflectometry on the EAST tokamak. The experimentally obtained damping rate exceeds prior theoretical predictions, and this discrepancy can be reconciled by incorporating the effective charge number $Z_{\text{eff}}$ into the accalculation of the damping rate. Furthermore, we observe that flow accumulation occurs when the time interval between successive fishbone bursts is sufficiently short, and we estimate the critical inter-burst interval threshold for accumulation to be approximately 1 ms under the present discharge conditions. These results establish an essential experimental foundation for understanding the temporal persistence of fishbone-driven flows and their implications for transport barrier dynamics.

title: Cross-machine profile prediction and differentiable optimization by learning multi-tokamak databases
abstract: Abstract The development of high-performance plasma regimes is becoming increasingly important for tokamak operation and scenario design. Conventional operation-space exploration relies on computationally expensive iterative simulations and experimental trial and error. Although machine-learning methods have recently been applied to this problem, many optimization approaches treat the predictive model as a black box. They can therefore require a large number of model evaluations and must be retrained when the objective or operational constraints change. In this work, we develop a neural-network surrogate for multi-tokamak profile prediction using public databases. Device-dependent dimensional input and output variables are transformed into appropriate normalized quantities. These normalizations of input and output variables enable the prediction model to be applied to new devices such as ITER. The surrogate forms a fully differentiable mapping from engineering parameters to plasma profiles and derived performance metrics. Automatic differentiation provides the exact Jacobian of this mapping and enables gradient-based optimization without treating the model as a black box. Under identical objectives and bounds, the proposed method requires substantially fewer model evaluations than other machine-learning approaches. The proposed framework offers an efficient route from multi-machine data to interpretable plasma optimization and reactor scenario design.

title: Automated shape optimization of stellarator divertor targets via Chebyshev parameterization and differential evolution
abstract: Abstract Managing extreme heat fluxes in the form of strike lines on divertor target plates is a central challenge that hinders the progression of reactor-relevant stellarators. We present an automated, fast, non-gradient-based optimization framework for shaping open stellarator divertor targets, applied to the Wendelstein 7-X (W7-X) island divertor as a test case. The target surface geometry is parameterized using a Chebyshev spectral basis whose low-order modes naturally encode the physics motivated deformations, namely: translation, tilting and higher-order bending, which have an influence on the incidence angle and flux tube connection-length distributions at the target surface. The heat flux distribution on a target surface is evaluated by EMC3-Lite, a fast three-dimensional Monte Carlo edge-plasma transport code that self-consistently solves an energy transport equation with a sheath boundary condition, thereby avoiding the fixed-velocity limitations of simpler field-line-diffusion proxies. A parallelized Differential Evolution algorithm explores the Chebyshev coefficient space, minimizing a composite objective that simultaneously reduces peak heat flux, promotes uniform heat spreading, and maximizes the fraction of scrape-off-layer power intercepted by the target. Truncating the Chebyshev polynomials to the first three toroidal modes in Z and holding the R coordinates constant, reduces the entire shape of the target surface to a single function Z ( φ ) . This function governs how quickly the surface drains the flux tubes it intersects and the radial width of the footprint. The optimized surface yielded a 24 % improvement in intercepted power, 47 % reduction in peak heat flux and a 71 % increase in the power weighted effective area.

title: Analysis of Xe-131 Prompt Gammas
abstract: The prompt gammas of Xe-131 from thermal neutron capture were measured for the first time at the Fission Product Prompt gamma-ray Spectrometer by irradiation of isotopically enriched Xe-130 in a high-purity quartz ampoule. Through gamma-gamma coincidences, 42 new prompt gammas were measured and 14 new nuclear states determined.
