title: Plasma-modified inelastic electron scattering for Mo 93 m nuclear isomer depletion in warm dense matter
Extended Quantum Diffusion Approach to Capture Reactions with Actinides
abstract: Abstract The Extended Quantum Diffusion Approach (EQDA), incorporating coordinate-dependent friction, is applied to a systematic study of capture cross sections for various projectile-target combinations involving the actinide nuclei ($^{238}$U, $^{244}$Pu, and $^{248}$Cm). For reactions with positive $Q_{2n}$ values, the two-neutron transfer is assumed to occur before capture, leading to an effective post-transfer entrance channel with modified nuclear properties and quadrupole deformations. The calculated excitation functions describe the available experimental data reasonably well down to deep sub-barrier energies, reaching about 15 MeV below the spherical Coulomb barrier. The systematic analysis shows that the sub-barrier slopes of excitation functions are governed by an interplay between nuclear deformation and the dissipative entrance-channel dynamics. The comparison of the initial and effective post-transfer channels illustrates the influence of the adopted effective-channel prescription, including the change in the projectile deformation description, while the comparison with constant friction demonstrates the role of coordinate-dependent dissipation in the deep sub-barrier region.

title: Discovery of a 62 minute Long-period Transient with Near-orthogonal Rotator Geometry
abstract: Abstract We report the serendipitous discovery of the radio long-period transient (LPT) J155543.7−563102 (hereafter LPT J1555−5631) with a period of 62.2 minutes in MeerKAT and ASKAP survey data. The source emitted bright (10–30 mJy), steep-spectrum ( α ∼ −1.5), highly polarized radio pulses during a 15 hr active window in 2022 May, with no other quiescent or pulsed emission detected before or after over ∼5 yr. The mean light curve exhibits two alternating pulses per cycle. A main pulse (MP) and an interpulse (IP) separated by Δ ϕ = 165 . ° 4, with similar amplitudes but different polarization properties: the wider MP (3.9%) is partially linearly and circularly polarized and shows a constant polarization position angle, while the narrow IP (1.1%) is ∼100% circularly polarized. We classify LPT J1555−5631 as a near-orthogonal rotator, for which emission from both magnetic poles is visible during one rotation and the magnetic and rotation axes are almost perpendicular. The 14 . ° 6 deviation from an antipodal separation and the nearly constant polarization position angle suggest that the emission does not arise from the standard dipolar polar-cap geometry of ordinary pulsars, but instead originates within a broader, more complex magnetosphere. The observed properties of LPT J1555−5631 can be accommodated by extended emission regions, and favor coherent emission mechanisms such as the electron cyclotron maser instability, although they do not uniquely determine the progenitor or emission physics. If these inferences apply more broadly to the LPT population, they could account for why their beam widths are decoupled from rotation periods, the prevalence of flat polarization position angles, and may favor an elevated incidence of orthogonal rotators.

title: Optical spectroscopy of 253 , 254 Cf near the N = 152 neutron shell: implications for kilonova spectra
Deep learning tearing mode evolution prediction for instability control
abstract: Abstract To address the general need for control oriented prediction of deleterious m / n = 2/1 tearing mode (TM) evolution in tokamak plasmas, this work develops a data-driven framework and is validated on J-TEXT experimental database. Based on multi-diagnostic histories and future control reference trajectories, including resonant magnetic perturbation (RMP) and electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) references, the framework forecasts the rotating 2/1 TM evolution trajectory over the energy confinement time scale by jointly forecasting the occurrence probability, rotation frequency, and mode amplitude, while locked phases are treated as the termination of the rotating state in the present framework. A sequence based learning model is adopted to capture correlations among diagnostic signals and control references, enabling direct multistep generation of full evolution trajectories for multiple prediction targets in a single forward pass. To help the model form latent representations of the rotating 2/1 TM state, a curriculum learning strategy is employed to guide the model from simpler present window, 2/1 mode identification tasks, to long horizon evolution prediction, which is informative for predicting control relevant transitions. To further evaluate the prediction performance critical for TM suppression involving the appearance and termination of rotating TM states, this research constructed targeted subsets. Finally, the model achieves an AUC of 98.4% on the full test dataset. On targeted subsets, it attains an onset prediction accuracy of 82.87%, and achieves an 11.4% relative improvement in similarity of predicted amplitude evolution trends. Finally, to examine the physical consistency of the model’s response to changes in control references, counterfactual analyses are performed under modified control conditions. The results indicate that the framework is capable of reproducing the corresponding evolution of key parameters of the rotating 2/1 TM state, supporting its potential as a data driven surrogate for future control-oriented studies.

title: Towards a natural language user interface of the ATLAS technical coordination expert system utilising large language models
abstract: Abstract The ATLAS detector at CERN and its supporting infrastructure form a highly complex system. It covers numerous interdependent sub-systems and requires collaboration across a team of multi-disciplinary experts. The ATLAS Technical Coordination Expert System provides an interactive description of the technical infrastructure and enhances its understanding. It features tools to assess the impact of interventions and document expert knowledge. However, the detector's complexity is inevitably reflected in the expert system, making the web-based information retrieval more complex and affecting the user experience. The submission proposes a natural language-based user interface for the Expert System. A large language model is used to interpret user queries and return the responses as human-friendly texts. This paper discusses the key aspects of the system's architecture and model selection, the process for building a domain-specific knowledge base, and evaluates the performance of an initial pilot. The pilot is based on the expected use cases and interactions defined by a range of Expert System users. The pilot interface is evaluated based on the factual correctness, task success and execution time. The results are promising, with a median factual correctness of 100% (percentile 5th=92%) and a median execution time of 7 s. Ultimately, this approach seeks to improve the user experience and increase its usage and impact within the ATLAS collaboration.

title: Upgrades to the National Ignition Facility neutron time-of-flight diagnostic for operation at yields greater than 10 MJ
abstract: The National Ignition Facility (NIF) is reaching MJ fusion yields and has plans to reach tens of MJ. Diagnostic operation at these yields introduces challenges, from detector linearity at high signal levels to increased backgrounds. We present two upgrades to the NIF neutron time-of-flight (nToF) diagnostic suite that will enable measurements at high yields. First, silver neutron attenuators are being installed in the collimated nToF beamlines, reducing neutron flux and maintaining optimal signal-to-background levels. Silver was selected for its smooth neutron transmission cross section and sufficient γ-ray transmission to retain the gamma peak used for hot-spot velocity measurements. Each line-of-sight will have four insertable silver pucks, providing ∼2–20× attenuation of 14 MeV neutrons. Second, microchannel plate (MCP) photomultiplier tubes using Zener diodes to establish constant MCP-to-anode acceleration voltages have been installed in the quartz Cherenkov detectors. These provide stable instrument response functions across large gain ranges and permit operation at MCP gains near unity. The combined upgrades will allow NIF nToFs to function at all projected future yields.

title: Performance evaluation of a D-band (130–170 GHz) heterodyne receiver front-end for radiometric applications
abstract: Abstract The performance of a millimeter-wave radiometer is strongly influenced by the characteristics of its radio-frequency (RF) front-end, making comprehensive experimental characterization essential prior to system deployment. This work presents the characterization methodology and performance evaluation of a commercially available D-band heterodyne receiver front-end operating over the 130–170 GHz frequency range. The study investigates the performance of the principal passive and active microwave components, including IMPATT local oscillators, balanced mixers, high-pass filters, cavity band-pass filters, isolators, directional couplers, and the calibration noise source, followed by evaluation of the integrated receiver front-end and its interface with an 8-channel intermediate-frequency (IF) receiver covering 1–20 GHz. The 130 GHz and 150 GHz IMPATT oscillators were characterized in terms of output power, phase noise, frequency stability, and short-term frequency drift. The balanced mixers exhibited an average conversion loss of approximately 9 dB while providing down-conversion from the 130–170 GHz RF band to a 1–20 GHz IF. Passive microwave components were evaluated through measurements of insertion loss, isolation, coupling characteristics, and transmission response, while a calibrated noise source with manufacturer-specified excess noise ratio (ENR) values was used as part of the receiver characterisation procedure.The complete receiver chain was subsequently validated through RF-to-IF measurements using an 8-channel IF receiver. The experimental results establish the performance of the individual receiver components as well as the integrated front-end architecture, demonstrating its suitability for high-sensitivity millimeter-wave radiometry and electron cyclotron emission diagnostic applications. The characterization methodology presented in this work also provides a practical framework for the evaluation and integration of D-band heterodyne receiver systems.

title: High-energy gamma-ray spectrometry with LYSO:Ce scintillators for fusion plasma experiments
abstract: High-performance gamma-ray spectrometry for fusion plasma diagnostics requires high detection efficiency in the MeV energy range, low pileup losses at high count rates, and an enhanced peak-to-background ratio. These requirements cannot be achieved simultaneously with a single large-volume scintillation detector. To address this limitation, a segmented detector consisting of a stack of three optically isolated lutetium–yttrium oxyorthosilicate doped with cerium scintillation crystals with a silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) readout was developed and tested. Each crystal was equipped with an independent, synchronized readout channel and digitized using a high-speed waveform-acquisition system, enabling operation at count rates of 200 kcps per crystal. Energy was reconstructed using charge integration, whereas event timing was determined using constant-fraction discrimination to enable coincidence measurements. System performance was evaluated using a Ga-66 gamma-ray source that emits multiple lines at energies of up to 5 MeV. A proof-of-principle demonstration of pileup deconvolution was performed using a pattern-based algorithm applied to raw waveforms. The method enabled overlapping events to be identified and reconstructed at a count rate of ∼200 kcps per scintillator. Coincidence selection identified a subset of events corresponding to ∼21% of the 2752 keV full-energy peak counts observed in the individual detector spectra, providing additional information on correlated interactions within the segmented detector. The results demonstrate that detector segmentation, combined with coincidence techniques and pileup deconvolution, enables efficient high-count-rate gamma-ray spectrometry using SiPM-based detectors and offers a promising solution for fusion plasma diagnostics in high-magnetic-field environments.

title: Development of a multi-channel diamond detector array for pulsed deuterium–tritium fusion neutron diagnostics
abstract: With both a fast time response and good energy resolution from the 12C (n, α) 9Be reaction, single crystal chemical vapor deposition diamonds are a valuable tool for measuring neutrons in fusion experiments. To measure both the reaction rate timing and neutron energy spectra at Helion Energy’s Polaris fusion prototype, a 64-channel array of diamond detectors was developed. The large number of channels allows acquisition of spectra with sufficient counting statistics for each 100 μs–1 ms fusion neutron burst from Polaris. We report here the design of the detector array, selection of the preamplifiers, and characterization of the array with neutron sources.

title: Design and characterization of the magnetic proton recoil neutron spectrometer for burning plasma studies on SPARC (invited)
abstract: The SPARC tokamak is expected to robustly enter the burning plasma regime (Q > 5) during deuterium–tritium operations and will provide a unique platform to study novel effects of alpha heating in reactor-relevant plasma scenarios. This article presents the near-final design and characterization of the high-resolution magnetic proton recoil (MPR) neutron spectrometer for SPARC and discusses the opportunities for burning plasma studies enabled by this instrument. The MPR spectrometer will be positioned in the midplane line of sight of the poloidal neutron camera and view SPARC’s core plasma. The as-built instrumental response function is calculated based on measured magnetic fields, which have been optimized to maximize resolution and sensitivity constrained by limited space and power. The spectrometer has variable resolution and sensitivity, with settings ranging from high efficiency (2.22 × 10−6 counts per incident neutron) and low resolution (1070 keV) to low efficiency (1.48 × 10−7 counts per incident neutron) and high resolution (149 keV). We also present kinetic simulations of burning plasma effects, which we use to calculate synthetic neutron spectra to better understand the diagnostic capabilities of the instrument. Based on these simulations, the spectrometer is expected to diagnose core ion temperature with less than 7% uncertainty and time resolution less than 100 ms in break-even campaign experiments. Non-thermal alpha knock-on fusion is found to be a small contribution to overall fusion power; however, it does produce a measurable feature in the neutron spectrum that can be used to evaluate alpha heating and confinement in high-gain scenarios.

title: Technological development and qualification of the HEPD-02 apparatus on board the CSES-02 satellite
abstract: Abstract The China Seismo-Electromagnetic Satellite (CSES) project is aimed at developing a satellite constellation dedicated to the measurement of electric and magnetic fields, plasma currents and particle fluxes in the terrestrial magnetosphere. The first satellite in the series, CSES-01, was launched in 2018 and is still operational. The second satellite, CSES-02, was successfully launched into orbit on 14 June 2025. Within this framework, the Italian Limadou collaboration developed the High-Energy Particle Detector (HEPD) for both missions. This article focuses on the technological development and qualification of the HEPD-02 apparatus, operating on board CSES-02. HEPD-02 is composed of various scintillator detectors and a pixel direction detector, aimed at measuring the energy spectra of charged particles, either incoming or trapped in the terrestrial magnetosphere. It is optimized for the identification of individual electrons with kinetic energies in the range between 3 and 100 MeV, and of protons between 30 and 200 MeV. This paper illustrates instrument and electronics design, outlining the main technological challenges and adopted solutions to ensure the desired operation and performance in the space environment for the expected lifetime of at least 6 years. It also describes the test campaign which was carried out to demonstrate the fulfilment of mechanical, thermal and electromagnetic requirements.

title: Shielding design and construction for the XINGZHI cold neutron triple-axis spectrometer: integrating velocity selector, S-bender polarizer, and neutron guide
abstract: Abstract The optimized design and construction of shielding for the velocity selector, S-bender polarizer, and neutron guide in the XINGZHI cold neutron triple-axis spectrometer have been successfully completed. The challenge of limited space available for XINGZHI has been met by a compact shielding structure, developed through Monte Carlo simulations and realized by purpose-built mechanical design, thus leaving more floor space for the spectrometer. An innovative lead-antimony alloy ensures rigidity for self-support, while optimized tolerances for gaps between mating blocks meet safety, machinability, and mounting requirements. Additionally, a long-distance alignment method has been implemented, facilitating the alternating installation of the neutron guide and shielding system. After six years of operation, this structure has been verified to meet radiation safety standards while maximizing available space, marking a significant advancement in neutron instrumentation in China and offering valuable methodologies for future development.

title: Liquid argon purification and purity monitoring: apparatus and first results
abstract: Abstract We report results from a 13-liter purified liquid argon test stand at Wellesley College in Massachusetts, U.S.A.. The system includes a single-pass liquid-phase purification column that can achieve sub-part-per-billion impurity levels. The liquid argon purity is measured with a double-gridded purity monitor to assess the electron lifetime. Measurements demonstrate an O 2 -equivalent impurity concentration of 0.21 ± 0.05 ppb (stable over a 20-hour duration), corresponding to an electron lifetime of 1.6 ms at a drift field of 500 V/cm. This test stand supports ongoing detector R&D on charge and light readout for liquid argon time projection chambers, such as Q-Pix and other cold electronics systems.

title: The (amide-)N-methylnicotinamide is a microbe-derived NAD + precursor that drives gut stem cell renewal
abstract: Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide (NAD) is a critical cellular coenzyme whose decline associates with various chronic and inflammatory diseases. Improved NAD restoration may reduce disease risks and extend healthy lifespan. We report here that certain commensal bacteria including specific probiotic species produce (amide-)N-methylnicotinamide (N-MNA), which is a structural isomer of methylnicotinamide, a nicotinamide degradative metabolite. Patients with gut dysbiosis and inflammation show reduced stool N-MNA. Stable isotope tracing revealed that N-MNA can be rapidly taken up and incorporated into NAD redox reactions by intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) and non-IECs of fruit fly, mouse, and human. Genetic and pharmacological analyses suggest that N-MNA is converted to NAD + via the Preiss-Handler pathway, independent of the salvage pathway. Cell-type-specific ablation or overexpression of SIRT1, an NAD-consuming enzyme, in Drosophila , along with intestinal stem cell (ISC) lineage tracing in mice revealed that systemic N-MNA supplementation promotes ISC regeneration and gut epithelial repair. Compared to known NAD precursors, N-MNA brings a methyl group into host cells, representing a class of microbe-derived NAD precursor that stimulates the tissue regenerative power.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: Human carotid plaque risk imaging using multiparametric photoacoustic and ultrasound fusion (hCAPRI)
abstract: Assessing the risk of carotid plaque rupture remains limited because current imaging methods cannot provide both plaque composition and structural information in real time. Here, we present human carotid plaque risk imaging (hCAPRI), a multiparametric photoacoustic and ultrasound (PA/US) fusion method for real-time carotid plaque assessment. hCAPRI combines PA imaging for detecting intraplaque hemorrhage (IPH) with US imaging for evaluating the plaque structure. PA imaging measured IPH size and methemoglobin content, while US imaging assessed stenosis severity, calcification, and plaque thickness. Combining these PA/US parameters, we compute an hCAPRI score. In 171 carotid arteries (CAs) from 120 patients, hCAPRI revealed the relationships among the PA/US parameters. In 36 CAs validated with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), hCAPRI showed high agreement with MRI. The hCAPRI score achieved 89% sensitivity and 84% specificity for high-risk plaque classification. hCAPRI offers a low-cost, real-time, and contrast-free approach for carotid plaque risk imaging.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: Constraints on the r -process Delay Time from Dwarf Spheroidal Galaxies
abstract: Abstract The ancient stellar populations and simple structure of the local dwarf spheroidal galaxies (dSphs) make them excellent laboratories for studying the chemical evolution of the early Universe. In this paper, we fit one-zone galactic chemical evolution models to C, Mg, Si, Ca, Fe, Sr, Y, Ba, and Eu abundances in the dSphs Sculptor and Draco. By including the s - and r -processes in our model, we are able to place constraints on the timescale of r -process enrichment in these dSphs. We find that neutron star mergers cannot be the only source of the r -process in Sculptor and Draco, and that a prompt r -process source is required to explain the observed stellar abundances. When neutron star mergers are the only source of the r -process in our models, their minimum delay time must be just 14–16 Myr. The neutron-capture abundances in Sculptor and Draco can also be fit by models with a longer neutron star merger minimum delay time combined with a prompt r -process source that operates on the same timescale as massive star evolution, such as magnetorotational supernovae. Additionally, the Sr and Y abundances in the dSphs set limits on the Sr and Y yields per r -process event. We find that theoretical r -process yields overestimate Sr and Y production by a factor of up to 100.
authors: Mithi A. C. de los Reyes
citation_authors: de los Reyes, Mithi A. C.

title: An (in)complete NIRSpec census of Balmer absorption in Type 1 AGN – radiation-driven outflows in little red dots, quasars and variable stars
abstract: Abstract A notable achievement of the first generation of JWST surveys was the discovery of an abundance of faint high-redshift (z > 4) broad-line active galactic nuclei (AGN) in the Lbol < 1045 erg s−1 regime, previously only accessible at z < 1. The high prevalence of absorption features in their broad hydrogen lines is one of the peculiarities of a significant fraction of this new population. In this paper, we conduct a broad census of Balmer absorption in a sample of 47 Type-1 AGN spanning 2 < z < 7. Accounting for incompleteness of JWST spectroscopic data, we estimate that $44_{-6}^{+21}$ % of Little Red Dots (LRDs) have absorption in Hα while the incidence rate is <25 % (at 2σ) in Little Blue Dots (LBDs). Additionally, R1000 JWST/NIRSpec data is strongly resolution limited, implying an inability to disentangle Doppler broadening in the absorption from optical depth effects. This is alleviated with R2700 observations, although some degeneracies remain. We find a significant correlation between the velocity of the Balmer absorption and the [OIII]5007 narrow line luminosity, suggesting a common driving mechanism. We do not find any other significant correlations (and do not confirm previously claimed correlations) between Balmer absorption and other spectral properties of LRDs (except for the expected correlation between Hα and Hβ absorption velocities). Comparing LRDs, quasars and stellar Hα absorbers, we establish that absorption in both LRDs and broad absorption line quasars is consistent with radiatively driven outflows, echoing the physics of variable stars yet occurring at vastly different scales.
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

title: Broadband non-thermal emission predictions based on 3D simulations of supernova explosions within active galactic nuclei jets
abstract: Context. Thermonuclear and core-collapse supernovae are statistically expected to happen within extragalactic jets, as these jets cross the inner regions of their host galaxies, and supernova ejecta–jet interactions can potentially lead to strong non-thermal activity. Aims. We model the non-thermal emission from a supernova interacting with a jet on kiloparsec scales, using detailed numerical simulations of the interaction. Methods. Using a post-processing method, we applied a non-thermal model of the acceleration and transport of electron and their synchrotron and inverse Compton emissions, simplified and tuned for flexibility and computational speed, to the results of a three-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics simulation of the ejecta of a supernova interacting with an extragalactic jet. Results. For typical magnetic field strengths, a jet power 10 44 erg s −1 , and an electron energy distribution characteristic of diffusive shock acceleration, we predict: synchrotron emission that peaks in X-rays but reaches up to 100 MeV, with an overall luminosity of a few times 10 41 erg s −1 ; and emission from inverse Compton scattering mostly off galactic infrared photons, peaking at ∼1 TeV and with a luminosity up to ∼10 40 erg s −1 . We also computed the evolution of the emission, and the distribution of the flux in the sky at its maximum, for five different energy bands: radio, optical, X-rays, high-energy and very high-energy γ -rays. The emission is roughly steady on a few 1000 yr timescales, with an extension on arcsec scales for a source in the local universe. Conclusions. For intermediate jet powers, radio, optical and X-ray fluxes from supernova ejecta-jet interactions may be detectable for distances ≲100 Mpc. The non-thermal luminosity budget and local conditions associated with these interactions could be enough to explain knots seen in kiloparsec scale jets at different energies. These conditions might also be suitable for the production of heavy ultra high-energy cosmic rays, but photon and neutrino generation from hadronic processes would be minor on kiloparsec scales. The leptonic γ -ray fluxes are modest but might non-negligibly contribute in TeV for the nearest or more powerful jet sources.

title: Realizing uniform implosion of double-cone ignition by combining a predictive model and Bayesian optimization
abstract: Abstract The direct-drive inertial confinement fusion schemes like the double-cone ignition (DCI) scheme can efficiently utilize the laser energy, while it faces significant challenges in uniform implosion and achieving high areal density of the fuel. This is because of the P2 asymmetry driven by the laser and the high-mode Rayleigh–Taylor instability (RTI) growth. We propose an efficient optimization approach by integrating multiple algorithms and physical models to address these limitations. Based on two-dimensional (2D) radiation hydrodynamics simulations, a scaling law for the areal density is derived, incorporating laser parameters, target structure, and instability factors, all of which have significant effects on the areal density. The particle swarm optimization algorithm is employed to optimize the irradiation positions and spot radius of the two-ring laser, improving the uniformity of laser intensity distribution on the target surface and thus reducing the P2 asymmetry. Combining one-dimensional simulations with the RTI growth theory, a quantitative predictive model for P2 asymmetry and a qualitative predictive model for high-mode RTI are established, significantly reducing computational costs. Finally, the outputs of the predictive models are used as input parameters to perform Bayesian optimization for iteratively optimizing laser profile and target structure. The areal density of the DCI in 2D simulations increases from 0.156 to 0.274 g cm − 2 with 2 × 16 kJ drive lasers. This method provides a new paradigm for the experimental design of DCI and polar direct-drive scheme.

title: Effects of uniaxial strain and free hydrogen/helium atoms on helium bubble coalescence in tungsten divertor
abstract: Abstract Tungsten (W) is a preferred plasma-facing material for fusion reactor divertors. During service, high heat loads induce considerable thermal strain, while large amounts of free hydrogen (H) and helium (He) atoms accumulate in the W matrix. These factors promote the nucleation and coalescence of near-surface He bubbles, affecting the service safety of plasma-facing components and the transport behavior of hydrogen isotopes. However, the combined effects of strain and free H/He atoms on He bubble coalescence in W remain unclear. This work employs molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to systematically investigate the mechanisms by which uniaxial strain and free H/He atoms affect He bubble coalescence in W. The analysis is further combined with the thermal strain characteristics of divertor service conditions and the equilibrium pressure behavior of He bubbles. The results show that both tensile and compressive strains promote He bubble coalescence, while compressive strain has a stronger effect. Tensile strain facilitates bubble expansion by reducing the local atomic density, whereas compressive strain increases the internal He bubble pressure and accelerates He bubble connection. In H-containing systems, H concentration shows a dual effect: low H concentration promotes coalescence, whereas high H concentration suppresses it due to competition for defect sites around He bubbles. In H–He coexisting systems, free He atoms form He or H–He clusters, which redistribute H atoms and reduce H adsorption by pre-existing He bubbles. A modified equilibrium-pressure relation was further introduced to describe strain-assisted He bubble coalescence. These results provide atomic-scale insight into He bubble evolution in divertor W under complex service conditions.

title: A study of the influence of prolonged baking on deuterium depth distribution and release in JET ILW components
abstract: Abstract Samples of JET ILW divertor and limiter tiles extracted from JET after the third ILW campaign underwent baking at elevated temperatures (350°C and 240°C, respectively) for 60-140 hours, to simulate the effects of baking as previously planned for ITER divertor and first wall. A combination of thermal desorption spectroscopy (TDS) and ion beam analysis (IBA) was used to characterize the dynamics of deuterium outgassing during baking and the resulting changes in deuterium depth distribution. It is shown that deuterium release during baking follow a power law time dependence with the average power law exponent of ~0.85 for divertor samples and ~0.68 for limiter ones. For divertor samples the average total fuel removal efficiency is ~47.5% and the near-surface one is ~21%, while for limiter samples they are ~3.8% and 97%, respectively. Spatial redistribution of deuterium during prolonged baking is demonstrated. The combination of TDS and IBA reveal a fundamental difference in deuterium redistribution behaviour between divertor and limiter baking conditions, with predominant diffusion towards the surface followed by desorption in the former and predominant inward diffusion in the latter. Possible promotion of fuel outgassing by a loose morphology of thick co-deposit layers is also observed.

title: Background of the BULLKID detector array operated with a moderate shield on the surface
abstract: We present the operation with moderate radiation shield in a surface laboratory of BULky and Low-threshold Kinetic Inductance Detector) (BULLKID), a cryogenic detector for searches of light dark matter or coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering. The detector consists of an array of 60 cubic silicon particle absorbers of 0.34 g each, sensed by cryogenic kinetic inductance detectors. The analysis presented focuses on data from 15 elements of the array, with two central units used to evaluate the background and with their surrounding elements used as veto. The low energy spectrum resulting from an exposure of 290 hours to ambient backgrounds, acquired with the use of external and internal radiation shields, is compatible with the simulations at the level of ( 6.8 ± 0.4 stat . ± 0.1 syst . ) × 10 4 counts / keV kg days from 2 keV down to an energy of 600 eV. The region between 225 eV and 600 eV shows a rise in background in disagreement with the simulations, while not sharing some of the key traits of the low energy excess observed in other cryogenic experiments. The high energy spectrum shape is in overall agreement with the simulations and displays the typical particle-induced x-ray emission of the surrounding lead.

title: Physical design of a high-charge beam injector for the on-axis swap-out injection scheme in an electron-positron collider
abstract: The Super Tau-Charm Facility (STCF), a next-generation electron-positron collider, adopts an on-axis swap-out injection scheme that demands high-charge electron bunches with exceptionally low emittance and minimal energy spread. This work presents a comprehensive and systematic beam dynamics design for the STCF electron injector. The bunching system, based on subharmonic bunchers and a traveling-wave buncher, is optimized using the nondominated sorting genetic algorithm III to efficiently explore the high-dimensional parameter space. Start-to-end simulations incorporating space-charge forces, wakefield effects, and alignment errors are performed, with beam-based alignment (BBA) applied to correct orbit deviations. The optimized injector delivers 8.5 nC bunches at 3.5 GeV with a normalized transverse emittance below 70 mm mrad and an rms energy spread below 0.5%, satisfying the stringent STCF requirements. The high transport efficiency achieved in simulations alleviates the design pressure on the electron source, while the excellent beam quality inherently suppresses beam halo effects. By integrating systematic multiobjective optimization with high-fidelity simulations, the proposed design overcomes the intrinsic limitations of thermionic cathodes while capitalizing on their proven stability, robustness, and cost-effectiveness, offering an efficient engineering solution for high-charge beam delivery in next-generation colliders.

title: Testing Exact Anisotropic Bianchi Type-V Cosmology in $f(T)$ Gravity with Cosmic Chronometers
abstract: Abstract Anisotropic cosmologies in modified gravity are useful only when exactsolvability is accompanied by isotropization, viable matter properties, andan acceptable mean expansion history. We examine these requirements forBianchi type-V cosmology in $f(T)$ gravity with a comoving perfect-fluid source. Within the pure-tetrad formulation, thefield equations select a linear torsion sector yielding three exactpower-law solution classes. We also derive the covarianttetrad-spin-connection equations, including the off-diagonal constraints.The $n>0$, $n\neq3$ anisotropic family satisfies the covariant compatibilityconditions in the linear, GR-equivalent sector, while the $n=0$ ansatzadmits an isotropically expanding solution with $K=0$ and unrestricted$l>0$. In the nonlinear isotropic sector, we reconstruct $f(T)$parametrically for general $n$ and obtain an explicit nonlinear functionfor $n=1$, without assuming its functional form.For the three pure-tetrad classes, we analyze the directionalHubble rates, mean expansion, shear, normalized anisotropy, deceleration andjerk parameters, reconstructed density, pressure, equation of state, andenergy conditions. Interestingly, only the first class approaches anisotropic matter-like regime, with decaying shear and normalized anisotropyand a mean expansion approaching matter-era behavior. Comparison with 33cosmic-chronometer measurements shows that this class reproduces thequalitative increase of $H(z)$ with redshift, but its law$H(z)=H_0(1+z)^{3/2}$ is too rigid for the late-time expansion history; thefixed-$\Omega_m$ flat $\Lambda$CDM model provides a better fit. Moreover, thereconstructed matter sector admits positive-density regions satisfying thenull and dominant energy conditions, while the strong energy condition isviolated for the representative positive-coupling choice. The remainingclasses expand too slowly and retain finite normalized anisotropy.In the isotropic Bianchi type-V limit, we further obtainan exact parametric reconstruction of nonlinear $f(T)$models, including an explicit functional form in the$n=1$ branch.

title: Spectroscopic quantities (ANC, SF) for the configuration 12 B→ 11 B + n from nucleon transfer reactions
abstract: The differential cross sections of the neutron transfer in the 11 B(d,p) 12 B reaction were measured at a deuteron energy of 14.5 MeV. These data were analyzed within the framework of a Modified Distorted-Wave Method. The values of the asymptotic normalization coefficients for the 12 B → 11 B + n configuration when the 12 B nucleus is formed in the ground (1 + ), excited 0.953 MeV (2 + ), 1.674 MeV (2 - ), 2.621 MeV (1 - ) and 2.723 MeV (0 + ) states were obtained.

title: Phase-resolved X-ray spectroscopy of the Vela pulsar with NICER observations
abstract: PSR J0835-4510 (the Vela pulsar) is the best studied pulsar in the southern hemisphere given its high radio brightness and large glitch activity. However, its X-ray brightness is lower, making the study of its X-ray profile difficult. We aim to investigate the X-ray emission of the Vela pulsar coming from the surface of the neutron star to infer the properties of its hotspots and assess whether they share a common spectral shape. We also aim to prove whether the 2021 glitch affected the hotspots. We used an ephemeris obtained from high-cadence radio observations with the radio telescopes of the Argentine Institute of Radio Astronomy to combine all the observations of the Vela pulsar after its 2019 glitch and before its 2024 glitch. We obtained a folded pulse profile for three different energy ranges and subsequently studied their phase-resolved energy spectra. We additionally analyzed a observation to quantify the pulsar's contribution to the total soft X-ray emission detected by , which cannot spatially resolve the pulsar from the surrounding pulsar wind nebula (PWN). NICER Chandra NICER The pulsar contribution to the total observed emission represents less than 40–45% of the flux below 0.9 keV, dropping to 3–4% in the 0.9--2.0 keV range and further down to ∼2% above 2 keV, where the PWN fully dominates. We find that the X-ray folded profile of the Vela pulsar was not measurably perturbed by the 2021 glitch. We studied seven regions of the pulse profile separately. We found that all of them are well modeled by one or two blackbodies. The temperatures of these hotspots are between 0.79(7) , łeq T łeq 4.8^ 10^ 6 K +0.8 _ -0.6 10^ 6 , , while their sizes vary between 0.048^ K +0.016 _ -0.009 , łeq R łeq 3.9^ km +0.9 _ -0.6 , , and their luminosities between 5 km 30 erg s^ -1 łesssim L < 1 32 erg s^ -1 .

title: Neutron star-companion interaction in core-collapse supernovae. Population synthesis based on detailed binary evolution models
abstract: Most massive stars live in binary systems. When the first supernova in a binary occurs, the ejecta hit the companion, which may inflate as a consequence, and then interact with the newly formed compact object. The recent Type Ic supernova shows a periodic modulation in its emission, which is interpreted as evidence of such interaction. 2022jli We derive predictions for the occurrence rate and observables of supernovae exhibiting these compact object--companion interactions (CCIs). We analyzed a comprehensive state-of-the-art grid of detailed binary stellar evolution models and implemented analytic prescriptions for the expansion of the companion star following its interaction with the supernova ejecta. We then employed the newly developed population synthesis code to derive the distribution functions of the properties of the supernovae affected by CCI and their companions, where we used different explodability and neutron star birth-kick distributions. SN-ORACLE We find that periodic CCI is expected to occur in more than half of the binary systems that produce a hydrogen-poor core-collapse supernova and are not disrupted, while the occurrence rate in systems producing hydrogen-rich supernovae is small. We found broad period ranges, peaking around 20-50 with the interaction lasting for 0.5-10 , , and . The inflation of the companion also increases their luminosity and brightness, increasing their detectability with current instruments. For , our best-fitting models predict a J-band magnitude of 21-23 for up to sim10 We identified specific binary evolution models that reproduce the observed period of the light curve undulations of 2022jli 2015ap 2022esa 2022jli We find that up to sim27% of H-poor supernovae could show periodicity in their light curves, while only a few such events have been identified so far. Our results may help identify periodic CCI features in future and archival supernova observations.

title: Contributions of massive stars and classical novae to Galactic Al 26
abstract: The radioactive isotope is believed to be mainly produced by massive stars and ejected into the interstellar medium through their winds and supernovae. Due to its lifetime of 1.04,Myr, it traces recent nucleosynthesis and star formation. The isotope Al 26 Fe 60 is similarly long-lived, with a lifetime of 3.8,Myr, and originates only in core-collapse supernovae (ccSNe). Stellar evolution models in combination with Galactic chemical evolution (GCE) models tend to over-predict the nuc Fe 60 / ratio. Population synthesis models that attempt to explain both the mass in the entire Milky Way and its spatial distribution through comparisons with the 1.8,MeV decay γ-ray line match the observational constraints only with an enhanced star formation rate (SFR) of ≳ 5, . Classical novae may contribute significantly to the production, potentially lowering the SFR inferred from massive stars, although previous studies suggest that their contribution is negligible or łeq,10%. However, a large nova contribution would also alleviate some tension in the Al 26 Al 26 -1 Al 26 Fe 60 / ratio. Al 26 In this work we aim to determine the mass distribution of as a function of the Galactocentric radius and estimate the contribution of (very) massive stars and classical novae to the 1.8 ,MeV signal. Al 26 We used 20,yr of INTEGRAL/SPI observations of the γ-ray line at 1.8, and compare the resulting mass distribution with different GCE models. to test different assumptions about the radial structure of Al 26 In our baseline analysis, all tested source models favour substantial nova contributions, with best-fit fractions of 77--84%. Because the nova and massive-star amplitudes are anti-correlated, the full two-parameter 2σ confidence regions permit substantially smaller nova fractions. The preferred large nova contribution alleviates tension in the / ratio and lowers the SFR from γ-ray measurements to 1--2, . Fe 60 Al 26 Al 26 -1 Our baseline fits favour a substantial contribution from classical novae, but the quantitative lower bound depends strongly on the adopted source profile and on the treatment of the Solar neighbourhood. Under some tested assumptions, the data allow little or no nova contribution at the 2σ level. Although it is difficult to gauge both contributions directly, next generation MeV telescopes may be able to identify individual massive stars, such as γ^2-Velorum.

title: A0538-66: A transient ultraluminous X-ray source with a relativistic outflow, 69 ms pulsations, and anomalous optical activity
abstract: A0538–66 is a peculiar Be/X-ray binary in the Large Magellanic Cloud, hosting the fastest spinning neutron star of its class (∼69 ms) and showing the brightest optical bursts of any system of this type. We report four XMM-Newton observations obtained near periastron in 2025, together with MAXI and REM monitoring, and a reanalysis of archival RXTE data. On 30 September 2025 the source reached L X ≈ 1.5 × 10 39 erg s −1 (0.2–10 keV), the highest level since 1980, and in February, May, and August 2026, MAXI detected similarly bright outbursts. During the XMM-Newton observation taken on 30 September 2025, we detected the pulsations, measuring P spin = 69.25878(2) ms and Ṗ spin = 6.58(9) × 10 −10 s s −1 ; the pulsed fraction was low (≈3% in 1–10 keV), increased with energy, and the soft and hard pulse profiles were shifted by half a cycle. A new detection in RXTE data of 3 December 1998 gives a faster spin period of P = 68.88813(28) ms. The XMM-Newton /RGS spectra show emission lines from photoionised plasma at rest and blueshifted absorption lines that imply an outflow at ∼0.12 c . This indicates a highly super-Eddington accretion rate and an intrinsic L X ≈ 1.5 × 10 39 erg s −1 , and it makes A0538–66 a transient ultra-luminous X-ray pulsar, a class of which only a few objects are known so far. Since 2023 the optical bursts observed by REM have become longer and brighter, resembling those of the 1980s, but most of them lack a luminous X-ray counterpart ( L X > 10 37 erg s −1 ). We interpret these results in terms of a radiation pressure dominated accretion disc whose geometrically thick inner regions intermittently screen the innermost emitting regions.

title: Development of an attention aware multimodal network for the identification of internal reconnection events in LTX-β
abstract: Abstract We present the IRE Identification Multimodal Network (IIMN), a classifier to automatically detectInternal Reconnection Events (IREs) in spherical tokamaks. The IIMN utilizes data from the LithiumTokamak eXperiment-β (LTX-β), a low-aspect-ratio spherical tokamak capable of operating withwalls coated in solid or liquid lithium. As a multimodal network, the IIMN is well-suited to handlingcomplex, multi-dimensional relationships among both image and tabular data. To train the model,7,265 events from 2,968 shots were manually reviewed and labeled, covering nearly two years ofdiagnostic data from LTX-β. Each event includes key plasma parameters in identifying IREs like thetime evolutions of the plasma current, average electron density, and Mirnov spectrogram. The modelconcatenates the results from a multilayer perceptron branch and a convolutional neural network(CNN) branch to return a one-hot encoded output that determines if the event is an IRE or not basedon the event’s plasma parameters. We show that the IIMN has an accuracy of 94.4±0.9%, a precisionscore of 0.934±0.014, and a recall score of 0.931±0.014. IIMN is fully automated such that it could beused quickly and easily by operators in the control room for spherical tokamak operation. To realizefull automation and zero human intervention, our current multimodal architecture incorporates aCNN that directly analyzes image-based data from select plasma diagnostics. By automating IREdetection, this tool can assist operators in monitoring fusion performance and developing strategiesto reduce confinement losses even in between two successive plasma discharges.

title: Weak charged current induced electron and positron scattering off proton at JLab and MAMI energies
abstract: Abstract The development of next-generation, high-luminosity, and high-precision charged-lepton beam facilities at JLab and MAMI has opened, in recent years, a new frontier in the exploration of weak interaction processes induced by electrons and positrons in the neutral current sector, which can also be used to study weak interaction processes induced by charged currents. In particular, these processes in the intermediate energy regime play a crucial role in understanding electroweak dynamics, nucleon structure, and hadronic response functions. In this review, we present a comprehensive analysis of some of the electron induced weak CC processes on the free proton due to quasielastic scattering channels. We also study the inelastic production of spin 1/2 and 3/2 resonances, as well as the inelastic production of η and K mesons, and the associated particle production of strange particles in electron and positron induced weak CC processes on free proton. Furthermore, in the quasielastic scattering sector, the polarization observables of the produced baryons as well as the possibility of using a polarized proton target, where spin asymmetries may be observed are investigated, highlighting their sensitivity to the underlying weak interaction dynamics. This review provides essential theoretical benchmarks for interpreting precision measurements of various observables in the electron and positron interaction with the proton target in the few-GeV energy domain of weak interaction physics in the charged current sector, directly relevant to the present and future experiments at JLab and MAMI. Beyond its phenomenological relevance, the explored kinematic region offers a unique and independent opportunity to constrain the axial vector sector of the weak interaction. In particular, it provides a discussion of alternative ways to determine MA in the quasielastic scattering region and the axial vector form factors in resonance excitations, free from the uncertainties present in their determination from the study of (anti)neutrino-induced weak processes.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Analysis of yield degradation in OMEGA-relevant cryogenic ICF implosions by multi-ion kinetic effects using Fokker–Planck simulations
abstract: Multi-ion kinetic effects have previously been shown to degrade neutron yield in gas-filled targets at the OMEGA laser facility, but their role in cryogenic implosions remains poorly understood. Using the Vlasov–Fokker–Planck code iFP, developed at Los Alamos National Laboratory, we simulate OMEGA-relevant deuterium–tritium (DT) cryogenic implosions during the deceleration phase to investigate the influence of multi-ion kinetic physics on fusion yield. Simulations were performed using individual DT ion distribution functions, along with average-ion equivalents, to isolate multi-ion kinetic contributions. Evidence of ion-temperature separation and density stratification is observed within the peak neutron-production regions; however, the resulting yield reduction is found to be negligible and below the measurable uncertainty on OMEGA.

title: Bag Parameters for Heavy Meson Lifetimes from a Lattice QCD Calculation at the SU ( 3 ) F -symmetric Point
abstract: We calculate the dimension-six Δ Q = 0 four-quark matrix elements describing heavy-meson lifetime ratios using the gradient flow with its short flow-time expansion (SFTX) as a renormalization procedure. On six RBC/UKQCD 2 + 1 -flavor domain-wall fermion ensembles, we determine flowed bag parameters for physical charm and strange quarks and match to the MS ¯ scheme with perturbative SFTX coefficients through next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO). A multiscale matching procedure using renormalization-group running improves the extrapolation to zero flow time. For the operators relevant to τ ( D s ) / τ ( D 0 ) at the SU ( 3 ) F symmetric point, we obtain B 1 MS ¯ ( 3 GeV ) = 1.0524 ( 97 ) , B 2 MS ¯ ( 3 GeV ) = 0.9621 ( 70 ) , ε 1 MS ¯ ( 3 GeV ) = − 0.2275 ( 76 ) , and ε 2 MS ¯ ( 3 GeV ) = − 0.0005 ( 8 ) using a specific choice of evanescent operators. This is the first lattice-QCD determination of Δ Q = 0 four-quark operators with a full error budget. It opens the path toward higher-precision predictions of heavy-meson lifetimes and similar quantities exhibiting operator mixing under renormalization.

title: Theoretical Study of i -process Contribution to the Post-AGB Star IRAS 14325-6428
abstract: Abstract The post-asymptotic giant branch (post-AGB) star IRAS 14325-6428 exhibits a peculiar heavy-element abundance pattern, characterized by a high [Ba/La] ratio and an anomalous odd-isotope Ba ratio ( f odd,Ba = 0.25 ± 0.08), which is difficult to explain via the classical slow neutron-capture process ( s -process). We theoretically investigate this abundance pattern by considering the intermediate neutron-capture process ( i -process) nucleosynthesis. The i -process nucleosynthesis calculations are performed with a one-zone network (NucNet Tools) at constant temperature and density, using intershell abundances obtained from a stellar model (1.5 M ⊙ , Z = 0.003) evolved with MESA to the thermally pulsing AGB phase. The observed heavy-element abundances are best reproduced by a model with neutron density N n = 5 × 10 13 cm −3 and neutron exposure τ = 1.4 mbarn −1 , followed by dilution with a scaled-solar composition. This model reproduces the high [Ba/La] and [Ba/Ce] ratios and yields a postdilution odd-isotope fraction f odd,Ba ≈ 0.51, which is supported by the observed value being substantially above the expectations of the pure s -process. The abundance pattern arises from the i -process path approaching the neutron magic number N = 82, where the flow slows, and the material accumulates at 135 I, which subsequently β − decays to 135 Ba, enhancing Ba production and reducing the synthesis of heavier species. Combined with its multielement i -process classification, our results provide quantitative support for a dominant i -process origin of the heavy elements in IRAS 14325−6428, likely triggered by a relatively short-lived proton-ingestion episode in its AGB progenitor.

title: Ab initio calculations of Th 229 band-to-band internal conversion rate in ThO 2 229
abstract: We present an ab initio calculation of the band-to-band internal-conversion rate of the $\hbar\omega_{\rm nuc} \approx 8.35$ eV isomeric transition in $^{229}$ThO$_2$. Because the nuclear transition energy exceeds the electronic band gap of ThO$_2$, the isomer can decay nonradiatively by resonantly promoting a valence electron into the conduction band. We formulate this process as a Brillouin-zone sum over vertical interband transitions weighted by local Th-centered hyperfine matrix elements, which are evaluated directly from all-electron full-potential linearized augmented-plane-wave Bloch spinors. A finite nuclear magnetization model is included to regularize the short-range hyperfine interaction and to account for the Bohr-Weisskopf effect. After applying scissor shifts to span the experimentally reported ThO$_2$ band gaps, we find calculated internal-conversion lifetimes in the range of $1-16~\mu{\rm s}$. The lifetime increases strongly as the band gap approaches $\omega_{\rm nuc}$ because the resonant interband phase space at the nuclear transition energy is reduced. For the larger reported ThO$_2$ gaps, the calculated lifetime is comparable to the measured conversion-electron M\"ossbauer lifetime [Nature 648, 300 (2025)]. Our analysis implies that choosing solid-state hosts with band-gap values slightly lower than $\omega_{\rm nuc}$ can optimize solid-state nuclear clock performance with internal-conversion electron readout.

title: Suppression of heavy-ion fusion by slow quasifission
abstract: Heavy-element synthesis hinges on the formation of a compound nucleus --- a fully equilibrated amalgam of the projectile and target nuclei --- but quasifission, a fast reseparation process, can prevent this outcome. Using the SOLITAIRE separator to directly count evaporation residues from reactions forming ${}^{220}$Th, this work shows that fusion can be suppressed by more than 50% even when the classic fingerprint of quasifission --- a correlation between fragment mass and emission angle --- is completely absent. Instead, a subtle broadening of the fission mass distribution is observed that points to slow quasifssion as an explanation for the suppression - a feature whose significance becomes clear only alongside the evaporation residue measurements.

title: Strong-gain water-window X-ray laser driven by plasma photocathode wakefield acceleration
abstract: Abstract X-ray free-electron lasers are large and complex machines, limited by electron beam brightness. Here we show through start-to-end simulations how to realise compact, robust and tunable X-ray lasers in the water window, based on ultra-bright electron beams from plasma wakefield accelerators. First, an ultra-low-emittance electron beam is released by a plasma photocathode in a metre-scale plasma wakefield accelerator. By tuning the beam charge, space-charge forces create a balance between beam fields and wakefields that reduces beam energy spread and improves energy stability – both critical for beam extraction, transport, and focusing into a metre-scale undulator. Here, the resulting ultra-bright beams produce wavelength-tunable, coherent, femtosecond-scale photon pulses at strong gain. This regime enables reliable generation of multi-gigawatt-class X-ray laser pulses across the water window, offering tunability via the witness beam charge and robustness against variations in plasma wakefield strength and plasma photocathode laser jitter. Our findings help democratise access to coherent, high-power, soft X-ray radiation.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Adapting the barrier distribution and synthesizing superheavy nuclei through 50 Ti- and 54 Cr-induced fusion reactions
Heavy Quark Transport Is Non-Gaussian beyond Leading Logarithm
abstract: We find that heavy quark transport beyond leading logarithm at weak coupling is intrinsically non-Gaussian: the longitudinal momentum transfer distribution has that are crucial for equilibration dynamics. We show this by computing the leading-order momentum transfer kernel for relativistic heavy quarks in weakly coupled non-Abelian plasmas, matching perturbative momentum transfer on the thermal scale to hard-thermal-loop-resummed soft physics. This is the same structure previously found in strongly coupled holographic plasmas, showing that it is not peculiar to weak or strong coupling, conformality, or supersymmetry. We therefore expect that this is a robust feature that physical quark-gluon plasma should also exhibit.

title: Glacial abrupt transitions in ocean circulation were much slower than ice-core records imply
abstract: Dansgaard-Oeschger (DO) events during the last ice age are thought to reflect rapid shifts in the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC). Greenland ice cores suggest warming transitions within only a few decades—or even just over 10 years. Using precisely dated speleothem oxygen-isotope records from the Asian monsoon region, we have shown that the same DO warmings unfolded over more than a century. Isotope modeling revealed that Greenland records primarily capture a rapid atmospheric reorganization triggered by the initial sea-ice retreat in the northeastern North Atlantic, whereas the parallel AMOC recovery and hemispheric thermal adjustment proceeded much more slowly. These findings reveal that natural AMOC transitions evolved more slowly than the rapid North Greenland oxygen-isotope shifts would imply, thereby refining our understanding of “abruptness” during DO events.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: Study of the shape coexistence in the 96 Zr, 96 Mo, 96 Ru isobars
abstract: Abstract Three stable isobars, 96 40 Zr 56 , 96 42 Mo 54 and 96 44 Ru 52 , which are in the vicinity of the harmonic oscillator proton shell closure Z = 40 and the spin-orbit neutron shell closure N = 50, are investigated for the presence of the shape coexistence and mixing phenomena. The ground state deformation of these isobars is extracted from the potential energy surface determined with the covariant density functional theory using a density-dependent point-coupling interaction, while the excited states are described involving the Bohr-Mottelson Hamiltonian with octic potential for both axially symmetric and γ-unstable quadrupole deformations. Within the broader view of the two approaches, the obtained results clearly highlight the significant contribution of these phenomena to the structure of the states of these nuclei.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Goldstone theory of gluon saturation in high energy QCD: From color glass to color superfluid condensate
abstract: In the high energy Regge asymptotics of QCD, the rapid overpopulation of gluons leads to gluon saturation, characterized by nonperturbative semi-classical lumpy configurations of size $1/Q_S$, where $Q_S\gg \Lambda_{\rm QCD}$ is a dynamical semi-hard saturation scale. We discuss here a generalization of the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) framework describing this phenomenon that is obtained by carefully treating the breaking of global symmetries by the condensate. In particular, we show that the breaking of a global subgroup of color results in a Goldstone effective field theory (EFT) whose dynamics is characterized by a Goldstone decay constant $f_G = \sqrt{N} Q_S$, where $N=O(1/\alpha_S)$ is the phase space occupancy of the condensate, which is large for $\alpha_S(Q_S)\ll 1$. Further, the coupling of these colored Goldstones to collinear gluon modes leads to a depletion of the condensate, thereby modifying the static shockwave scattering framework of the CGC on timescales controlled by $f_G$. The CGC EFT on these longer time scales is a novel color superfluid. Low frequency modes with $\omega\leq \alpha_S Q_S$ in an external probe of the CGC are sensitive to superfluid dynamics, with interesting physical consequences for deeply inelastic scattering and ultrarelativistic nuclear collisions.

title: Quantum computing for high energy nuclear physics
abstract: Quantum information science (QIS) offers a new set of conceptual and computational tools ideally suited to exploring the many-body, out-of-equilibrium, and real-time properties of strongly interacting quantum systems. These themes find a natural counterpart in high energy nuclear physics, whose central goal is to describe the properties of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), the theory of the strong interaction, under extreme conditions. Relevant examples range from the formation and internal structure of hadrons, to the collective and thermalization dynamics of strongly interacting QCD matter, and the properties of complex many-body scattering processes. Although tremendous progress has been made over the past decades in our understanding of QCD in the nuclear physics context, through perturbative methods, lattice QCD, and effective theory descriptions, phenomena that are intrinsically connected to real-time dynamics, highly entangled many-body evolution, or finite density regimes remain only partially accessible with existing approaches. In this article, we argue that QIS can help realize a new paradigm for addressing these open questions. With the aim of making the discussion accessible to both high energy nuclear physics and QIS audiences, we provide an overview of selected open problems in high energy nuclear physics, with emphasis on aspects motivated by collider phenomenology, and discuss how they can be approached using QIS tools. This connection is illustrated through representative examples drawn from the recent literature, making the case that QIS can become a driving force for discovery in nuclear physics in the coming years.

title: Efficiency measurements of GEM GE1/1 chambers in the upgraded CMS Endcap Muon System using 2023 collision data at √( s ) = 13.6 TeV
abstract: Abstract The CMS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider employs Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) detectors, a technology based on gaseous ionization, as one of the muon detectors. The muon spectrometer is being upgraded to handle the increased muon flux in the forward region. This study analyzes muon detection efficiency in the GE1/1 triple-GEM detector, using 2023 proton-proton collision data at √( s ) = 13.6 TeV. A dataset enriched with muons from Z boson decay, with a total recorded luminosity of 17.8 fb -1 has been used for this study. The detection efficiency of 137 GEM detectors are measured using muon trajectories established using other detectors in the tracking and muon systems, without use of the GEM detectors. The average efficiency of 137 GEM detectors is ∼ 93.3%. A subset of 108 detectors that had no shorts were operated at the nominal HV working point with average efficiency of ∼ 96%. Efficiency is found to be unaffected by the number of p-p interactions per bunch crossing (pile-up).

title: Effects of in-medium $NN$ inelastic cross sections and the high-momentum tail of nucleon momentum distributions on pion production in heavy-ion collisions
abstract: Pion production in intermediate-energy heavy-ion collisions (HICs) provides a sensitive probe of the nuclear equation of state and of the isospin dependence of reaction dynamics. In particular, pion production near threshold is strongly affected by the nucleon-nucleon ($NN$) inelastic cross sections and by the high-momentum components of the nucleon momentum distribution. To explore the influence of these two ingredients on pion production and charged-pion ratios, the in-medium $NN$ inelastic cross sections calculated within the relativistic Boltzmann-Uehling-Uhlenbeck transport theory and the short-range correlation induced high-momentum tail (HMT) are introduced into the Ultra-relativistic Quantum Molecular Dynamics model. By simulating Au+Au collisions at intermediate energies, we find that the in-medium modification of the $NN$ inelastic cross sections suppresses the pion multiplicity by reducing the probability of $N\Delta$ production in dense matter. The HMT, on the other hand, enhances the high-momentum components of nucleons and modifies the available energy in individual $NN$ collisions, thereby affecting $NN\rightarrow N\Delta$ reactions and the subsequent pion production. With the simultaneous inclusion of these two effects, the pion yields and the $\pi^-/\pi^+$ ratio data can be better reproduced. These results highlight the importance of both the in-medium reaction cross sections and short-range correlation induced high-momentum components in pion production in intermediate energy HICs.

title: Search for the 229Pa Parity Doublet via Internal-Conversion Spectroscopy at FRIB
abstract: The radioisotope $^{229}$Pa is predicted to possess a nearly degenerate ground-state parity doublet. Previous $\gamma$-ray and conversion-electron spectroscopy suggests a splitting of $\Delta E = (60\pm 50)~\mathrm{eV}$, although the doublet's existence remains unconfirmed. Such a small splitting would give $^{229}$Pa an exceptionally large enhancement of symmetry-violating nuclear properties. However, the splitting, and with it the sensitivity of $^{229}$Pa to CP-violating physics, remains uncertain by orders of magnitude. We propose an experiment to measure this splitting with sub-eV precision within a few days of measurement time by using delayed-coincidence internal-conversion spectroscopy of $^{229}$Pa ions produced by the electron-capture decay of $^{229}$U$^{+}$ ions stored in a Penning trap at the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB). This measurement would provide the key nuclear-structure input needed to establish $^{229}$Pa as a leading candidate for next-generation atomic and molecular electric-dipole-moment (EDM) experiments.

title: Experimental Characterization of Bulk Micromegas for Development of Active Target Time Projection Chamber for Nuclear Astrophysics Studies
abstract: A Micromegas-based active target Time Projection Chamber, namely Saha Active Target TPC (SAT-TPC), is under development at Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics for its application in nuclear astrophysics experiment to measure the branching ratio of the direct and sequential decay of the Hoyle state of $^{12}$C. A bulk Micromegas was characterized to optimize its operating parameters and its performance for $\alpha$-particle tracking was investigated using gas mixtures Ar + CO$_{2}$ (90:10) and Ar + i-C$_4$H$_{10}$ (95:5) at atmospheric pressure using 5.9~keV X-ray and 5.48~MeV $\alpha$-particles from radioactive sources. A hydrodynamic transport model was used to simulate the charge-deposit profile of the $\alpha$-particle track on the Micromegas readout and compared to the experimental data to complement the experimental measurement as well as validate the numerical model. A good agreement was observed that confirmed the suitability of the choice of the bulk Micromegas in the development of the SAT-TPC prototype and the hydrodynamic modelling of the detector dynamics

title: Test and irradiation results of the NKF7 10.24 Gbps serializer prototype chip for ALICE ITS3
abstract: Abstract The coming ALICE Inner Tracking System (ITS) upgrade uses MAPS (Monolithic Active Pixel Sensors) with multiple integrated 10.24-Gbps transmitters. The NKF7 chip is a proto transmitter serializing a 16-bit input into a 10.24-Gbps output. Connecting NKF7 16-data inputs to an FPGA allows for the generation of arbitrary patterns. A PRBS7 pattern results (at the end of the ITS3 FPC cable) into open eyes at 5.12 Gbps (Bit Error Ratio < 10 -15 ) but closes at 10.24 Gbps (BER > 10 -9 @ V DD = 1.45 V). Reducing V DD further degrades BER and increases jitter which is also seen in chip simulations after adding GND and V DD bond wire inductance. This inductance gives on-die supply noise which will be mitigated in future chips by integrating on-die regulators. Irradiation with 32-MeV protons gives σ SEU ≈ 10 -12 cm 2 and NKF7 withstands a TID > 10 Mrad.

title: Characterizing $\pT$-differential Radial-Flow Fluctuations in Au+Au Collisions at FAIR with a Multi-Phase Transport Model
abstract: We report the first predictions of the transverse-momentum ($\pT$)-differential radial-flow fluctuation observable, $\vzpT$, in Au+Au collisions at the top SIS100 energy, $\snn=4.9$~GeV, which will be available at the FAIR accelerator complex. Radial flow and its fluctuations are studied for different centrality intervals and reference-$\pT$ selections to investigate the properties and robustness of the calculated long-range correlation. $\vzpT$ displays a characteristic evolution from negative values at low $\pT$ to positive values at higher $\pT$. The integrated $v_0$, obtained with different reference-$\pT$ intervals, follows a common trend, with an approximately inverse-square-root dependence on the inclusive charged-particle multiplicity ($\nch$). The $\vzpT$ signal changes little when the pseudorapidity gap is varied between 0.2 and 0.8, or when the edges of the reference-$\pT$ interval are varied, in the bulk region. For identified particles, the pion and proton $\vzpT$ are ordered at low $\pT$, qualitatively similar to the mass ordering seen at higher energies. However, unlike at higher collision energies, $\vzpT$ does not exhibit constituent-quark number scaling, so the results do not support an interpretation in terms of partonic collectivity. The results are also in partial contradiction with the behavior of hadronic elliptic flow in these low-energy collisions. These results provide constraints on the evolution of radial correlations toward lower collision energies and motivate comparisons with complementary observables to clarify their connection to collective dynamics.

title: Identifiability of g mode resonances in eccentric binary neutron stars with multidetector observations
abstract: $g$ mode resonances in eccentric binary neutron star systems are potential probes of internal stratification, superfluidity, composition gradients, and the equation of state. Although such weak dynamical tidal signatures are unlikely to be resolved with current detector sensitivities, third generation observations may make them accessible, in which case identifying the weak resonant phase shift would provide information beyond the bulk adiabatic tidal deformability. We build a four class dataset in an eccentric harmonic framework, containing point particle, adiabatic tide, resonant $g$ mode, and pure noise samples, and use Einstein Telescope (ET) and Cosmic Explorer (CE) detector data to test whether this weak resonant phase signature can be identified from noisy time domain strain. The ET, CE, and ET+CE deep learning models reach accuracies of $0.650$, $0.809$, and $0.875$, respectively. On the same simulated samples, the matched filtering method reaches lower accuracies of $0.534$, $0.703$, and $0.718$. This result arises from the fact that the resonant correction manifests as a weak phase morphology difference superimposed on the adiabatic tidal background, whereas matched filtering is sensitive only to the overall similarity. Hence, in the presence of weak phase differences, the neural network employed for the classification task is better able to learn these local phase and morphology features from the complete time domain strain segment. The results indicate that joint third generation observations improve the identifiability of weak internal mode phase information.
