title: Gravitational-Wave Constraints on $R^2$ Gravity
abstract: Gravitational waves from compact binary coalescences provide a unique opportunity to test general relativity in the strong-field regime. Quadratic $f(R)=R+aR^2$ gravity is among the simplest higher-curvature extensions of general relativity and introduces a massive scalar degree of freedom whose finite interaction range can modify compact-binary dynamics and gravitational-wave emission. We map this theory onto the effective-field-theory waveform for generic massive scalar-tensor gravity, obtaining a theory-specific inspiral phase correction governed by the single coupling parameter $a$. Using Bayesian analyses of the binary-neutron-star events GW170817 and GW190425, we obtain a combined constraint on the quadratic-curvature coupling of $a\lesssim6.2\times10^6\,\mathrm{m}^2$ at $90\%$ credibility, corresponding to a lower bound on the scalar mass of $m_s\gtrsim3.2\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{eV}$. This constitutes the strongest astrophysical constraint on the quadratic-curvature coupling, improving the previous best bound by approximately five orders of magnitude and demonstrating the sensitivity of binary-neutron-star inspirals to finite-range scalar interactions in the strong-field regime.

title: Probing α clustering in 12 C at energies available at the Cooling Storage Ring facility using the jet A A microscopic transport model
SOLPS-ITER simulation analysis on the synergistic effect of boron and neon in detached plasma on EAST
abstract: Abstract EAST experiments have demonstrated that combined neon (Ne) and boron (B) injection overcomes the narrow operational window of pure neon seeding, and compensates for the insufficient radiative capacity of B alone, establishing a stable ELM-suppressed H-mode with a partially detached outer divertor and good confinement (H 98 ∼1) [Sun et al 2026 Nucl. Fusion 66 044002]. To reveal the underlying physical mechanisms, SOLPS-ITER simulations of Ne–B co-injection are performed under EAST conditions. Three mechanisms are identified. First, B and Ne form a poloidal radiation synergy: Ne radiates efficiently at T e ∼20–27 eV near the X -point, while B fills the radiative gap below ∼17 eV in the divertor region, together extending the energy dissipation zone from the X -point to the target and enabling deep energy detachment. Second, the B-enhanced D + -D charge exchange in the near-scrape-off layer amplifies momentum loss and substantially reduces the target particle flux. Third, the reduced Ne seeding rate through compensating B radiation is the dominant lever for lowering core radiation and Z eff , because core impurity content is governed by Ne, with its density exceeding that of B by nearly two orders of magnitude regardless of injection rate. Additionally, the deeper detachment state further promotes B deposition on the divertor target, reinforcing wall conditioning. These mechanisms provide a generalizable physics framework for mixed low- Z /high- Z impurity injection strategies on ITER and future fusion devices.

title: Revisiting p- 11 B fusion: updated cross-sections, reactivity, and energy balance
abstract: Abstract Recent experimental progress has substantially improved the available cross-section data for the p- 11 B fusion reaction, particularly in energy regions that previously lacked direct measurements. In this study, we develop a high-precision analytical parameterization of the p- 11 B reaction cross-section over the 0–10 MeV energy range, incorporating the new experimental data into a continuous and numerically efficient representation. Using this parameterization, we evaluate the thermonuclear reactivity of the p- 11 B reaction and examine the effects of the dominant resonance at 0.6 MeV and a newly observed resonance around 4.7 MeV. Furthermore, we assess the energy balance by analyzing the fusion power density and the electron bremsstrahlung power density. Our results indicate that p- 11 B fusion is not precluded by bremsstrahlung constraints when contemporary cross-section data and self-consistent thermal modeling are employed.

title: Precise and accurate nuclear electric quadrupole moment of $^{223}$Ra from molecular spectroscopy
abstract: Nuclear electric quadrupole moments of unstable isotopes are commonly extracted from laser spectroscopy of the atomic hyperfine structure, where the accuracy is limited to the several-percent level by the available electric-field-gradient (EFG) calculations. In this study, we determine the spectroscopic quadrupole moment of $^{223}$Ra (half-life $t_{1/2} = 11.4$ d) from hyperfine-resolved collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy of the radioactive molecule $^{223}$Ra$^{19}$F. The $X\,^2\Sigma^+$ electronic ground state of RaF provides a large axial EFG at the radium nucleus that can be calculated with relativistic coupled-cluster theory to sub-percent accuracy. Together with a three-fold improvement in spectral resolution over previous fast-beam measurements of radioactive molecules, this yields $Q_s = +1.211(7)_\mathrm{stat}(2)_\mathrm{syst}(5)_\mathrm{theo}\,e\mathrm{b}$ for $^{223}$Ra with a total uncertainty of 0.73%, approximately three times better than atomic and ionic determinations. This result demonstrates that molecular spectroscopy can provide access to the electromagnetic structure of unstable nuclei with a precision competitive with, and in favorable cases better than, atomic spectroscopy, and may thus be envisioned for studies beyond the limitations of current radioactive-atom experiments.

title: Microscopic spin-parity distributions of fission fragments
First Measurement of the Masses of the ϒ 1 ( 1 D ) and ϒ 3 ( 1 D ) States and the Energy Dependence of the Cross Sections for e + e − → ϒ J ( 1 D ) η and e + e − → ϒ J ( 1 D ) π + π −
abstract: We study the processes e + e − → ϒ J ( 1 D ) η and e + e − → ϒ J ( 1 D ) π + π − at center-of-mass energies s = ( 10.73 − 11.02 ) GeV using a 142.5 fb − 1 data sample, including 122 fb − 1 near the ϒ ( 10860 ) peak ( s = 10.866 GeV ), collected with the Belle detector at the KEKB asymmetric-energy e + e − collider. From the peak sample, the products of Born cross section times branching fraction are obtained for σ Born ( e + e − → ϒ J ( 1 D ) η ) or σ Born ( e + e − → ϒ J ( 1 D ) π + π − ) and B ( ϒ J ( 1 D ) → χ b 1 γ ) or B ( ϒ J ( 1 D ) → χ b 2 γ ) for each ϒ J ( 1 D ) state. The corresponding branching fractions for ϒ ( 10860 ) decays are also obtained. The significances of the ϒ 1 ( 1 D ) , ϒ 2 ( 1 D ) , and ϒ 3 ( 1 D ) signals are 4.8 σ , > 10 σ , and 3.0 σ , respectively, including systematic uncertainties. The mass for ϒ 2 ( 1 D ) is measured to be ( 10167.0 ± 1.0 ± 0.2 ) MeV / c 2 , where the first and second uncertainties are statistical and systematic. The mass splittings Δ m 12 = m ( ϒ 2 ( 1 D ) ) − m ( ϒ 1 ( 1 D ) ) and Δ m 23 = m ( ϒ 3 ( 1 D ) ) − m ( ϒ 2 ( 1 D ) ) are ( 11.8 ± 1.5 ± 0.4 ) MeV / c 2 and ( 7.6 ± 2.4 ± 0.6 ) MeV / c 2 , respectively. We determine the energy dependence of the cross sections for e + e − → ϒ J ( 1 D ) η and e + e − → ϒ J ( 1 D ) π + π − for the ϒ 1 ( 1 D ) , ϒ 2 ( 1 D ) , and ϒ 3 ( 1 D ) states, combined.

versions.abstract: We study the processes $e^+e^-\to\Upsilon_J(1D)\eta$ and $e^+e^-\to\Upsilon_J(1D)\pi^+\pi^-$ at center-of-mass energies $\sqrt{s}$=(10.73 -- 11.02) GeV using a $142.5\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ data sample, including 122~fb$^{-1}$ near the $\Upsilon$(10860) peak ($\sqrt{s}$ = 10.866 GeV), collected with the Belle detector at the KEKB asymmetric-energy $e^+e^-$ collider. From the peak sample, the products of Born cross section times branching fraction are obtained for $\sigma_{\rm Born}(e^+e^-\to\Upsilon_J(1D)\eta)$ or $\sigma_{\rm Born}(e^+e^-\to\Upsilon_J(1D)\pi^+\pi^-)$ and ${\cal B}(\Upsilon_J(1D)\to\chi_{b1}\gamma)$ or ${\cal B}(\Upsilon_J(1D)\to\chi_{b2}\gamma)$ for each $\Upsilon_J(1D)$ state. The corresponding branching fractions for $\Upsilon(10860)$ decays are also obtained. The significances of the $\Upsilon_1(1D)$, $\Upsilon_2(1D)$, and $\Upsilon_3(1D)$ signals are 4.8$\sigma$, ${>}10\sigma$, and 3.0$\sigma$, respectively, including systematic uncertainties. The mass for $\Upsilon_2(1D)$ is measured to be $(10167.0\pm 1.0\pm 0.2)$ MeV/$c^2$, where the first and second uncertainties are statistical and systematic. The mass splittings $\Delta m_{12}=m(\Upsilon_2(1D))-m(\Upsilon_1(1D))$ and $\Delta m_{23}=m(\Upsilon_3(1D))-m(\Upsilon_2(1D))$ are $(11.8\pm1.5\pm0.4)$ MeV/$c^2$ and $(7.6\pm2.4\pm0.6)$ MeV/$c^2$, respectively.~We determine the energy dependence of the cross sections for $e^+e^-\to\Upsilon_J(1D)\eta$ and $e^+e^-\to\Upsilon_J(1D)\pi^+\pi^-$ for the $\Upsilon_1(1D)$, $\Upsilon_2(1D)$, and $\Upsilon_3(1D)$ states, combined.

title: Differentiable emulation for high-dimensional Bayesian calibration of nuclear reaction models
Decay mechanism of the breakup reaction 6 Li+ 90 Zr using the dynamical cluster-decay model
Nucleon-nucleon potential using N 3 LO chiral effective field theory
Impact of instrumental effects and target thickness on the SPARC magnetic proton recoil spectrometer response function
abstract: The SPARC tokamak aims to demonstrate net fusion power gain in tokamaks (Q-fus > 1). To measure neutron emission, a neutron spectrometer based on the magnetic proton recoil technique is being developed. This diagnostic operates by converting collimated neutrons into recoil protons through elastic scattering on a polyethylene target. The recoiled protons are then separated based on their momentum by a magnetic field and subsequently detected by a hodoscope composed of plastic scintillation detectors coupled to photomultiplier tubes. This allows neutron energies in the 2–20 MeV range to be discriminated, though only neutrons in a narrower energy window (±25% around the selected central energy) can be measured. The instrument will contribute to the determination of the total fusion power and provide information on plasma parameters such as ion temperature and the presence of non-thermal fuel ions. In this study, the design rationale of the hodoscope is presented and the main instrumental effects that govern proton collection are characterized. The hodoscope is divided into three regions with different channel widths, depths, and lengths, jointly optimized to satisfy three coupled physical requirements: sufficient energy resolution at the 14.1 MeV DT peak, full proton containment up to 18.75 MeV, and limitation of the background through minimization of the detector volume. Three correction factors are evaluated through dedicated simulations: the vertical signal loss due to protons falling outside the scintillator rod length, the cross-talk between adjacent channels, and the background contribution per channel. A correction scheme combining all three factors is presented.

title: Cumulative protons and pions at the intermediate energies in the FRAGM experiment
abstract: One of the important research objectives of the FRAGM experiment operating at the TWAC heavy-ion accelerator-storage complex was the study of particle production in the cumulative region. Differential cross sections were measured for the production of pions - resulting from the fragmentation of carbon nuclei at an energy of 3.2 GeV/nucleon, as well as protons with energy range from 300 to 2000 MeV/nucleon at an angle of 3.5 degrees relative to the incident ion beam. The parameterization of cumulative effect used in experiments investigating nucleus-nucleus interactions is discussed. It is shown, that the energy dependencies of these parameters are analogous to those observed in nucleon-nucleus interactions and indicate the presence of nuclear scaling behavior.

title: Beyond constant error: Heteroscedastic Bayesian model combination for modeling unmeasured nuclei
abstract: Experimentally inaccessible regions of the nuclear chart remain a challenge for global models of atomic nuclei to predict. This includes exotic nuclei near particle drip lines, superheavy elements at the extremes of mass and charge, and the neutron-rich pathways of astrophysical processes in explosive stellar environments where heavy elements are created. Given that individual nuclear models are imperfect, deep extrapolations are best approached using model ensembles, which allow for the systematic combination of diverse theoretical predictions. In this study, we employ the recently introduced Bayesian model combination (BMC) method, based on statistical machine learning, that provides robust uncertainty quantification for forecasts using model ensembles. To account for the inherent degradation of predictive power as models extrapolate into the yet-unexplored domain, we introduce a heteroscedastic BMC framework in which the combined theoretical uncertainty is treated as a dynamic quantity. We apply this methodology to an ensemble of realistic energy density functionals with a specific focus on the Z = 46 – 52 isotopic chains. We rigorously validate the approach using both experimental data and synthetic data designed to assess performance in the deep extrapolation regime. Our results demonstrate that the proposed heteroscedastic approach yields superior calibration metrics and provides statistically principled assessments of the particle drip lines.

title: Observation of Scaling of Higher-Order Flow in a Unitary Fermi Gas
abstract: Collective flow emerging from spatially anisotropic many-body systems is a fundamental manifestation of strongly interacting quantum matter, from ultracold quantum gases to the quark-gluon plasma created in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. Yet how collective flow emerges across different spatial harmonics and how dissipation modifies its evolution remain largely unexplored. Here we investigate the nonequilibrium expansion of a unitary Fermi gas initially confined in nearly homogeneous potentials with engineered angular deformations. By suddenly releasing the confinement, we resolve anisotropic flow harmonics up to the seventh order. Remarkably, after normalization and rescaling by the characteristic expansion timescale, the different harmonics and system sizes exhibit a universal early-time evolution. At longer times, this universality breaks down and we observe an approximately quadratic dependence of the harmonic attenuation on harmonic order, consistent with viscous acoustic scaling. Furthermore, temperature-dependent measurements reveal the role of shear viscosity in the dissipative evolution of higher-order flow. Our results open a new route to exploring the interplay between universal hydrodynamic expansion and dissipative transport, connecting collective dynamics in ultracold quantum gases with anisotropic flow in strongly interacting nuclear matter.

title: Bayesian inference of the magnetic component in the quark-gluon plasma
abstract: The chromomagnetic monopoles (CMM), emergent topological excitations of non-Abelian gauge fields carrying chromomagnetic charge, have long been postulated to play an important role in the vacuum confinement of quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the deconfinement transition at temperature T c ≈ 160 MeV , as well as the strongly coupled nature of quark-gluon plasma (QGP). While such CMMs were found to help provide resolutions for challenging puzzles from heavy-ion collision measurements, they were typically introduced as model assumptions in the past. Here we perform a data-driven Bayesian inference of the chromomagnetic component, within the CUJET framework, and extract its temperature-dependent abundance for the first time. Using the 3 framework for calculations of jet energy loss and analyzing a comprehensive experimental dataset for nuclear modification factor ( R AA ) and elliptic flow ( v 2 ) of high-transverse-momentum hadrons, the fraction of CMMs in the QGP is obtained by Bayesian inference and is found to be substantial in the 1 ∼ 2 T c region. The posterior CMM fraction is further tested against additional data and is also shown to predict QGP transport properties that are quantitatively consistent with the state-of-the-art knowledge.

versions.title: Bayesian inference of the magnetic component of quark-gluon plasma
versions.abstract: The chromo-magnetic monopoles (CMM), emergent topological excitations of non-Abelian gauge fields carrying chromo-magnetic charge, have long been postulated to play an important role in the vacuum confinement of quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the deconfinement transition at temperature $T_c\approx 160\rm MeV$, as well as the strongly coupled nature of quark-gluon plasma (QGP). While such CMMs have been found to provide solutions for challenging puzzles from heavy-ion collision measurements, they were typically introduced as model assumptions in the past. Here we show how their very existence can be determined and their abundance extracted in a data-driven way for the first time. Using the \textsc{cujet3} framework for calculations of jet energy loss and analyzing a comprehensive experimental data set for nuclear modification factor ($R_{\mathrm{AA}}$) and elliptic flow ($v_2$) of high-transverse-momentum hadrons, the fraction of CMMs in the QGP is obtained by Bayesian inference and is found to be substantial in the $1\sim 2 T_c$ region. The posterior CMM fraction is further validated by excellent agreement with additional data and is also shown to predict QGP transport properties quantitatively consistent with the state-of-the-art knowledge.

versions.title: Bayesian inference of the magnetic component in the quark-gluon plasma
versions.abstract: The chromomagnetic monopoles (CMM), emergent topological excitations of non-Abelian gauge fields carrying chromomagnetic charge, have long been postulated to play an important role in the vacuum confinement of quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the deconfinement transition at temperature T c ≈ 160 MeV , as well as the strongly coupled nature of quark-gluon plasma (QGP). While such CMMs were found to help provide resolutions for challenging puzzles from heavy-ion collision measurements, they were typically introduced as model assumptions in the past. Here we perform a data-driven Bayesian inference of the chromomagnetic component, within the CUJET framework, and extract its temperature-dependent abundance for the first time. Using the 3 framework for calculations of jet energy loss and analyzing a comprehensive experimental dataset for nuclear modification factor ( R AA ) and elliptic flow ( v 2 ) of high-transverse-momentum hadrons, the fraction of CMMs in the QGP is obtained by Bayesian inference and is found to be substantial in the 1 ∼ 2 T c region. The posterior CMM fraction is further tested against additional data and is also shown to predict QGP transport properties that are quantitatively consistent with the state-of-the-art knowledge.

title: Neutron Capture Information in Improving IBD Angular Resolution
abstract: One of the most important neutrino interactions is the Inverse Beta Decay (IBD). However, the IBD events typically carry no directional information in water Cherenkov detectors as the positron directions are mostly isotropic at low energies, such as those in supernova studies. As gadolinium is being added to Super-Kamiokande, the improved neutron tagging efficiency not only allows better background rejection, but the neutron capture information could potentially provide additional information that allows better event reconstruction. Due to neutron diffusion in water, event-by-event reconstruction is difficult. However, if the final neutron capture position is correlated with the initial neutrino momentum, it may be possible that neutrino directionality could be reconstructed statistically, with or without using the positron information. In this work, we use Geant4 to simulate neutron propagation in water. We show that in a wide range of neutrino energies from about 10 MeV to several hundred MeV, neutron capture information could statistically enhance the neutrino directionality, compared to positron-only inference, even with neutron diffusion considered. However, practical application of this technique depends crucially on detection effects, especially the vertex reconstruction resolutions. Our work therefore motivates developments of better reconstruction algorithms and techniques, as well as detector upgrades.

title: Multi-beamlet operation of the ITER negative ion source prototype SPIDER towards full beam extraction
abstract: Abstract The neutral beam heating systems for ITER will be based on radio-frequency driven sources, accelerating a negative ion beam current of tens of amperes for up to one hour. In its second operation phase SO-2, the full-scale prototype source SPIDER was operated for the first time in multi-beamlet configuration at ∼70 kW driver −1 , extracting a H — current density of 215 A m −2 over ¼ of the extraction area at 0.3 Pa source filling pressure, providing a total accelerated beam power of ∼700 kW. Scaling of the results confirms the specifications of the on-going RF generators upgrade, indicating that target current density of 330 A m −2 in hydrogen is achievable by increasing the RF power to 100 kW driver −1 . Beam uniformity was assessed at the beamlet-group scale under moderate underperveance conditions: at high power row-averaged beamlet currents were within ±10% for fifteen out of sixteen rows. A lower homogeneity was observed at the single-beamlet level. The influence of the magnetic filter field on beam uniformity was also characterized, confirming the beneficial effect of multi-driver operation on homogeneity at the extraction region. A caesium conditioning procedure was developed and validated for the partial-source configuration. An anomalous amplification of the acceleration current peculiar of the vacuum-insulated source design specific to ITER sources, attributed to stray backstreaming charges and surface emission effects, was identified and mitigated by electrostatic shielding. Together with the ongoing installation of new solid-state RF generators and an improved pumping system, the results presented in this work open the way to full-source operation in the next experimental campaign and yield findings of direct relevance to the ITER injector design.

title: Investigation of Medium Modifications to $^{12}$C Structure Functions in the Resonance Region
abstract: We present results from a high precision experimental study of the nuclear modification of the longitudinal ($F_L$) to transverse ($F_1$) structure function ratio for bound nucleons in the resonance region. The inclusive electron scattering cross sections were measured in Jefferson Lab Experimental Hall C on carbon and deuterium nuclei for a large range of kinematics, allowing for separations of the longitudinal and transverse structure functions to be performed at a range of four-momentum transfer values $0.5 \le Q^2 \le$ 3.75 GeV$^2$. In contrast to the significant body of measurements of the nuclear modification of the $F_2$ structure function in the deep inelastic scattering region, there is very little on $F_L$ and $R = F_L / 2xF_1$ in the region of the nucleon resonances. In this paper we present measurements of the nuclear effect on $R$ for $^{12}$C ($R_C$) relative to deuterium ($R_D$). These results indicate regions in which in $R_C>R_D$, requiring that the nuclear modifications be different in all three structure functions, $F_2$, $F_1$ and $F_L$.

title: Hydrogen Electron Cyclotron Resonance Dissociator Demonstrator for the Project 8 Experiment
abstract: Project 8, a neutrino mass experiment, employs the novel frequency technique of cyclotron radiation emission spectroscopy (CRES) to perform a model independent measurement of neutrino mass via tritium beta decay. Our pioneering experiment will consist of a beamline that dissociates molecular tritium, surface cools atoms through accommodation, evaporatively cools and slows atoms, and traps them in a CRES resonant cavity to advance towards our sensitivity goal of 40 meV/c^2 for our final electron-weighted neutrino mass measurement. We are prototyping an electron cyclotron resonance (ECR) dissociator that uses a tunable 1 kW 2.45 GHz RF generator and electromagnets to ignite a hydrogen plasma in an aluminum resonant cavity. Our ECR source is designed to produce a high atom flux (~10^19 atoms/second) near room temperature. We present the engineering development, gas diagnostics, and spectroscopy data from our hydrogen plasma.

title: Reconstruction of the impact parameter in nucleus-nucleus collisions at the MPD experiment
abstract: Abstract Event classification by centrality is one of the key tasks of the MPD (Multi-Purpose Detector) experiment at the NICA collider. Centrality characterizes the initial geometry of heavy-ion collisions through the correlation of measured observables with the impact parameter. Typically, charged-particle multiplicity serves as the observable of choice. However, this approach can introduce autocorrelation in net-proton multiplicity fluctuation studies. In this work, we propose a novel approach based on the combined use of signals from the forward hadron calorimeter (FHCal) and the electromagnetic calorimeter (ECal). This method is expected to suppress autocorrelation in the study of proton multiplicity fluctuations, while the combination of data from both detectors will enable unambiguous centrality event classification across the full centrality range.

title: Photon emission from rotating plasmas: A generalized McLerran-Toimela formula and the onset of superradiance
abstract: The photon emission and absorption spectra of a plasma rotating with constant angular velocity Ω are derived in terms of the spectral function of the current-current correlator. In contrast to the nonrotating case, the leading contribution arises already at one-loop order. The photon emission spectrum and its elliptic flow are calculated for a rotating quark-gluon plasma and compared with the leading two-loop result for a nonrotating plasma. The rotating plasma is found to emit significantly more soft photons than the nonrotating one. An analysis of the emission and absorption of cylindrical waves indicates that photons with energy ω and azimuthal quantum number m satisfying ω < m Ω are emitted at a higher rate than they are absorbed, thereby exhibiting the phenomenon of superradiance. It is further argued that these superradiant modes induce an instability of the magnetic field that is generated concurrently with the plasma in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.

title: Information content of the Gamow Teller Resonance: Bayesian inference with self-consistent Skyrme models
abstract: Many important charge-exchange weak processes, such as beta decays, double beta decays, and neutrino-nucleus and neutrino-nucleon reactions, are closely related to the spin- and isospin-dependent nuclear force, yet few of them can be precisely measured, or even observed, in terrestrial experiments. The Gamow-Teller resonance (GTR) in finite nuclei is one of the few experimental probes of this spin-isospin force. In a companion letter, we obtained the probability distribution of the Landau-Migdal parameter $G'_0$, which characterizes the main part of the spin-isospin force, from GTR measurements using Bayesian inference. In this follow-up work, we quantitatively study the correlations emerging from this Bayesian analysis. From the posterior, we identify two standard Skyrme parameterizations (nuSky*) that reproduce, in a unified manner, ground-state observables of finite nuclei, the salient features of the GTR, and the bulk properties of neutron-star matter. Since collective excitations in finite nuclei and in neutron-star matter are related, we use the Skyrme interactions sampled from the posterior to constrain the axial-current, charged-current neutrino-nucleon reaction rates in hot and dense compact-star matter, as the first astrophysical application of this study. The GTR-informed calculations substantially reduce the spread of the neutrino opacity; nevertheless, significant uncertainties remain due to the poorly constrained symmetry energy at sub-saturation densities. Constraining this quantity on top of a well-constrained spin-isospin interaction would pave the way towards a systematic determination of neutrino interactions in dense matter.

title: How Neutron Star Radii Encode the Dense-matter Equation of State and Hadron–Quark Transition
abstract: Abstract We investigate how future high-precision neutron star (NS) radius measurements encode microscopic information about the dense-matter equation of state (EOS), focusing on a possible first-order hadron–quark phase transition and the resulting mass–radius topology. Within a Bayesian framework using metamodel EOSs with nine microscopic parameters, we analyze mock radius measurements R 1.4 = 11.9 ± σ R km with σ R = 0.9 and 0.1 km for canonical NSs. Rather than relying only on marginalized posterior probability distributions, we introduce inverse EOS–radius mappings by studying the conditional mean of each EOS parameter as a function of the model-predicted canonical radius R 1.4 . Their slope measures the sensitivity of an EOS parameter to the radius, while their curvature determines the leading precision dependence of its posterior mean through the Jensen expansion. Resolving the mappings into four mass–radius topologies, Connected, Disconnected, Both, and No-Quark-Matter, reveals a clear hierarchy of information. The symmetry-energy parameters L (slope) and K sym (curvature) are strongly encoded in R 1.4 and their posterior means shift appreciably with improved radius precision, whereas the higher-order hadronic parameters show stronger topology dependence. Among the transition parameters, the transition density ρ t is the most strongly encoded in R 1.4 , while the energy-density jump and quark-matter sound speed are more strongly associated with the topology of the full mass–radius sequence. Since the different topologies have strongly overlapping R 1.4 distributions, even precise radius measurements cannot by themselves identify the topology or uniquely determine the high-density transition properties. These results provide a parameter-dependent hierarchy for assessing the scientific return of future high-precision radius measurements and complementary probes of high-density NS EOSs.

title: Generation of femtosecond electron bunches via CSR-induced self-compression
abstract: Abstract Ultrashort electron bunches are a key requirement for a broad range of modern accelerator applications, including pump-probe experiments, advanced radiation sources, and plasma-based acceleration schemes. Their generation is essential for accessing ultrafast temporal scales and increasing peak current. Here, we investigate a self-compression scheme for producing high-brightness, femtosecond electron bunches at low energy (< 100 MeV) in compact accelerators (< 10 m). The method uses a wiggler-chicane configuration in which CSR-induced energy modulation in the wiggler is converted into high-current spikes by a downstream chicane. As a case study, we assess its feasibility for TEX, which hosts a C-band photoinjector facility currently under commissioning at INFN-LNF. Numerical estimates and beam dynamics simulations (ASTRA, Elegant, TStep) are used to evaluate the achievable bunch lengths for different photoinjector operating modes and compression strategies. Building on previous studies, this work also investigates collective effects at low energies, showing that space-charge forces enhance the longitudinal compression factor. Overall, the results highlight the potential for producing high-brightness, femtosecond electron bunches within strict spatial constraints.

title: Deep Learning for Longitudinal Asymmetry in Heavy-Ion Collisions at RHIC Energies
abstract: We developed a deep neural network framework to predict the longitudinal asymmetry and the corresponding rapidity shift in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The model was trained using sufficiently large datasets for Au+Au and Cu+Cu collision systems at center-of-mass energies of 62.4 and 200 AGeV at RHIC. It successfully learns the underlying relationships between the input parameters and reconstructs the corresponding target quantities with good precision. Its predictions agree well with theoretical simulations across both trained and untrained centrality intervals. The influence of longitudinal asymmetry on final-state flow observables has also been studied, and the model results are in reasonable agreement with the simulation. A SHAP-based correlation analysis further supports the physical consistency of the learned feature dependencies and suggests that the observed correlations are not primarily driven by feature redundancy. The proposed framework provides a computationally efficient approach to estimating event-by-event results, potentially reducing the computational cost of large-scale theoretical model simulations. This work presents an initial study exploring the use of deep neural networks to investigate longitudinal asymmetry and rapidity shifts in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.

title: Characterization of plasma parameters of compact penning ion source by triple Langmuir probe diagnostics
abstract: Abstract Plasma characteristics of a compact Penning ion source are investigated using a triple Langmuir probe. Electron temperature and number density are estimated for continuous and pulsed mode of discharge at various range of pressure and anode voltage. The spatial and temporal behavior of plasma is analyzed to study the effect of operating parameters on the discharge stability of the ion source. The dynamics of electron temperature and number density are studied under varying discharge conditions. The decline in electron temperature with increasing pressure and enhancement with anode voltage are recorded. Electron density increases with injected gas pressure and acceleration potential. The maximum value of 4.4 × 10 10 electron/cm 3 and 5.5 × 10 12 electron/cm 3 have been measured in continuous and pulsed mode of discharge respectively. These results are essential to optimize Penning ion source for research and industrial application where stable, dense and low-temperature plasmas are required.

title: Formation of bound composite vortices of a singly quantized 1 S 0 vortex and half-quantized 3 P 2 vortices in the 1 S 0 - 3 P 2 coexisting phase in neutron stars
abstract: Pulsar glitches are believed to originate from the dynamics of quantized vortices in the neutron superfluid interior. The outer core of a neutron star hosts a $^3\text{P}_2$ spin-triplet superfluid, whose half-integer quantum vortices (HQVs) are qualitatively different from the $^1\text{S}_0$ singly quantized vortices (SQVs) in the inner crust. It has recently been proposed that the coupling between these two vortex species gives rise to a large-scale vortex network, providing a candidate mechanism for the diversity of observed pulsar glitch phenomena. Using the Gross--Pitaevskii equations for the $^1\text{S}_0$ and $^3\text{P}_2$ condensates, we perform two-dimensional simulations of one SQV and two HQVs in a coexistence phase near the crust-core boundary, varying the density--density and Josephson coupling constants. We find that the Josephson term, arising from the relative phase between the two condensates, induces a strong attractive interaction between the two HQVs and the SQV, which dominates over the density--density coupling. When pinning potentials are applied to the HQVs and the SQV at spatially separated locations, this attraction is found to be sufficiently strong to drive vortex depinning. These results suggest that two HQVs and one SQV can form a tightly bound composite vortex at the crust-core boundary, with implications for the glitch mechanism in neutron stars.

title: Thermofractal Dynamics in the Multisource Thermal Model: A Unified Approach to Multiparticle Production
abstract: The empirical success of non-extensive Tsallis statistics and multisource thermal models in describing transverse-momentum (pT ) spectra and rapidity distributions in high-energy relativistic collisions highlights a deep connection between expansion geometry, non-extensive thermodynamics, and QCD dynamics. In this work, we establish a theoretical framework showing that the thermofractal structure of QCD phase space provides a direct microscopic foundation for the multisource thermal model. By exploiting the Euler integral representation of non-extensive statistical factors, we demonstrate that a single thermofractal emission source generating q-exponential distributions is mathematically equivalent to a continuous superposition of local Boltzmann thermal sources whose temperature fluctuations follow an inverse-Gamma distribution. Furthermore, we prove that multi- component phenomenological fits with discrete source temperatures represent the exact, optimal Gauss-Laguerre quadrature discretisation of this underlying continuous thermofractal field. We show how this continuous field constrains the temperature parameter space in multisource formulations, matches pQCD hard-scattering power-law asymptotics, and provides a robust vacuum baseline for medium-induced jet quenching and nuclear modification factor (RAA ) calculations.

title: Parametrization of unitary matrices, parametrizing the symmetric $S$ matrix and the $NN$ $S$ matrix above the inelastic threshold
abstract: None of the $S$-matrix representations used in analyses of nucleon-nucleon ($NN$) scattering above the inelastic threshold is implicitly unitary, general, and connected to low-energy (Stapp) parameters, and hence correspondingly related to the physical properties of the scattering. Such a representation is also needed to solve the corresponding inverse scattering problem. I present an $S$-matrix representation which satisfies these requirements. As a by-product, I derive a parametrization of an $n$-dimensional unitary matrix.

title: Balanced multi-specification indirect testing of analog circuits via heterogeneous dual-level ensemble regression
abstract: Indirect testing reduces analog integrated-circuit test cost by predicting electrical specifications from low-cost response-derived features. In practical multi-specification flows, target difficulty is often uneven: easy labels can dominate mean accuracy, whereas difficult labels determine test-flow reliability. This paper formulates multi-specification indirect testing as a balanced regression problem evaluated by mean accuracy, worst-target performance, and cross-target stability. We propose Heterogeneous Dual-Level Ensemble Regression (HDLER), a target-wise framework that trains complementary base regressors independently, fuses them by stacking with feature passthrough, and adaptively blends the stacked output with base-model averaging using out-of-fold validation. On a simulated operational-amplifier dataset with 5000 samples, 58 features, and 11 specifications, HDLER achieves a mean target-wise test R2 of 0.9508 across five random seeds, outperforming stacking alone (0.9339) and simple averaging (0.7843). Relative to stacking, it improves worst-target R2 from 0.6487 to 0.6939, increases difficult-target mean R2 from 0.8264 to 0.8659, and reduces the across-target standard deviation from 0.1120 to 0.0952. A measured-data validation on commercial OPA314 devices further obtains a mean R2 of 0.9874 and a worst-target R2 of 0.9670. The results show that target-aware fusion improves multi-specification reliability when performance is limited by the weakest labels.

title: The long period radio transient ASKAP J1448−68 is a cataclysmic variable
abstract: Abstract Wide-field time-domain radio surveys have recently unveiled a new class of Galactic radio emitter: long period radio transients (LPTs). Despite the rapid pace of discovery, their origins remain poorly understood, with two main theories emerging: slowly spinning magnetars or binary white dwarfs (WDs) with magnetic interactions. All three LPTs with well-characterised optical counterparts are WDs in binary systems, but even within that class there is diversity, with one accreting and two detached systems. In this Letter, we show that the LPT ASKAP J1448-68 is a cataclysmic variable (CV)—a WD accreting from a low-mass companion—with a spectroscopic orbital period consistent with the radio pulse period, and specifically, potentially consistent with being a polar. Unlike the other known LPT CV, ASKAP J1448-68 does not exhibit the He ii emission that is a hallmark of magnetic CVs in their high accretion states. We also present new optical time-series and infrared photometric observations, showing flickering at the 10% level and suggesting a possible period bouncer origin. This identification of ASKAP J1448-68 adds to the small sample of characterised LPT counterparts, and shows that LPT emission can persist in an accreting WD binary at a low accretion rate.
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

title: Single-particle structure of the semimagic nucleus Zr 90 from a nonlocal dispersive optical model
abstract: A nonlocal dispersive-optical-model (DOM) analysis has been carried out for neutrons and protons in the semi-magic nucleus $^{90}$Zr. Elastic-scattering angular distributions, total and reaction cross sections, single-particle energies, the neutron and proton numbers, the charge distribution, and the binding energy have been fitted to extract the neutron and proton self-energies both above and below the Fermi energy. The resulting spectroscopic factors and other DOM ingredients yield a good description of the $(e,e'p)$ cross sections when the open-shell proton system is described with an extension of the DOM that treats pairing. The distinct difference between the open-shell proton system and a closed one is illustrated by the smooth transition from mostly full to mostly empty orbits.

title: S factor of C 13 ( α , n ) O 16 at low energies in cluster effective field theory
abstract: The $^{13}$C($α$,$n$)$^{16}$O reaction at low energies is studied by constructing an effective field theory. We choose a separation scale at $E=1$~MeV, where $E$ is the initial $α$-$^{13}$C energy in center-of-mass frame, just below the sharp resonant $5/2^+$ state of $^{17}$O, and include two open channels, $α$-$^{13}$C and $n$-$^{16}$O, and resonant $1/2^+$, $5/2^-$, $3/2^+$ states of $^{17}$O in the study. Parameters of the theory are fitted to experimental data, $S$ factor of $^{13}$C($α$,$n$)$^{16}$O at the energies below $E=1$~MeV, including the data sets recently reported by the LUNA and JUNA collaborations, and the $S$ factor of $^{13}$C($α$,$n$)$^{16}$O is extrapolated to the Gamow peak energy $E_G= 0.19$~MeV in the low mass AGB stars. We discuss an uncertainty in the estimate of the $S$ factor and confirm that the main part of the uncertainty emerges from the model assumptions about the near-breakup threshold $1/2^+$ state of $^{17}$O.

title: New Constraints on r -process Nucleosynthesis in Neutron Star Mergers from GW170817 Late-phase Spectra
abstract: Abstract The neutron star merger event GW170817 provided the first direct evidence of r -process nucleosynthesis. Observed spectra of its electromagnetic counterpart AT2017gfo exhibited several features that encode information on the nature and abundance of the synthesized r -process elements. In this study, we investigate the late nebular-phase spectral features of the kilonova AT2017gfo, which provide important probes of the elemental abundance of the ejecta. We construct an analytic spectral model that computes emission features produced by the radiative decay of collisionally excited ions through allowed and forbidden transitions. By comparing our model to AT2017gfo, we identify La III and Ce III as the main contributors to the emission features at 1.4 and 1.6 μ m, respectively. We also confirm Te III as the dominant contributor to the 2.1 μ m feature proposed in previous works. We infer mass fractions of X (La) ≈ 0.025–0.05, X (Ce) ≈ 0.05–0.1, and X (Te) ≈ 0.04–0.08, although the La and Ce abundance estimates remain tentative due to uncertainties in the radiation field. From the nondetections of Kr and Sb lines, we derive upper limits of X (Kr) ≲ 0.03 and X (Sb) ≲ 0.003. These results suggest that nucleosynthesis in the inner ejecta of GW170817 produced a suppressed first r -process peak and an enhanced abundance of heavier elements compared to the solar r -process pattern, with an estimated lanthanide fraction of X LN ≈ (3–6) × 10 −2 . Our conclusions are consistent with the apparent universality of heavy r -process elements and the lanthanide fraction inferred from observations of r -enhanced metal-poor stars.

title: In Situ Isotopic Analysis of Presolar Graphite Challenges Stellar Models
abstract: Abstract We have analyzed zirconium, molybdenum, and barium isotopes for the first time in situ in two presolar graphite grains found in polished thin sections from the CM2 meteorites Maribo and Murchison. Both grains most likely originated in low-mass, low-metallicity AGB stars. The Maribo grain has almost pure s -process molybdenum in a subgrain, challenging AGB star models that assume homogenization of s -process material in the convective stellar envelope prior to grain condensation. Either this grain formed in a chemically and isotopically distinct high-density region or after its parent star had already lost its envelope. Furthermore, neutrons from the 22 Ne( α , n ) 25 Mg reaction were only marginally captured by 95 Zr in both grains’ parent stars, which further challenge stellar models and the theoretically derived neutron-capture cross section of 95 Zr. Finally, both grains showed contamination with molybdenum of solar composition in some regions of the grains, probably from aqueous alteration on their parent asteroids, emphasizing the importance of depth-resolved isotope studies.

title: Relativistic transport near moving interfaces
abstract: We study linear disturbances localized near planar surfaces moving at constant velocity $v$ in relativistic media. Depending on the physical setting, the surface may represent a moving obstacle, a thermal boundary, or an external source, providing a unified description of boundary layers, wakes, and the asymptotic tails of shock waves. The central result is a propagator representation of the interface solution that yields a geometric characterization of these phenomena. Using a Laplace-transform formulation, we show that the solution is a superposition of modes with purely imaginary frequency and wavenumber. For a given interface velocity, the admissible modes are selected by the line $i\omega=vik$ in the $\{i\omega,ik\}$ plane. As $v$ varies, this line sweeps across the spectrum, providing a unified geometric description of interface-localized solutions for arbitrary interface velocities. We illustrate the formalism with applications to relativistic hydrodynamics and kinetic theory.

title: Non-uniqueness of the amplitude reconstruction in the inverse scattering problem and a refinement of Hoehler's resonance clustering
abstract: Reaction-amplitude reconstruction in the inverse scattering problem is limited by the bilinear form of all reaction observables. At fixed kinematics, N complex amplitudes contain 2N real quantities, whereas complete measurements determine at most 2N-1 parameters. Uniqueness therefore depends on whether additional physical constraints, such as unitarity, supply the missing information. We examine the consequences for resonance identification, focusing on angular-momentum assignments. Building on published results showing how truncation redistributes pole-bearing contributions among effective partial waves, we examine exact and practical ambiguities associated with imposing coupled-channel unitarity. A 4 x 4 counterexample shows that different on-shell unitary amplitudes can produce identical measurable bilinears. Practical unitary descriptions can also yield different pole content while remaining compatible with experimental uncertainties. We update Hoehler's clustering using the thirteen four-star N* resonances in PDG 2026 and Bonn-Gatchina results published in 2025. Nearby poles with different partial-wave assignments occur both in the PDG compilation and within Bonn-Gatchina, so their proximity is not solely a consequence of PDG averaging. Some groupings persist, while others change appreciably. We discuss a conditional interpretation in which truncation redistributes a common pole-bearing contribution among effective partial waves, with additional reconstruction uncertainties potentially accounting for departures from coincident pole positions. These considerations allow, but do not establish, a common origin for cluster members. The necessity of separate states and the stability of their angular-momentum assignments remain questions for further investigation.

title: Low-lying states of neutron-rich $N=50$ isotones in multi-reference covariant density functional theory
abstract:
Predictions for the systematics of low-lying states in neutron-rich $N=50$ isotones from 
uclide[80]{Zn} to 
uclide[70]{Ca}, where experimental information remains scarce, exhibit substantial model dependence. We investigate these nuclei using multi-reference covariant density functional theory based on a relativistic energy density functional, in which nuclear wave functions are constructed as superpositions of symmetry-restored mean-field states with different quadrupole deformations. The low-lying states of 
uclide[78]{Ni} are reasonably reproduced, and a prolate rotational band built on the second $0^+$ state is predicted in addition to a near-spherical ground state. As the proton number decreases toward $Z=20$, the low-energy structure exhibits a nonmonotonic evolution from spherical to strongly deformed and subsequently back to spherical shapes, consistent with valence-space shell-model predictions. In particular, the emergence of deformed ground states in 
uclide[76]{Fe} and 
uclide[74]{Cr} is accompanied by enhanced quadrupole collectivity and stronger shape mixing. The results provide a coherent microscopic description of the structural evolution from the doubly magic 
uclide[78]{Ni} to the neutron-rich $N=50$ isotones.

title: Lattice study of spin interactions between heavy quarks in the quark-gluon plasma
Tensor analyzing power T 20 in the reaction γ d ⃗ → p n at photon energies 350–680 MeV
Structural evolution and isotopic sensitivity in 16 O-induced compound systems
S -wave kaon condensation in neutron-star matter within a chiral model framework with dynamical meson masses
Modeling fragmentation of $^{20}$Ne nuclei at the LHC
abstract: Fragmentation of relativistic neon nuclei was studied with the Abrasion-Ablation Monte Carlo for Colliders model (AAMCC-MST), which incorporates pre-equilibrium clustering of spectator matter via a Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) algorithm, subsequent decays of the excited clusters, and Coulomb repulsion between final fragments. After validating the model against data on $^{20}$Ne and $^{22}$Ne fragmentation on various targets, the production of spectator nuclear fragments, neutrons, and protons in $^{20}$Ne-$^{20}$Ne collisions at the LHC was modeled at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.36$ TeV. The production cross sections, transverse and longitudinal momentum distributions for $^2$H, $^4$He, $^6$Li, $^{10}$B, $^{12}$C, $^{14}$N, and $^{16}$O fragments were calculated as these fragments may contaminate $^{20}$Ne beams circulating in the LHC. A simple parametrization describing relative width of the longitudinal momentum distributions calculated for these fragment species was constructed. To study the sensitivity of results to $\alpha$-clustering and nuclear density distributions in neon nuclei, two density profiles for $^{20}$Ne and $^{22}$Ne were used: a deformed Woods-Saxon, and a five-$\alpha$ bi-pyramidal configuration. In addition, a spherical profile was considered for $^{20}$Ne. Comparing results obtained with these profiles and with or without MST clustering shows that the calculated yields of spectator nucleons and fragments, their momentum distributions are sensitive to the details of nuclear structure of $^{20,22}$Ne and fragmentation modeling. The results provide the input for simulations of the transport of secondary forward nuclei in the LHC to estimate their interaction rates with circulating $^{20}$Ne beam nuclei, and also for calculations of responses of neutron and proton Zero Degree Calorimeters to $^{20}$Ne-$^{20}$Ne events.

title: Global polarization of Λ hyperons and its sensitivity to equations of state in low-energy heavy-ion collisions
Empirical and microscopic evidence for π h 9 / 2 configuration assignment to the one-quasiproton band in 235 Np
Breakup coupling effects in 6 Li-induced α transfer reactions on intermediate-mass nuclei
AI-based plasma equilibrium parameter inference in KSTAR for DEMO-relevant reactors using only ex-vessel magnetic diagnostics
abstract: Abstract This study proposes a deep neural network for high-fidelity equilibrium parameter inference, serving as a surrogate of the magnetic EFIT reconstruction and relying exclusively on ex-vessel magnetic signals. The objective is to circumvent the long-term integrity constraints of in-vessel magnetic diagnostics in the nuclear environment of the Demonstration Fusion Power Reactor (DEMO)-relevant devices. Using KSTAR data (2021–2024), a baseline model trained solely on measured ex-vessel magnetic diagnostics (the Measurement-only model) is compared with an Augmented model, which addresses informational sparsity via virtual-sensor signals computed from the GEQDSK. The Augmented model achieves predictive fidelity comparable to off-line EFIT, with a coefficient of determination ( R 2 ) above 0.99 and a range-normalized root-mean-squared error (NRMSE) of 0.332 % averaged over all parameters, against 2.385 % for the Measurement-only model. Because the virtual-sensor inputs derive from the EFIT solutions that define the targets, these figures quantify the surrogate fidelity with respect to the magnetic EFIT and constitute an upper bound on the accuracy attainable with physically installed ex-vessel probes, not that of an independent reconstruction. As the reference floor for the Measurement-only model, the magnetic fitting residuals of the parent EFIT reconstructions against the measured probe signals are quantified, yielding pooled range-normalized residuals of 1.55 % – 3.87 % per campaign with structured, campaign-persistent components that random noise perturbations do not emulate. Robust accuracy is maintained during neutral beam injection (NBI)-induced transients, and Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based attribution verifies that the Augmented model captures the underlying magnetohydrodynamic physics, specifically the Shafranov shift. With a median single forward pass inference latency of 3.47 ms (99th percentile: 3.53 ms), the framework is a viable surrogate for conventional numerical solvers. In conclusion, this study demonstrates that an idealized, EFIT-consistent realization of a densified ex-vessel sensor configuration retains sufficient information for high-precision equilibrium parameter inference, provided that magnetic probes are physically installed at the designated locations. This establishes the information-content prerequisite for ex-vessel-only inference in DEMO. The accuracy attainable from physically installed probes, subject to conductor-model, calibration and structured measurement-model errors, is not established and requires validation against measured ex-vessel signals.

title: CLVisc Agent for autonomous relativistic hydrodynamics studies
abstract: Abstract We enable large language model (LLM) agents to autonomously perform end-to-end hydrodynamic simulations of the quark–gluon plasma evolution and calculation of final hadron spectra in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. We design a meta skill that allows an agent to explore a project’s source code, craft a specialized skill, and iteratively refine it. Applying this meta skill to the (3+1)D viscous hydrodynamic code CLVisc, the agent builds a CLVisc skill encoding its operational knowledge and then independently executes full scientific workflows: designing parameter scans, running simulations, comparing ensemble results, and producing publication-ready figures. Crucially, the agent draws on literature-informed heavy-ion physics to select physically meaningful observables and interpret outcomes without explicit instruction. We demonstrate the pipeline in two scenarios: temperature-dependent shear viscosity over entropy density $\eta/s$, and nuclear-structure effects in O+O collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 5.36$~TeV using four \textit{ab initio} descriptions of $^{16}$O. In both, the agent plans, executes, and analyzes autonomously, devising new initial-state observables to explain final observations and extract qualitative knowledge. The meta skill is agnostic to code versions and Monte Carlo generators, promising future multi-agent systems in high-energy nuclear physics.

title: n=1 ideal MHD stability of tokamak plasmas with low aspect ratio and negative triangularity
abstract: Abstract Spherical tokamaks (STs) exhibit excellent ideal magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) stability owing to their low-aspect-ratio configuration, while negative triangularity (NT) configurations have attracted extensive attention in recent years for their superior confinement performance, despite relatively inferior MHD stability. This paper investigates the n=1 ideal MHD stability of NT configurations at low aspect ratios, to evaluate the potential compatibility of these two advantageous regimes. Using the MARS-F code, we perform beta-limit scans over various triangularity and aspect ratio values, with fixed safety factor $q$ profiles and normalized pressure gradient $p'$ profiles. The results show that the stability of positive triangularity (PT) configurations is enhanced at low aspect ratios, consistent with classical expectations; however, counterintuitively, the stability of NT configurations deteriorates with decreasing aspect ratio. We present a physical interpretation of this phenomenon, demonstrating that two intuitive concepts ( the ``most natural shape" and ``good/bad curvature") and magnetic well depth can fully explain this geometric effect and the observed stability trend. In addition, the stabilizing effect of the safety factor preserves at low aspect ratios for both PT and NT configurations, partially mitigating the aforementioned stability deterioration of NT plasmas.

title: Wave-energy partition governs weak collisional damping in cold plasmas
abstract: Abstract Weak dissipation can control wave propagation, mode competition, and instability thresholds in plasmas, yet the physical origin of large branch-to-branch differences in collisional damping is often obscured by dielectric-tensor calculations. We show that weak collisional damping in cold plasmas is governed by wave-energy partition. In the one-rate cold plasma model with independent-relaxation collisions, the damping rate of a positive-energy collisionless eigenmode equals, to leading order in weak collisions, the collision frequency multiplied by the fraction of the total wave energy stored in plasma motion. This result recasts the standard perturbative damping formula into a compact and physically transparent law, immediately explaining why field-dominated branches such as whistlers can be much less damped than the collision frequency, whereas quasi-electrostatic modes can exhibit damping of comparable magnitude. Analytic examples for Langmuir, transverse electromagnetic, whistler, and extraordinary waves show that the energy-partition form classifies weak collisional damping across distinct branches and provides a simple diagnostic for mode competition in multibranch plasma-wave systems.

title: Three-dimensional assessment of toroidal heat-load distribution on divertor targets in EAST
abstract: Abstract Although actively cooled W/Cu monoblock targets are designed for high steady-state heat exhaust, local overheating and damage have been observed on these targets in EAST. These observations suggest that, beyond the nominal heat-removal capability, the practical thermal margin may be compromised by engineering alignment, target geometry and plasma operating conditions—all of which can alter the local surface-normal heat flux via modifications in magnetic incidence and magnetic shadowing. In this work, the toroidal distribution of the heat loads on the EAST divertor is analyzed by integrating infrared thermography, finite element heat flux inversion, and three-dimensional field-line tracing using PFCFlux. This analysis focuses on the effects of toroidal-field ripple, cassette misalignment in the presence of ripple, and divertor geometry. It is shown that the 16-fold toroidal field ripple can produce a 2 π / 16 modulation of the peak heat flux on the current upper outer divertor target, with a peak fluctuation amplitude of approximately 17.75 % . Under a peak heat flux constraint of Q safe = 10 MW m − 2 , the allowable average heat flux on the upper outer target (OT) decreases from 4.28 MW m − 2 in the absence of ripple to 3.94 MW m − 2 in the presence of ripple. When ripple and relative cassette misalignments are considered simultaneously for the same target, the allowable average heat flux is further reduced to 3.11 MW m − 2 , 2.79 MW m − 2 , and 2.27 MW m − 2 for Δ = 0.6 mm , 1.0 mm , and 3.0 mm , respectively. Compared with the present upper OT, the toroidally curved lower outer vertical target (OVT) has higher allowable average heat fluxes under both ripple-free and ripple conditions without cassette misalignment, with values of 7.00 and 5.98 MW m − 2 , respectively, compared with 4.28 and 3.94 MW m − 2 for the upper OT. Undertoroidal-field ripple and a Δ = 1 mm misalignment, the new upper horizontal target achieves a higher allowable average heat flux than the lower outer horizontal target (OHT), with values of 4.70 and 4.01 MW m − 2 , respectively. These results show that magnetic ripple, assembly tolerances, and toroidal geometric continuity must be considered in the thermal design of divertor targets in fusion devices.

title: The multiscale nonlinear interactions between kinetic ballooning mode and drift wave turbulence critical for confinement improvement of hybrid fusion plasmas
abstract: Abstract Nonlinear suppression of short-wavelength drift wave turbulence by long-wavelength kinetic ballooning mode (KBM) in tokamak fusion plasma is proposed to be the main cause for confinement improvement in the core of hybrid fusion plasmas. Specifically, the ambient ion temperature gradient (ITG) turbulence, which can contribute considerable transport flux if not mitigated, is fully suppressed in the presence of KBM. KBM is demonstrated to be robustly unstable from fully electromagnetic gyrokinetic simulations. While its flux is low under low magnetic shear, KBM can generate significant stabilizing zonal flow whose velocity well surpasses the normalized linear growth rate (linear growth rate divided by its wave number) of ITG. This multiscale physics phenomenon is convincingly verified on a representative ASDEX-Upgrade hybrid scenario plasma.

title: System identification simulations using the advanced fluid neutral model and wide grid formalism in SOLPS-ITER
abstract: Abstract This work presents a first step towards using the SOLPS-ITER code package (Wiesen 2015 J. Nucl. Mater. 463 480–4) for synthetic system identification (SysID) using multisine perturbations. Numerical modelling is used to replicate SysID experiments performed to establish exhaust control done on MAST-U (Kool 2025 Nat. Energy 10 1116–31), (Van Berkel 2025 DPP 2025 (APS)). These experiments involve perturbing the gas injection rate and observing the Scrape-Off-Layer (SOL) response in the frequency domain. The model used is the Advanced Fluid Neutral (AFN) model of SOLPS-ITER (Horsten 2022 Nucl. Mater. Energy 33 101247), implemented in the Wide Grids version of the code (Dekeyser 2021 Nucl. Mater. Energy 27 100999). The grid was generated with the Grid Optimization and Adaptation Toolbox (Van den kerkhof 2024 Contrib. Plasma Phys. 64 e202300134) and extends to the vessel wall, to enable calculating fluid neutral parameters across the entire domain. New boundary condition types were implemented in the code to allow for multisine gas injection perturbations, as well as reservoir models for remote vessel regions without plasma. In steady state, it is possible to simulate plasmas ranging from attached to deeply detached using different gas injection rates. This allows for comparison between simulation and experimental results at similar levels of detachment. Comparison between simulation and experimental data in the frequency domain shows that the AFN SOLPS-ITER simulations predict faster response times to divertor fuelling perturbations than the experiments, likely in part due to the fluid approximation used for the neutrals. When including the reservoir models for remote vessel regions the phase shifts increase, but are still too low compared to experiments.

title: Nonlinear dynamics induced by strong radio-frequency fields in ReBCO high temperature superconductors
abstract: Probing the dynamics of superconducting transitions induced by strong electromagnetic fields is vital to designing high power devices leveraging these materials. The development of high temperature superconductors (HTS) is particularly interesting due to critical temperatures ($T_c$) approaching 90\,K, the ability to support high current densities, and their ability to operate in strong static magnetic fields. This work aims to determine the transition dynamics of these materials at radio-frequencies (rf) in the microwave range where they have enormous potential for new applications ranging from particle accelerators to dark matter searches. We have tested two types of coatings formed from rare earth barium copper oxide (REBCO): a film deposited by electron-beam physical vapor deposition, and HTS conductor tapes soldered to a copper substrate with exposed REBCO surfaces. Testing was performed via a hemispherical transverse-electric mode cavity that maximizes the surface rf magnetic field and minimizes the surface electric field on a 2-inch diameter sample. We report on steady-state measurements at low rf power, as well as fully time-resolved transition dynamics on the microsecond timescale seen for the first time with strong surface rf fields.

title: Electromagnetic gyrokinetic analysis in Tokamak Energy’s pre-concept design of the ST-E1 fusion power plant
abstract: Abstract ST-E1 is Tokamak Energy’s concept for a fusion power plant. As part of the pre-concept design, a series of reference flat-top plasma operating points have been developed and analysed in [McNamara et al (2026 Nucl. Fusion 66 086008)]. The present work focuses on the low-density baseline conceptual power plant (BCP) operating point of [McNamara et al (2026 Nucl. Fusion 66 086008)] selected as a representative operating point for the ST-E1 pilot plant and investigates its micro-stability, turbulent transport and transport-informed optimisation using first-principles spectral flux-tube electromagnetic gyrokinetic simulations. Linear gyrokinetic calculations, involving electrons, thermal ions, impurities, and thermal and fast helium ions, complemented by dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) to identify subdominant and stable drift-wave eigenmodes, reveal two principal long-wavelength electromagnetic instability branches: hybrid h-ITG modes driven by thermal gradients and FI-KBMs, i.e. kinetic-ballooning-like modes strongly influenced by the plasma beta (a ratio of thermal to magnetic energy) and the fast-ion (FI) population. At shorter wavelengths, electron-temperature-gradient (ETG) modes become unstable towards the plasma edge while remaining stable in the core. A comprehensive sensitivity analysis identifies the principal equilibrium parameters governing these instabilities. Building on these linear predictions, nonlinear electromagnetic gyrokinetic simulations are performed to quantify the resulting turbulent transport of the thermal plasma and fast helium ions. The reference operating point is found to exhibit saturated, rather than runaway, electromagnetic turbulence, establishing it as a physically meaningful baseline for further optimisation. The nonlinear simulations show that turbulent transport is governed primarily by the combined effects of the plasma beta, safety factor and fast-ion fraction, with intrinsic-rotation-driven E × B shear providing an additional, complementary reduction in transport. Although fast ions provide the free energy driving the FI-KBM branch, increasing the fast-ion fraction is found to reduce the saturated turbulent transport across all species through nonlinear self-organisation. To efficiently explore the resulting multidimensional parameter space, defined by the plasma beta, safety factor and fast-ion fraction, a physics-informed interpolation framework constrained and validated by nonlinear gyrokinetic simulations has been developed, enabling the identification of transport-favourable operating points without requiring exhaustive nonlinear parameter scans. The resulting framework yields a family of transport-favourable operating points for the ST-E1 low-density BCP equilibrium and provides quantitative targets for future self-consistent equilibrium optimisation.

title: Bayesian inference of moments of inertia for wobbling motion in Pr 135
abstract: Bayesian inference is applied to the core-quasiparticle coupling (CQPC) model with Metropolis-Hastings Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling to quantify the uncertainties of the principal moments of inertia (MoIs) for wobbling in $^{135}\mathrm{Pr}$. Using only the experimental yrast and wobbling energies as constraints, the posterior MoI supports the ordering ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{I}}}_{m}>{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{I}}}_{s}>{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{I}}}_{l}$ and reveals correlations among the three parameters. Propagating the posterior yields credible intervals for the energy spectra and, as predictions at fixed electromagnetic inputs, for transition probabilities and angular momentum geometry. Within the energy compatible MoI region, the decrease-then-increase of the wobbling energy and the angular momentum geometry remain stable, supporting a robust transverse-to-longitudinal evolution. This work provides a practical Bayesian protocol for assessing the statistical robustness of odd-$A$ wobbling interpretations in the CQPC model.

title: AI-Newton: A concept-driven physical law discovery system without prior physical knowledge
abstract: While current artificial intelligence (AI)-driven methods excel at deriving empirical models from individual experiments, a significant challenge remains in uncovering the common fundamental physics that underlie these models—a task at which human physicists are adept. To bridge this gap, we introduce AI-Newton, a framework for concept-driven scientific discovery. Our system autonomously derives general physical laws directly from raw, multiexperiment data, operating without supervision or prior physical knowledge. Its core innovations are twofold: (1) proposing interpretable physical concepts to construct laws and (2) progressively generalizing these laws to broader domains. Applied to a large, noisy dataset of mechanics experiments, AI-Newton successfully rediscovers foundational and universal laws, such as Newton's second law, the conservation of energy, and the universal gravitation. This work represents a proof-of-concept step toward autonomous, humanlike scientific discovery.

title: A fully electromagnetic hybrid PIC-fluid model for predictive fusion neutron yield in dense plasma focus
abstract: Abstract A fully electromagnetic hybrid ion-PIC/electron-fluid framework is developed for the implosion-to-pinch phase of dense plasma focus (DPF) discharges. Ions are advanced kinetically, electrons form a charge-neutralizing fluid under the quasi-neutral approximation, and the full Maxwell equations are solved in both plasma and vacuum. The generalized Ohm law includes resistive, electron pressure-gradient, and Hall terms. Applied to a non-hollow 180 kA geometry initialized from a pre-ionized end-of-rundown state, the framework reproduces the axial rundown, radial compression, and pinch stages. The sheath front trajectory agrees with fully kinetic benchmarks within 10%, and a pinch-radius comparison captures the radial collapse. A beam-target neutron diagnostic applied to the simulated ion distribution gives a yield of 0.296e7, at the same scale as the fully kinetic reference. The ion spectrum develops a non-Maxwellian suprathermal tail to about 0.25 MeV. The yield remains sensitive to the electron-temperature closure and anode geometry. The framework captures relevant macroscopic observables and ion-kinetic diagnostics at a computational cost roughly 1e5-1e6 times lower than comparable fully kinetic electromagnetic PIC simulations.

title: Quantum simulation of bottomonium dynamics in the quark–gluon plasma via the Lindblad equation
abstract: Abstract Quantum computing provides a powerful framework for simulating real-time dynamics in open quantum systems, offering key advantages for modeling heavy-quarkonium transport in high-energy nuclear collisions. In this work, we perform quantum simulations of the isotropic next-to-leading-order Lindblad equation for bottomonium in the quark-gluon plasma using a reduced spherical coordinate representation. We discretize operators and wavefunctions, map the physical state onto qubits, and execute time evolution via parameterized quantum gate operations. By extracting the Υ(1S) survival probability, we quantitatively isolate the color-octet contribution to the correlated regeneration of the bottomonium ground state, demonstrating that its overall impact is small in the final production of the bottomonium ground state Υ(1S) in the hot QCD medium at temperatures accessible at the Large Hadron Collider. Additionally, we have further optimized the quantum simulation algorithm for the Lindblad equation. The improved algorithm requires only a single ancillary qubit to realize the Lindblad evolution, thereby minimizing the circuit significantly.
